ActivateDesignOptionsInCombinations.description: Activates one design option in each of the given combinations, without listing all active design options of the combination. Available from Archicad 29.
ActivateDesignOptionsInCombinations.name: ActivateDesignOptionsInCombinations

designOptionsToActivate.description: The design options to activate, each in the given combination.

ActivateLayerCombination.description: Activates the given layer combination in the current window, like choosing it in the Quick Layers palette. Saved views are not changed.
ActivateLayerCombination.name: ActivateLayerCombination

AddCommentToIssue.description: Adds a new comment to the specified issue.
AddCommentToIssue.name: AddCommentToIssue

author.description: The author of the new comment.

AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.description: Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).
AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.name: AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is deleted first, so the newly added file replaces the loaded library part. By default false: the existing loaded part stays in use. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

AddLibraries.description: Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded.
AddLibraries.name: AddLibraries

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

AddLoadCasesToLoadCombination.description: Adds load cases with their factors to the given structural analysis load combination in one undo step.
AddLoadCasesToLoadCombination.name: AddLoadCasesToLoadCombination

loadCombinationId.description: The identifier of the load combination to add the load cases to.

loadFactors.description: The load cases to add, with their factors.

AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.description: Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27.
AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.name: AddMEPPreferenceTableRows

rows.description: The rows to add, with their key and optionally their values. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29. Segment tables have a row for each reference id, so no row can be added to them. Archicad 27: the key has the shape only, the table gives the index.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

AddPropertyToAttributes.description: Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.
AddPropertyToAttributes.name: AddPropertyToAttributes

attributeIds.description: The attributes (for example Building Materials) to make the property available for.

propertyId.description: An existing custom property. Create it first with CreatePropertyDefinitions if needed.

AlignElements.description: Aligns elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view to one edge of their plan bounding boxes (left, right, top or bottom) or to their middle (centerX, centerY), either of the whole set or of a reference element, by moving them in one undo step. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still aligned.
AlignElements.name: AlignElements

alignTo.description: The edge of the plan bounding boxes to align: left (smallest X), right (largest X), bottom (smallest Y), top (largest Y), centerX (the middle in X, so the elements line up on one vertical line) or centerY (the middle in Y, on one horizontal line).

elements.description: The elements to align: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database.

reference.description: Optional element to align to; it is not moved itself. Without it the elements are aligned to the outermost edge of the whole set (its leftmost left edge, its topmost top edge, ...), or for centerX and centerY to the middle of the bounding box of the whole set.

ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault.description: Makes the settings of the given Favorite the settings of its tool, and returns the element type of that tool. Available from Archicad 29.
ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault.name: ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault

favoriteName.description: The name of the Favorite whose settings become the settings of its tool.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool whose settings changed.

ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults.description: Apply the given favorites to element defaults.
ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults.name: ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults

ApplyFavoritesToElements.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. With favorite instead of favoritesToApply, one Favorite is read once and applied to the given elements, or to every element of its type that matches the filter.
ApplyFavoritesToElements.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements

applyCategories.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.

applyClassifications.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's classifications. Default is true.

applyProperties.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's property values. Default is true.

applySettings.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc.). Geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is never applied - the element stays on its own home story - except that a Window or Door takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included, while keeping its wall, marker and placement. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. A Dimension's text size, text pen and text frame are not changed (tested in Archicad 28): the dimension creation commands take textHeight, textPen and textFrame for them. Default is true.

elements.description: The elements to apply the single favorite to, one execution result each, in the same order. Only with favorite.

favorite.description: The name of one Favorite to apply to many elements, instead of favoritesToApply: to the given elements, or without elements to every element of the Favorite's type that matches the filter. The Favorite is read only once. Needs elements or filter.

favoritesToApply.description: The elements and the Favorite to apply to each. Give this or favorite.

filter.description: Server-side element filter for the single favorite. Without elements the favorite is applied to every element of its type that matches it; an element of elements that does not match it gets a failed execution result. Only with favorite.

keepFields.description: Fields of the target element to keep: after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width', 'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column; 'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height', 'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a story. Default: nothing is kept.

AttachElementsToIssue.description: Attaches elements to the specified issue.
AttachElementsToIssue.name: AttachElementsToIssue

BreakHotlinkNodes.description: Breaks hotlink nodes, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does: the elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file.
BreakHotlinkNodes.name: BreakHotlinkNodes

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to break, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. The elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does. In Teamwork the Hotlink and XRef management has to be reserved first (ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement).

CalculateSunPosition.description: Calculates the sun position (azimuth and altitude in degrees) for a date and time, at the project location unless another one is given, without changing the project.
CalculateSunPosition.name: CalculateSunPosition

dateTime.description: The date and time to calculate the sun position for; the fields left out keep the project's date and time.

location.description: The location to calculate the sun position at; the fields left out keep the project location.

CanMoveElementsToDesignOptions.description: Checks whether the given elements can be moved to another design option or to the main model, with the reason when they cannot. Available from Archicad 29.
CanMoveElementsToDesignOptions.name: CanMoveElementsToDesignOptions

canMoveElements.description: The result for each given element, in the order of the input.

canMove.description: Whether the element can be moved to another design option or to the main model.

error.description: The reason why the element cannot be moved. Only present when canMove is false.

CaptureElementState.description: Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier.
CaptureElementState.name: CaptureElementState

type.description: How GetElementChangesSince finds the changed elements between this state and another one. ModificationStamp (the default) compares the modification stamps of the elements, so any change to a tracked element counts. 3DModel compares the 3D model of the elements, so only a change that alters the 3D model counts, and capturing it generates the 3D model of the project. Two states can only be compared when they were captured with the same type. With either type the changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the result even when they were created, modified or deleted.

stateId.description: The identifier of the captured state, accepted by GetElementChangesSince and ReleaseElementState. It is only valid in the Archicad session and project it was captured in.

type.description: The type the state was captured with.

Change3DStyles.description: Changes the given fields of existing 3D styles, identified by name. Available from Archicad 27.
Change3DStyles.name: Change3DStyles

styles.description: The 3D styles to change, identified by their name. Only the given fields change.

ChangeAddOnViewpoints.description: Changes the ID, name, view settings flags or attached data (base64 encoded) of the given add-on viewpoint items; only the given fields are changed. Roots and groups can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.
ChangeAddOnViewpoints.name: ChangeAddOnViewpoints

viewpoints.description: The add-on viewpoint items to change. Only the given fields are changed.

ChangeDrawingLink.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.
ChangeDrawingLink.name: ChangeDrawingLink

items.description: An existing Drawing and the navigator item it should be relinked to.

elements.description: One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

ChangeFavorite.description: Gives an existing Favorite the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. Available from Archicad 29.
ChangeFavorite.name: ChangeFavorite

favoriteName.description: The name of the Favorite to change.

source.description: Where the new settings of the Favorite come from: exactly one of favoriteName and toolDefault.

favoriteName.description: Take the settings of this Favorite.

toolDefault.description: Take the current settings of this tool.

ChangeHotlinkInstances.description: Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances.
ChangeHotlinkInstances.name: ChangeHotlinkInstances

hotlinkInstances.description: The placed hotlink instances to change. Every field but elementId is optional; a field that is omitted keeps its current value.

ChangeHotlinkNodes.description: Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.
ChangeHotlinkNodes.name: ChangeHotlinkNodes

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to repoint at another source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. The placed instances stay where they are. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks on the same nodes to re-read the content from the new file.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the new module source file (.mod or .pln).

ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.description: Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B).
ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.name: ChangeLibraryPartOfElements

elementsWithLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part to change them to. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects.

keepParameters.description: Copies the values of the element's GDL parameters to the parameters of the new library part that have the same name, type and array dimensions; the other parameters get the new part's defaults. Default: true.

keepSize.description: Keeps the size (A and B) of the element; when false, the element gets the new part's default size. Default: true.

libraryPart.description: The new library part, given by one of name, index or guid. It has to be a placeable library part of the element's type in the loaded libraries.

name.description: The name of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in documentName.

index.description: The index of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it.

guid.description: The main guid of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in guid.

ChangeSelectionOfElements.description: Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection.
ChangeSelectionOfElements.name: ChangeSelectionOfElements

ChangeTextContent.description: Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content.
ChangeTextContent.name: ChangeTextContent

contentChanges.description: The content changes, applied in order (several changes of one element see the content as the previous one left it). Unlike ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, the rest of the content is not rebuilt: the other runs, their styles and any autotext in them stay as they are, and the inserted piece takes the style of the character at 'from'.

ChangeWindow.description: Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. The databaseId of a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened opens its Project Map item instead (from Archicad 27). With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan. windowType 'Report' on its own opens the Session Report window (from Archicad 26); its text cannot be read through the Archicad API.
ChangeWindow.name: ChangeWindow

CheckLibraries.description: Checks the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library check. Returns the error the API reports, if any.
CheckLibraries.name: CheckLibraries

CheckMEPPortConnectability.description: Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27.
CheckMEPPortConnectability.name: CheckMEPPortConnectability

portPairs.description: The pairs of ports to check.

results.description: The result for each pair of ports, in the order of the input.

CheckPropertyValues.description: Checks whether the given values are acceptable for the given property definitions, without changing anything.
CheckPropertyValues.name: CheckPropertyValues

propertyValues.description: The values to check, each with the property definition it is checked against.

results.description: One item for each value, in the order of the input: whether it is acceptable, or an error if the property was not found.

isValid.description: True if the value can be converted to the type of the property and Archicad accepts it for the property definition.

CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.
CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap.name: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap

viewsData.description: Array of views to clone from the Project Map to the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the Project Map viewpoint to clone.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the View Map folder to place the clone in. Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

CloseWindows.description: Closes the windows of the given databases (for example layouts, sections or details opened earlier with ChangeWindow), with one execution result per window; a window Archicad cannot close gets a failed result. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
CloseWindows.name: CloseWindows

CompareLibraryPartUnIds.description: Compares two library part unique IDs with Archicad's own comparison and tells whether their main and revision GUIDs are the same.
CompareLibraryPartUnIds.name: CompareLibraryPartUnIds

unId1.description: A library part unique ID, '{main GUID}-{revision GUID}', as GetLibraryPartIdentities returns it.

unId2.description: The library part unique ID to compare unId1 with.

apiErrorCode.description: The code ACAPI_LibraryPart_CompareLibPartUnIds returned: 0 (NoError) when Archicad reports the two unique IDs as matching, otherwise the API error code that tells how they differ.

sameMainGuid.description: True when the two unique IDs have the same main GUID, that is they are revisions of the same library part.

sameRevisionGuid.description: True when the two unique IDs have the same revision GUID.

ConnectMEPElements.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. The first or last node of the 'connectToId' route must lie exactly on the 'routingElementId' route, so for a tee pass the main route as 'routingElementId' and the branch as 'connectToId'. A failed connection says which condition is not met. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27.
ConnectMEPElements.name: ConnectMEPElements

ConnectToElectricalCircuits.description: Connects electrical devices, or panels as sub-panels, to electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.
ConnectToElectricalCircuits.name: ConnectToElectricalCircuits

connectionsData.description: Array of electrical devices or panels and the circuits to connect them to. A panel connected to a circuit becomes a sub-panel of the panel of that circuit.

ConsolidateFills.description: Runs the Fill Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
ConsolidateFills.name: ConsolidateFills

result.description: What Archicad answered for the JSON query, as it came. Present when the query ran. The Archicad API does not document its content; it may report a failure of the menu command even though the query itself ran.

ConsolidateLines.description: Runs the Line Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
ConsolidateLines.name: ConsolidateLines

result.description: What Archicad answered for the JSON query, as it came. Present when the query ran. The Archicad API does not document its content; it may report a failure of the menu command even though the query itself ran.

ConvertAnalyticalLinksToNonShortest.description: Converts the given shortest analytical links (associative to a curve member or a surface member edge) to links connected to a fixed coordinate, in one undo step, and returns the converted links. Available from Archicad 26.
ConvertAnalyticalLinksToNonShortest.name: ConvertAnalyticalLinksToNonShortest

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

links.description: The link the API returns for each element after the conversion, in the order of the input. An element that cannot be converted is represented by an error object.

ConvertImages.description: Converts base64 encoded images from one image format to another with Archicad's own image converters, for example a PNG preview image to JPEG. The formats are Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG and PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read or write. The output is aligned with the input array of images. Changes nothing in the project.
ConvertImages.name: ConvertImages

image.description: The base64 encoded image, for example a previewImage returned by GetElementPreviewImage.

inputFormat.description: The format of the image: Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG or PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read (for example image/x-targa).

outputFormat.description: The format to convert the image to: Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG or PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can write.

images.description: The converted images in the order of the input, or an error.

ConvertRevealOffsets.description: Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.
ConvertRevealOffsets.name: ConvertRevealOffsets

openings.description: Windows and doors placed in walls, each with exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset.

revealOffsets.description: The reveal depth offset of each opening in both references, aligned with the input, or an error.

ConvertUnitValues.description: Formats lengths, areas, volumes and angles (given in meters, square meters, cubic meters and radians) as Archicad shows them with the unit and rounding of the given Project Preference, returning the text, its extra accuracy decimals and the unit. The output is aligned with the input array of values. Available from Archicad 27.
ConvertUnitValues.name: ConvertUnitValues

convertedValues.description: The converted values, in the order of the input. A value that cannot be converted is an error item.

CopyElements.description: Copies elements by an offset, like dragging a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is moved by n times the offset, which makes a linear array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy (a part of a curtain wall, stair or railing, a locked element or one on a hidden or locked layer, ...) gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.
CopyElements.name: CopyElements

count.description: Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is moved by n times the offset, so more than one makes a linear array. By default it's 1.

elements.description: The elements to copy.

offset.description: The vector in meters the first copy is moved by from its element.

copies.description: One item for each given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.

error.description: Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

CopyElementsToDatabase.description: Copies 2D elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, hotspots, texts, hatches, independent labels) from one database into another, e.g. from a worksheet into another worksheet, a detail or a layout, optionally moved by an offset. Returns the new elements in the order of the given ones.
CopyElementsToDatabase.name: CopyElementsToDatabase

elements.description: The 2D elements to copy: Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hotspot, Text, Hatch or Label (not associated with an element). Drawings are not copied yet: created from their own data they lose the link to their source view.

offset.description: Optional vector the copies are moved by in the target database. Without it they keep the coordinates of the originals.

sourceDatabaseId.description: The database the elements are in. Default is the current database.

targetDatabaseId.description: The database to copy the elements into, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases).

elements.description: The new element of each given element, in the same order, or the reason it was not copied.

CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary.description: Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.
CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary.name: CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary

files.description: The files to copy. Each keeps its file name inside the target folder.

overwriteIfExists.description: Optional. When true, an item with the same name in the target folder is replaced. By default false.

targetFolder.description: Optional. The folder relative to the embedded library to copy the files into, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing folders are created. By default the root of the embedded library.

CopyLibraryParts.description: Copies loaded library parts, given by name or by an element placed from them, under a new file name into a folder, by default the embedded library. The copy gets a new unique ID unless the main GUID is kept. An existing file is never overwritten. The libraries are reloaded once afterwards, so the copies can be found by name. Available from Archicad 28.
CopyLibraryParts.name: CopyLibraryParts

libraryParts.description: The library parts to copy, each given by its name or by an element placed from it, with the name of the copy.

librariesReloaded.description: Whether the libraries were reloaded after copying. False when nothing was copied or the reload failed; then the copies are not found by name until the libraries are reloaded.

libraryParts.description: The copies in the order of the input, or an error for a library part that was not copied.

Create3DStyles.description: Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27.
Create3DStyles.name: Create3DStyles

styles.description: The 3D styles to create. Each starts from the current 3D style; only the given fields differ from it.

CreateAddOnViewpoints.description: Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.
CreateAddOnViewpoints.name: CreateAddOnViewpoints

viewpoints.description: The add-on viewpoint items to create. The identifier of a new root or group is only known from the response, so create the parents in an earlier call.

data.description: Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

parentViewpointId.description: The root or group to create the item in. Required for a group or a leaf node, ignored for a root.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of a leaf node, as Archicad stores them (a bit field). Ignored for a root or a group.

viewpoints.description: The identifier of each created item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that could not be created.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the created add-on viewpoint item.

CreateAnalyticalLinks.description: Creates analytical links from their settings and connected member parts, as GetAnalyticalLinks returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26.
CreateAnalyticalLinks.name: CreateAnalyticalLinks

links.description: The links to create, as GetAnalyticalLinks returns them. Each is created from the defaults of the Analytical Link tool.

CreateAnalyticalLoadCases.description: Creates structural analysis load cases in the given load groups in one undo step and returns their identifiers.
CreateAnalyticalLoadCases.name: CreateAnalyticalLoadCases

loadCaseIds.description: The identifiers of the new load cases, in the order of the input. A load case that could not be created is represented by an error object.

CreateAnalyticalLoadCombinations.description: Creates structural analysis load combinations, optionally with their load factors, in one undo step and returns their identifiers. The combination type is available from Archicad 27.
CreateAnalyticalLoadCombinations.name: CreateAnalyticalLoadCombinations

loadCombinationIds.description: The identifiers of the new load combinations, in the order of the input. A load combination that could not be created is represented by an error object.

CreateAnalyticalLoadGroups.description: Creates structural analysis load groups in one undo step and returns their identifiers.
CreateAnalyticalLoadGroups.name: CreateAnalyticalLoadGroups

loadGroupIds.description: The identifiers of the new load groups, in the order of the input. A load group that could not be created is represented by an error object.

CreateAnalyticalLoads.description: Creates analytical point, edge and surface loads from their settings, loaded member part and custom data, as GetAnalyticalLoads returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26.
CreateAnalyticalLoads.name: CreateAnalyticalLoads

loads.description: The loads to create, as GetAnalyticalLoads returns them without their geometry. Each is created from the defaults of its tool. An edge load needs the curve and a surface load the contour it is applied on, in customData.

CreateAnalyticalSupports.description: Creates analytical supports from their settings and supported member part, as GetAnalyticalSupports returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26.
CreateAnalyticalSupports.name: CreateAnalyticalSupports

supports.description: The supports to create, as GetAnalyticalSupports returns them. Each is created from the defaults of the Analytical Support tool.

CreateArcs.description: Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters.
CreateArcs.name: CreateArcs

arcsData.description: Array of data to create Arcs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Arc.

begAngle.description: Beginning angle of the arc in radians.

endAngle.description: End angle of the arc in radians.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the arc on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

CreateAssociativeDimensions.description: Creates associative dimensions from explicit witness point references: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance). A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.
CreateAssociativeDimensions.name: CreateAssociativeDimensions

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.

marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection.description: Creates associative dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column, door and window presets: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance), e.g. level marks. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds. For Opening tool elements, which Archicad does not associate with dimensions, the OpeningEdges preset places fixed points at their edges instead.
CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection.name: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.

marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

preset.description: OpeningEdges puts fixed points, not associated ones, at the edges of an Opening tool element as the section draws it: left and right for a horizontal direction, bottom and top for a vertical one. Archicad does not associate dimensions with openings in sections.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of a single section element. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

sectionElementIds.description: A list of section elements whose preset points are merged into one continuous dimension chain. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

CreateAttributeFolders.description: Creates attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path (the folder names from the root folder down). Missing parent folders are created too; a folder that already exists is kept and reported as success. Available from Archicad 26.
CreateAttributeFolders.name: CreateAttributeFolders

CreateBeams.description: Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyBeams, besides the position, shape, slant and cross section; settings not given come from the Beam tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.
CreateBeams.name: CreateBeams

anchorPoint.description: The point of the cross section that lies on the reference line (begCoordinate to endCoordinate at zCoordinate). Top anchors hang the beam below zCoordinate, Bottom anchors stand it on top, MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it. Left and Right anchors put the line on the beam's left or right edge, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate; TopCenter, Center and BottomCenter keep it on the beam's axis.

arcAngle.description: Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the beam in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

offset.description: Horizontal distance of the beam from its reference line, in meters; positive moves the beam to the left of the line, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate.

profileAngle.description: Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

slantAngle.description: Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

verticalCurveHeight.description: Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the beam's reference line. Which point of the cross section lies on the reference line is set by anchorPoint: with a Top anchor the beam hangs below zCoordinate, so zCoordinate 10 and height 0.1 span 9.9 to 10; MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it on zCoordinate; Bottom anchors stand it on top. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given.

CreateBuildingMaterials.description: Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateBuildingMaterials.name: CreateBuildingMaterials

buildingMaterialDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Building Materials.

items.description: Data to create a Building Material.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

collisionDetection.description: Whether the Building Material participates in collision detection.

cutFillOrientation.description: ProjectOrigin, ElementOrigin, or FitToSkin. Orientation of the cut fill.

description.description: Decription.

id.description: Identifier.

index.description: Index of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Building Material with the given name will be overwritten.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Building Material if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateCircles.description: Creates Circle elements based on the given parameters.
CreateCircles.name: CreateCircles

circlesData.description: Array of data to create Circles.

items.description: The parameters of the new Circle.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the circle on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

CreateClassificationItems.description: Creates Classification Items in the given Classification Systems based on the given parameters.
CreateClassificationItems.name: CreateClassificationItems

classificationItemIds.description: The identifiers of the new classification items, in the order of the input. An item that could not be created is an error item. An item whose children failed is still listed, because it was created; its execution result has the error.

CreateClassificationSystems.description: Creates Classification Systems including Classification Items based on the given parameters.
CreateClassificationSystems.name: CreateClassificationSystems

classificationSystemIds.description: The identifiers of the new classification systems, in the order of the input. A system that could not be created is an error item. A system whose items failed is still listed, because it was created; its execution result has the error.

CreateColumns.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyColumns, besides the position, size, slant, cross section and veneer; settings not given come from the Column tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.
CreateColumns.name: CreateColumns

columnsData.description: Array of data to create Columns.

items.description: The parameters of the new Column.

axisRotationAngle.description: Optional column rotation angle in radians.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the column in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

height.description: Optional column height.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

slantAngle.description: Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

slantDirectionAngle.description: Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.

veneer.description: Veneer of the column (type, thickness, building material); the fields not given come from the tool defaults or favoriteName, thickness 0 creates the column without veneer. Applied to all segments.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

CreateComposites.description: Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateComposites.name: CreateComposites

compositeDataArray.description: Array of data to create Composites.

items.description: Data to create a Composite.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Composite with the given name will be overwritten.

separators.description: Array of skin separator data. The number of items must be the number of skins plus one. Required when creating a new Composite. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current separators are kept (only possible if the number of skins does not change).

items.description: Data to represent a skin separator.

skins.description: Array of skin data. Required when creating a new Composite. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current skins are kept.

items.description: Data to represent a skin.

type.description: Skin type (Core, Finish, or Other)

useWith.description: Array of types the composite can used with. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current setting is kept.

items.description: Element type (Wall, Slab, Roof, or Shell)

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Composite if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateCurtainWalls.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.
CreateCurtainWalls.name: CreateCurtainWalls

curtainWallsData.description: Array of data to create Curtain Walls.

items.description: The parameters of the new Curtain Wall. Everything not given here - the frame and panel classes, the surfaces, the boundary and corner frames, the pattern - comes from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults of the open project.

cells.description: Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

primaryPattern.description: Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

secondaryPattern.description: Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

zCoordinate.description: Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.

CreateDesignOptionCombinations.description: Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateDesignOptionCombinations.name: CreateDesignOptionCombinations

CreateDesignOptionSets.description: Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateDesignOptionSets.name: CreateDesignOptionSets

CreateDesignOptions.description: Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateDesignOptions.name: CreateDesignOptions

CreateDetailMarkers.description: Places Detail markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Detail viewpoint, like the Detail tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.
CreateDetailMarkers.name: CreateDetailMarkers

angle.description: Rotation of the marker symbol in radians. Default is that of the tool defaults.

clipPolygon.description: The boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

floorIndex.description: Story of the marker when it is placed on a floor plan. Default is the current story.

id.description: Reference ID shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker. Default is that of the tool defaults.

markerCoordinate.description: Where the marker symbol is placed. Default is the first point of clipPolygon.

name.description: Name of the new viewpoint. Default is that of the tool defaults.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

CreateDetails.description: Creates independent Detail databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new detail.
CreateDetails.name: CreateDetails

databases.description: One item per input item, in the same order.

CreateDoors.description: Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters.
CreateDoors.name: CreateDoors

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Door favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Door tool defaults before the create.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a door library part. Set on the created door only, with its A and B from `width` and `height` (or the tool default's width and height); the Door tool defaults are not changed.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

CreateDrawings.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.
CreateDrawings.name: CreateDrawings

angle.description: Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

clipPolygon.description: Optional polygon to clip the drawing with, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as position) - not the coordinates of the source view's model. Stored as given: position, angle, scale and modelOffset are not applied to it, and it does not move the content (see position).

drawingScale.description: Ignored: Archicad takes the scale from the source view (API_DrawingType::drawingScale is output only). GetDetailsOfElements returns the scale the Drawing got.

modelOffset.description: Offset of the model origin within the drawing, in model meters. Archicad uses it only with clipPolygon and then adds modelOffset * drawing scale (times scale, rotated by angle) to the new Drawing's pos; without clipPolygon it is ignored. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

name.description: Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.

nameType.description: Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

position.description: Where the Drawing is placed on the layout, in meters; this becomes its pos. Without clipPolygon it is the lower left corner of the Drawing (before rotation). With clipPolygon it is the point where the origin of the source view lands (on a floor plan the project origin): a model point (x, y) appears at position + scale * drawing scale * (x, y), rotated by angle, and the clipPolygon chooses which part is shown.

scale.description: Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.

CreateElectricalCircuits.description: Adds new circuits to electrical panels, optionally with the given description, voltage, wiring type and used phases. Available from Archicad 30.
CreateElectricalCircuits.name: CreateElectricalCircuits

electricalCircuitsData.description: Array of data to create electrical circuits. Each item adds one circuit to the given panel.

CreateElectricalDevices.description: Places electrical devices with the default settings of the Electrical Device tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, apparent power and load classification, and connects them to a circuit. Available from Archicad 30.
CreateElectricalDevices.name: CreateElectricalDevices

electricalDevicesData.description: Array of data to create electrical devices. The fields that are not given are taken from the default settings of the Electrical Device tool.

CreateElectricalPanels.description: Places electrical panels with the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, panel name and circuit naming. Available from Archicad 30.
CreateElectricalPanels.name: CreateElectricalPanels

electricalPanelsData.description: Array of data to create electrical panels. The fields that are not given are taken from the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool.

CreateElementSets.description: Creates element sets of the given elements. An element set is a hidden, persistent collection of elements (it is not a group and has no effect on selection or editing).
CreateElementSets.name: CreateElementSets

elements.description: The elements to put into the element set.

elementSets.description: The identifier of each created element set, or an error, in the order of the input.

elementSetId.description: The identifier of an element set.

CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers.description: Creates elements (beams, columns, walls, slabs, roofs) from the given curve, surface or segmented surface members, in the form GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns them, optionally with the settings of a favorite, in one undo step. Returns the new elements and, from Archicad 26, the mapping of their edges and vertices to member parts.
CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers.name: CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers

members.description: The analytical members to create elements from, in the form GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns them, so a member read there can be passed on as it is. The elemGuid of a member is ignored. A curve member needs analyticalMemberType and curve, a surface member (or segment) analyticalMemberType and contour; the other fields are zero when left out.

elements.description: The new element of each member, in the order of the input. A member no element could be created from is represented by an error object.

CreateElevations.description: Creates Elevation elements on the floor plan. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active.
CreateElevations.name: CreateElevations

id.description: The reference ID shown in the elevation marker and in the Project Map. Without it the elevation takes the ID of the Elevation tool defaults.

CreateFavorite.description: Creates a Favorite in the given folder from the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. conflictPolicy says what happens when the name is taken: fail, skip, overwrite the existing Favorite's settings or create the new one under a free name. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateFavorite.name: CreateFavorite

folder.description: The folder of the Favorites palette to create the Favorite in, as the folder names from the root down. The folder must exist. Empty or omitted = root.

name.description: The name of the new Favorite.

folder.description: The folder of the Favorite, as the folder names from the root down. Empty for the root. Missing when Archicad cannot read it.

name.description: The name of the Favorite: the given name, or the new name with RenameNew.

CreateFavoriteFolder.description: Creates a folder in the Favorites palette, in the parent folder given by its path. Returns the new folder. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateFavoriteFolder.name: CreateFavoriteFolder

name.description: The name of the new folder.

parentPath.description: The path of the folder to create the new folder in, in the format GetFavoriteFolders returns: the folder names from the root down. Empty for the root folder.

CreateFavoritesFromElements.description: Create favorites from the given elements.
CreateFavoritesFromElements.name: CreateFavoritesFromElements

CreateFills.description: Creates or overwrites Fill attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateFills.name: CreateFills

fillDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Fills.

items.description: Data to create a Fill.

angle.description: The angle of the fill in radians (Vector, Symbol, and gradient fills).

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Fill to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

bitPattern.description: 16 hex characters (8 bytes) describing the fill's bitmap pattern, one line of the pattern per byte, matching the Pattern field of the Attribute Manager XML export.

horizontalSpacing.description: The fill's spacing factor in the X direction (Vector fills).

index.description: Index of the existing Fill to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

lineItems.description: Vectorial fill line items (Vector fills only).

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Fill with the given name will be overwritten.

percent.description: Translucency percentage [0..1] (gradient and Solid fills). A Solid fill with a percent below 1 is created as a percent fill (like the 25 % fill), 1 makes it a full Solid fill.

subType.description: Vector, Solid, Empty, Symbol, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, or Image. Defaults to Vector. Only one Solid and one Empty fill may exist. Image fills use the texture field's name to reference the image library part.

symbolArcs.description: Arc items of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).

symbolHotspots.description: Hotspot coordinates of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).

symbolLines.description: Line items of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).

symbolOffset1.description: First offset vector of the repeating symbol motif, X1/Y1 in the Fill Types dialog (Symbol fills only).

symbolOffset2.description: Second offset vector of the repeating symbol motif, X2/Y2 in the Fill Types dialog (Symbol fills only).

symbolSolidFills.description: Filled polygons of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only), as GetFills returns them.

texture.description: Used for Image and gradient fills. Only name, rotationAngle, xSize, ySize, mirrorX, and mirrorY are used for Fills.

useForCover.description: This fill can be used for cover fills.

useForDraft.description: This fill can be used for drafting fills.

useForWalls.description: This fill can be used for cut fills.

verticalSpacing.description: The fill's spacing factor in the Y direction (Vector fills).

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Fill if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary.description: Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.
CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary.name: CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary

folderPath.description: The path of the folder relative to the embedded library, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing parent folders are created too; folders that already exist are kept.

CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations.description: Creates graphic override combinations from existing rules. Available from Archicad 27.
CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations.name: CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations

graphicOverrideCombinations.description: The graphic override combinations to create.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The rules of the combination, in priority order.

name.description: The name of the combination, unique within the project.

graphicOverrideCombinationIds.description: The identifiers of the created combinations, or errors, in the order of the input.

CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: Creates empty graphic override rule groups. Available from Archicad 27.
CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.name: CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups

ruleGroupNames.description: The names of the rule groups to create, unique within the project. The groups are created empty.

CreateGraphicOverrideRules.description: Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27.
CreateGraphicOverrideRules.name: CreateGraphicOverrideRules

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules to create.

criterion.description: The criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.

criterionXML.description: The criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements. Left out together with 'criterion': Archicad's default criterion for new rules.

name.description: The name of the rule, unique within the project.

ruleGroupName.description: The name of the rule group to put the rule in. Created when it does not exist.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The identifiers of the created rules, or errors, in the order of the input.

CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination.description: Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later.
CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination

name.description: Name of the override combination. When a combination with this name exists, its rule list is replaced.

ruleNames.description: Names of the override rules in the combination, in order. Rule names are unique in the project, whatever the rule group. An empty list makes a combination without rules.

combinationId.description: The created or changed override combination.

CreateGraphicalOverrideRule.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.
CreateGraphicalOverrideRule.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule

criterionXML.description: Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index override for lines, markers and texts. Only a positive index takes effect.

name.description: Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.

overrideContours.description: Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden surfaces are recolored too.

ruleGroupName.description: Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.

surfaceRGB.description: Optional color override of the cut and uncut surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.

ruleId.description: The created or overwritten override rule.

CreateGridElements.description: Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.
CreateGridElements.name: CreateGridElements

begCoordinate.description: Start point of the grid line (the object's insertion point).

endCoordinate.description: End point of the grid line. Sets the direction and, unless lengthMode is 'none', the length.

floorIndex.description: Home story index. Default: the tool default.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index. Only a positive index takes effect. Default: the tool default.

lengthMode.description: How the line length is applied. length (default): to the GDL parameter AC_Length when the library part has it, as the Grid Tool's grid marker does; otherwise to the object's A size, converted to xRatio as CreateObjects does. none: the length is left to 'parameters'.

parameters.description: GDL parameters to set by name (read the names with GetGridElementDefaults). The value is a number, a boolean or a string. Unknown names and wrong value types are reported in warnings and skipped. The tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the Grid Tool (for example a short line with a leader to the bubble); to get the same look, copy the parameters of such a grid (GetGridElements with includeParameters).

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

warnings.description: Parameters that were not set, prefixed with the index of the grid element.

CreateGroups.description: Creates groups of the passed elements
CreateGroups.name: CreateGroups

elementGroups.description: A list of element groups to create.

groupGuids.description: The results of the group creation operations.

CreateHatches.description: Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches.
CreateHatches.name: CreateHatches

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

hatchesData.description: Array of data to create Hatches.

items.description: The parameters of the new Hatch.

arcs.description: The arcs of the hatch outline.

backgroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.

contourPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the contour. By default the current pen is used.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the hatch outline. Do not repeat the first point at the end.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

fillId.description: Optional fill attribute. By default the current fill is used.

fillPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the fill. By default the current pen is used.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

foregroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.

holes.description: Optional holes of the hatch, each with its polygonOutline and optional polygonArcs (arc indices are relative to the hole's own outline). The same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts and GetDetailsOfElements returns for hatches.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the hatch on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

roomSpecial.description: Special area percent in a room (negative means OFF).

CreateHotlinkInstances.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.
CreateHotlinkInstances.name: CreateHotlinkInstances

CreateHotlinkNodes.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).
CreateHotlinkNodes.name: CreateHotlinkNodes

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink module nodes to create.
