A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.

name.description: Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

refFloorIndex.description: Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).

storyRangeType.description: Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

hotlinkNodes.description: One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

CreateHotspots.description: Creates Hotspot elements based on the given parameters.
CreateHotspots.name: CreateHotspots

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

hotspotsData.description: Array of data to create Hotspots.

items.description: The parameters of the new Hotspot.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the hotspot on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

penIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

CreateInteriorElevations.description: Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room.
CreateInteriorElevations.name: CreateInteriorElevations

interiorElevationsData.description: Array of data to create Interior Elevation elements.

name.description: The name of the issue.

tagText.description: Tag text of the issue, optional.

CreateKeynoteFolders.description: Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.
CreateKeynoteFolders.name: CreateKeynoteFolders

foldersData.description: Array of data to create keynote folders.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

CreateKeynoteItems.description: Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.
CreateKeynoteItems.name: CreateKeynoteItems

itemsData.description: Array of data to create keynote items.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

CreateKeynoteLabels.description: Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateKeynoteLabels.name: CreateKeynoteLabels

labelsData.description: Array of data to create keynote labels.

contentFields.description: The keynote fields to include in the label text as autotext. Optional; defaults to all fields.

position.description: The reference point of the label.

CreateLabels.description: Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.
CreateLabels.name: CreateLabels

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create Labels.

items.description: The parameters of the new Label.

begCoordinate.description: The begin coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter, but either begCoordinate or parentElementId must be provided. Unless midCoordinate and endCoordinate are both given too, the label is created at its default position relative to the parent element (Archicad's 'createAtDefaultPosition'), so the label may not end up at begCoordinate - read it back with GetDetailsOfElements after creation.

endCoordinate.description: The end coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with midCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor or the floor of the parent element is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

labelClass.description: Optional; if omitted, inherits the current Label tool default (which may silently resolve to either class - explicitly setting this avoids ambiguity). 'Symbol' needs a symbol library part, which only the Label tool default or the favorite given in favoriteName can provide: when those are a Text label, the item fails instead of placing a label without content.

midCoordinate.description: The mid coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with endCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

parentElementId.description: The parent element if the label is an associative label.

runs.description: Multi-style text content for a text label: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

text.description: The text content if the label is a text label. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

CreateLamps.description: Creates Lamp elements based on the given parameters. A library part named in libraryPartName starts from its own default size and GDL parameters, not from those of the part the Lamp tool holds; the dimensions and the GDL parameters given (by name, in parameters) override them. layerIndex places the element on a layer. With databaseId the lamps are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, instead of the current one.
CreateLamps.name: CreateLamps

databaseId.description: Optional database to place the elements in, e.g. a worksheet or a detail (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), for a legend of symbols. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are placed in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

lampsData.description: Array of data to create Lamps.

items.description: The parameters of the new Lamp.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the lamp library part to use.

lightColor.description: Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

parameters.description: Optional GDL parameters to set by name, after dimensions. The value is a number, a boolean or a string; array parameters are not supported. A or B also set the size. An unknown name or a value of the wrong type fails the item, and nothing is created for it.

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

CreateLayerCombinations.description: Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateLayerCombinations.name: CreateLayerCombinations

layerCombinationDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Layer Combinations.

items.description: Data to create a Layer Combination.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Layer Combination to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Layer Combination to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

layers.description: Layer states to set. Layers not listed keep their current state when overwriting an existing Layer Combination (or get the default visible/unlocked state for a new one), so this can be omitted to e.g. only rename an existing Layer Combination.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Layer Combination with the given name will be overwritten.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Layer Combination if exists with the same guid/index/name. The default is false.

CreateLayers.description: Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateLayers.name: CreateLayers

layerDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Layers.

items.description: Data to create a Layer.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

intersectionGroupNr.description: Intersection group. Elements on layers having the same group will be intersected.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Layer with the given name will be overwritten.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Layer if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateLayout.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. A layout that was created but could not be placed is returned with both its databaseId and the error.
CreateLayout.name: CreateLayout

customLayoutNumber.description: The layout's own number, used when customLayoutNumbering is true. It only replaces this layout's displayed number: the layout still counts in its subset's numbering, so the sheets after it are renumbered. Use doNotIncludeInNumbering to leave it out.

customLayoutNumbering.description: Use customLayoutNumber instead of the automatic number. Does not leave the layout out of the subset's numbering; see doNotIncludeInNumbering.

doNotIncludeInNumbering.description: Leave the new layout out of its subset's automatic numbering, so the numbers of the other sheets do not change.

paperHeight.description: Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.

paperWidth.description: Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.

position.description: Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.

oneOf.description: The layout was created, but it could not be moved to the place asked for by previousNavigatorItemId or position: it stays where Archicad put it.

CreateLevelDimensions.description: Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.
CreateLevelDimensions.name: CreateLevelDimensions

levelDimensionsData.description: Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).

items.description: The parameters of the new Level Dimension.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Level Dimension favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (marker, format, text style, layer, pen) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: The index of the floor to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the floor of the parent element, otherwise the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the favorite or the Level Dimension tool default is used.

level.description: Optional fixed level value in meters (absolute, from the project zero). Only used without parentElementId; the dimension then shows this value instead of the floor level.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

parentElementId.description: Optional element the level dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object, Stair ...). The dimension then shows the element's height at the position and follows the element when it changes. Without it the dimension measures the floor level, or the given static level.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

position.description: The location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parentElementId it must lie on that element, the measured level is the parent's height at this point. Outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (GetDetailsOfElements reads a level of -110000000).

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size), applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text, applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

CreateLibraryPart.description: Creates a new library part file (.gsm) of the given loaded subtype, inheriting its parameters, and reports whether it is loaded with its index and names. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateLibraryPart.name: CreateLibraryPart

ancestorSubtype.description: The name of a loaded library part that is a subtype, with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts. The new object is of this subtype and inherits its parameters.

path.description: The full path of the new library part file. It must end with .gsm, must not exist yet, and its folder must exist.

isLoaded.description: Whether the new library part is loaded in the project. It is only loaded when its folder is in a loaded library; otherwise only the file was created.

libraryPart.description: The new library part, in the same form as in GetAvailableLibraryParts. Left out when it is not loaded.

CreateLibraryPartFromElements.description: Creates a library part in the embedded library (or in a given local library folder, which is added to the loaded libraries when needed) whose 2D symbol is a copy of the given 2D drawing elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and hotspots), under the given parent subtype, with optional master, 2D, 3D and parameter scripts, comment and keywords. A and B are taken from the extent of the symbol. The elements themselves are not changed.
CreateLibraryPartFromElements.name: CreateLibraryPartFromElements

comment.description: Optional. The comment (description) of the library part.

elements.description: The 2D drawing elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and hotspots) whose copies make up the 2D symbol of the new library part. They keep their plan coordinates, so the project origin becomes the origin of the symbol. The elements themselves are not changed.

folder.description: Optional. The folder of the new .gsm file, relative to the embedded library (or to libraryFolder), created when missing. By default the embedded library (or libraryFolder) itself.

keywords.description: Optional. The keywords of the library part.

libraryFolder.description: Optional. The absolute path of a local library folder to create the library part in instead of the embedded library. A folder that is not one of the loaded libraries yet is added to them first, and stays added.

name.description: The name of the new library part, as shown in the library and used by CreateObjects as libraryPartName.

overwrite.description: Optional. When true, a library part file of the same name in the folder is overwritten. By default false: the new library part then gets a unique name, which the response returns.

parentId.description: The parent subtype of the new library part: its unique ID ('{main}-{revision}') or its main GUID, as GetAvailableLibraryParts reports it. Either parentId or parentName is required.

parentName.description: The document name of the parent subtype, e.g. 'General Object' or 'Model Element'; used when parentId is not given.

placeable.description: Optional. Whether the new library part can be placed. True by default.

scripts.description: Optional. The GDL scripts of the new library part.

2D.description: The 2D script. When it is empty, the 2D symbol is drawn; a 2D script draws it with FRAGMENT2 ALL, 0.

a.description: The default A (X size) of the library part, the width of its 2D symbol.

b.description: The default B (Y size) of the library part, the depth of its 2D symbol.

fileName.description: The file name of the created library part, with its extension.

guid.description: The main GUID of the created library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts reports it.

index.description: The index of the created library part in the loaded libraries.

name.description: The name of the created library part.

unId.description: The unique ID of the created library part ('{main}-{revision}').

CreateLibraryParts.description: Creates GDL library parts in the embedded library from their scripts (master, 2D, 3D, parameter, interface, properties) and parameter definitions, under the given parent subtype. The new parts are placeable right away, e.g. with CreateObjects. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new part is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).
CreateLibraryParts.name: CreateLibraryParts

libraryParts.description: The library parts to create in the embedded library.

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new library part is deleted first, so the new one replaces the loaded library part. By default false: creating on an existing path fails. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

libraryParts.description: The created library parts, in the order of the input, or the error of each one that could not be created.

CreateLineElements.description: Creates Line elements based on the given parameters.
CreateLineElements.name: CreateLineElements

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

linesData.description: Array of data to create Lines.

items.description: The parameters of the new Line.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the line on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

CreateLines.description: Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateLines.name: CreateLines

lineDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Lines.

items.description: Data to create a Line.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

dashItems.description: Dash-gap pairs describing one period (Dashed line type only).

defineScale.description: The floor plan scale the line type is defined with. Only used if scaleWithPlan is true.

height.description: The height of the symbol line (Symbol line type only).

index.description: Index of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

lineItems.description: Symbol items describing one period (Symbol line type only).

lineType.description: Solid, Dashed, or Symbol. Defaults to Solid.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Line with the given name will be overwritten.

period.description: The length of one period (Dashed and Symbol line types).

scaleWithPlan.description: If true, the line type parameters are defined in meters at the given defineScale and scale on printout with the actual plan scale. If false (default), the parameters are fixed values in millimeters as the line will appear on the printout.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Line if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateMEPElements.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with another library part, size (from Archicad 30), MEP system, port sizes and shapes and a changed insulation, which apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateMEPElements.name: CreateMEPElements

elementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP elements.

CreateMEPFlexibleSegments.description: Creates MEP flexible segments through the given control points, or along a polyline of alternating line and spline parts (Piping), with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain, optionally with the orientation (control points) or direction (polyline) at both ends. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateMEPFlexibleSegments.name: CreateMEPFlexibleSegments

flexibleSegmentsData.description: Array of data to place MEP flexible segments with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain (see GetMEPToolDefaults).

CreateMEPPhysicalSystems.description: Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateMEPPhysicalSystems.name: CreateMEPPhysicalSystems

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to create physical systems.

CreateMEPPreferenceTables.description: Adds empty preference tables with the given names to the preference table container of a domain of Archicad 27 and returns their id, in one undo step. Only for Archicad 27.
CreateMEPPreferenceTables.name: CreateMEPPreferenceTables

domain.description: The MEP domain of a preference table container.

tables.description: The tables to add, empty, to the preference table container of the domain.

executionResults.description: One result per table, in the order of the tables.

CreateMEPRoutingElements.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateMEPRoutingElements.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

CreateMEPSystemGroups.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.
CreateMEPSystemGroups.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to create system groups.

CreateMEPSystems.description: Creates or overwrites MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface) based on the given parameters.
CreateMEPSystems.name: CreateMEPSystems

mepSystemDataArray.description: Array of data to create new MEP Systems.

items.description: Data to create an MEP System.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing MEP System to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

centerLinePen.description: The index of the center line pen [1..255].

centerLineTypeId.description: Identifier of the center line type attribute.

contourPen.description: The index of the contour pen [1..255].

domain.description: Only elements belonging to the same domain can use this system.

fillBackgroundPen.description: The index of the background pen [0..255]. 0 means transparent background.

fillId.description: Identifier of the fill pattern attribute.

fillPen.description: The index of the fill (foreground) pen [1..255].

index.description: Index of the existing MEP System to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

insulationMaterialId.description: Identifier of the surface (material) attribute applied to the insulation of the elements of the system.

materialId.description: Identifier of the surface (material) attribute applied to the 3D model of the elements of the system.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing MEP System with the given name will be overwritten.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the MEP System if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

CreateMEPTakeOffs.description: Creates MEP take-offs on the given routing segments, at a distance from the beginning of the segment (not more than its length) and optionally rotated around its axis by a multiple of 90 degrees, with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain (by default the domain of the segment's routing element), optionally with their length and without insulation, which apply only to what is created. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Available from Archicad 28.
CreateMEPTakeOffs.name: CreateMEPTakeOffs

takeOffsData.description: Array of data to create MEP take-offs on routing segments with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain.

CreateMeshes.description: Creates Mesh elements based on the given parameters.
CreateMeshes.name: CreateMeshes

meshesData.description: Array of data to create Meshes.

items.description: The parameters of the new Mesh.

buildingMaterialId.description: Optional building material of the mesh. Its top, side and bottom surface overrides are cleared, also one from the Mesh tool defaults, so the mesh shows the building material's own surface.

contourPen.description: Optional pen attribute index for the mesh's contour line.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

level.description: The Z reference level of coordinates.

levelPen.description: Optional pen attribute index for the mesh's level lines.

lineTypeIndex.description: Optional line type attribute index for the mesh's contour.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the mesh.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 3D coordinates of the outline polygon of the mesh.

showLines.description: Whether to show secondary mesh lines (level lines other than the user-defined ones) on plan.

sublines.description: The leveling sublines inside the polygon of the mesh.

CreateMorphs.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions or arbitrary bodies. Each item may name a favorite (favoriteName) to start from, a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id); the given geometry and floor are kept.
CreateMorphs.name: CreateMorphs

body.description: Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Morph favorite to base the new morph on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The geometry (basePoint, size or body, axes) and the floor always come from this item, not from the favorite.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

size.description: Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.

topExpansion.description: Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.

CreateObjects.description: Creates Object elements based on the given parameters. A library part named in libraryPartName starts from its own default size and GDL parameters, not from those of the part the Object tool holds; the dimensions and the GDL parameters given (by name, in parameters) override them. layerIndex places the element on a layer. With databaseId the objects are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, instead of the current one.
CreateObjects.name: CreateObjects

databaseId.description: Optional database to place the elements in, e.g. a worksheet or a detail (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), for a legend of symbols. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are placed in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

objectsData.description: Array of data to create Objects.

items.description: The parameters of the new Object.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part to use.

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

parameters.description: Optional GDL parameters to set by name, after dimensions. The value is a number, a boolean or a string; array parameters are not supported. A or B also set the size. An unknown name or a value of the wrong type fails the item, and nothing is created for it.

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

CreateOpenings.description: Creates Opening elements in the given host elements.
CreateOpenings.name: CreateOpenings

CreatePenTables.description: Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters.
CreatePenTables.name: CreatePenTables

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Pen Table if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

penTableDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Pen Tables.

items.description: Data to create a Pen Table.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

isActiveForLayout.description: Make this the active Pen Table for layouts. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.

isActiveForModel.description: Make this the active Pen Table for the model window. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Pen Table with the given name will be overwritten.

pens.description: The pens to set in the Pen Table, on top of the 255 pens copied from sourceAttributeId (or the current Pen Table, or an arbitrary existing one - see sourceAttributeId). Only list the pens you actually want to change.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of the Pen Table whose 255 pens are used as the starting point, before the pens listed in the pens array are applied on top. Defaults to the Pen Table being overwritten itself (so unlisted pens keep their current color/width/description), or an arbitrary existing Pen Table in the project when creating a brand new one (or a plain black, 0.1 mm pen for all 255 if the project has no Pen Table at all yet).

CreatePolylines.description: Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters.
CreatePolylines.name: CreatePolylines

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

polylinesData.description: Array of data to create Polylines.

items.description: The parameters of the new Polyline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the polyline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Pen index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current pen is used.

lineTypeIndex.description: Line type attribute index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current line type is used.

penWeightMm.description: Optional pen weight override in mm.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

CreateProfiles.description: Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.
CreateProfiles.name: CreateProfiles

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Profile if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

profileDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Profiles.

items.description: Data to create or modify a Profile. Its geometry (the cross-section shape) comes from sourceAttributeId (an existing Profile's geometry, copied), from newSkins (AC27+ only, caller-supplied polygon geometry), or both combined. When creating a brand-new Profile (overwriteExisting false, or true but no existing match), at least one of the two must be given. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, both are optional - the existing Profile's own current geometry is preserved by default (e.g. to change only wallType, or to add newSkins on top of the unchanged existing shape). skinOverrides and newSkins' edgeOverrides target skins/edges by the identifiers/indices GetProfiles reports.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

beamType.description: Profile available for beams. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

coluType.description: Profile available for columns. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

handrailType.description: Profile available for handrails. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

index.description: Index of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

moveVertices.description: Moves vertices of the copied (or, when overwriting, the preserved existing) geometry in place, e.g. to change the height of a wall profile by moving its top band, without rebuilding its skins: the skins keep their skinIds, edges and edge settings, so the profileModifiers, the stretch zones and every edge flag are kept. Applied in order, after skinOverrides and before newSkins. Hotspots and fixed modifier anchors inside the region are moved too, and so is a stretch zone limit inside it: a vertical stretch zone limit (a height) when the region has no xMin/xMax, a horizontal one when it has no yMin/yMax.

region.description: Selects the vertices to move: those with xMin <= x <= xMax and yMin <= y <= yMax, in the coordinates GetProfiles reports in skins[].outlineCoords. Each omitted bound leaves that side open, so { "yMin": 2.5 } selects every vertex at or above 2.5. Omit region to move every vertex.

skinIds.description: Moves only the vertices of these skins (GetProfiles' skins[].skinId). Omit to move the vertices of every skin.

vector.description: The displacement of the selected vertices.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Profile with the given name will be overwritten.

newSkins.description: AC27+ only. Adds brand-new skins built from caller-supplied polygon geometry, instead of (or in addition to) whatever was copied from sourceAttributeId. Combine with sourceAttributeId to add skins to a copied Profile, or omit sourceAttributeId to build a Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins.

otherGDLObjectType.description: Profile available for other GDL based objects. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

replaceSkins.description: AC27+ only. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, discard every one of its existing skins (and any sourceAttributeId geometry given alongside it) before applying newSkins, instead of adding newSkins on top of the preserved existing geometry. Use this to fully replace a Profile's cross-section with a caller-authored shape while keeping its guid and scalar fields (wallType etc.) - e.g. to sync a Profile's geometry from another project, where sourceAttributeId can't be used because it only resolves within the same file. Also discards any existing profileModifiers, since those are tied to the specific geometry being replaced. Ignored when creating a brand-new Profile (there is nothing to discard yet).

skinOverrides.description: Modifications to apply to specific skins of the copied geometry, e.g. to change a skin's building material without rebuilding the profile's shape. Each skinId comes from a prior GetProfiles call's skins[].skinId on the source Profile (or, when overwriteExisting is true, on the Profile being overwritten).

edgeOverrides.description: Modifications to specific edges of this skin, targeted by their position (0-based) in GetProfiles' skins[].edges.

skinId.description: Identifies which skin to modify, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of an existing Profile whose geometry (cross-section shape) will be copied as the starting point. Optional if newSkins is given: omit it to build the Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins instead of copying anything (AC27+ only).

wallType.description: Profile available for walls. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

CreateProjectInfoFields.description: Creates one or more custom project info fields. From Archicad 30 the Project Info group of each field can be given; without it the field goes to the first group.
CreateProjectInfoFields.name: CreateProjectInfoFields

projectInfoFields.description: Array of custom project info fields to create.

CreateProjectInfoGroups.description: Creates Project Info groups with the given names, at the end of the group list. Available from Archicad 30.
CreateProjectInfoGroups.name: CreateProjectInfoGroups

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to create, in order. Each is added to the end of the group list.

name.description: The name of the new group. It must not be used by another group.

CreatePropertyDefinitions.description: Creates Custom Property Definitions based on the given parameters.
CreatePropertyDefinitions.name: CreatePropertyDefinitions

propertyDefinitions.description: The parameters of the new properties.

CreatePropertyGroups.description: Creates Property Groups based on the given parameters.
CreatePropertyGroups.name: CreatePropertyGroups

propertyGroups.description: The parameters of the new property groups.

propertyGroupIds.description: The identifiers of the created property groups.

CreateRailings.description: Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite, from an existing railing (templateElementId) or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices.
CreateRailings.name: CreateRailings

railingsData.description: Array of data to create Railings.

items.description: The parameters of the new Railing. Everything not given here - the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters - comes from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults of the open project. Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices from them.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base height of the railing relative to the floor level. When omitted, the value of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the railing on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

templateElementId.description: Optional existing Railing whose settings the new railing takes instead of the tool defaults (or the favorite): its node and segment settings, from which the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters are generated, its story visibility, pens, bottom offset, layer and home story. floorIndex, bottomOffset and height given here override them. The reference line of a railing cannot be changed through the Archicad API, so a railing is given a new reference line by creating it again with itself as templateElementId and deleting the old one.

CreateRailingsFromPolyline.description: Creates Railing elements along a 3D reference polyline: each node has its own elevation and segments can be arcs. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults.
CreateRailingsFromPolyline.name: CreateRailingsFromPolyline

railingsData.description: Array of data to create Railings.

items.description: The parameters of the new Railing. Everything not given here - the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters - comes from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults of the open project. Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices from them.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

polylineArcs.description: Optional arc segments of the reference line. begIndex and endIndex are indices into polylineCoordinates and must be consecutive (endIndex = begIndex + 1).

polylineCoordinates.description: The nodes of the reference line of the railing. z is the elevation of the node relative to the floor level of the home story, so the railing can climb or descend along its segments.

CreateRoofs.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.
CreateRoofs.name: CreateRoofs

angle.description: Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

pivotLine.description: If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

CreateSections.description: Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active.
CreateSections.name: CreateSections

depth.description: The distance of the depth line from the section line, on the left of the start to end direction, which is the direction the section looks in. Default is 1.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Section favorite to base the new section on, marker included. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The Section tool defaults are restored afterwards.

id.description: The reference ID shown in the section marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker. Without it the section takes the ID of the Section tool defaults, or none with a favoriteName, as a Section favorite carries no ID.

CreateShells.description: Creates extruded, revolved and ruled Shell elements from profile polylines, with thickness, structure, an optional clipping contour and holes.
CreateShells.name: CreateShells

shellsData.description: Array of data to create Shells.

items.description: The parameters of the new Shell.

axis.description: Revolved only: the coordinate system whose Z axis the profile is turned around, in base plane coordinates. By default the base plane's Y axis.

basePlane.description: Base plane of the shell, in project coordinates; the profiles, the extrusion, the axis and the contour and hole polygons are given in it. The project axes by default, except for a Revolved shell, whose default base plane stands upright (its Y axis is the project Z axis), so the profile's x is the radius and its y the height.

begPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the start plane of the extrusion, in radians.

begShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the start of the shell (the start plane of an extrusion, the begin angle of a revolution, the first profile of a ruled shell). Perpendicular at pi/2 by default, as the Shell tool draws it, also when favoriteName is given.

begSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's first point sweeps from the start to the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

beginAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the revolution starts at, in radians.

contour.description: Optional clipping contour: only the part of the shell inside this polygon, seen along the Z axis of its plane, is kept. Its 'depth' is ignored.

distortionAngle.description: Revolved only: shear of the revolution, in radians. pi/2 (no shear) by default.

endPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the end plane of the extrusion, in radians.

endShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

endSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's last point sweeps. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

extrusionStart.description: Extruded only: the point the extrusion starts from, in base plane coordinates.

extrusionVector.description: Extruded only, required: the direction and length of the extrusion, in base plane coordinates.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Shell favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the shell. Without it the shell is placed on the story of the Shell tool defaults.

holes.description: Optional holes, each requiring 'depth' to extrude its cutting polygon along the Z axis of its plane.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

isFlipped.description: Applies the thickness to the other side of the reference surface.

morphingRule.description: Ruled only: how the two profiles are joined, segment by segment (Paired) or smoothly.

profile.description: The profile polyline. Extruded: in the plane across the extrusion, x horizontal and y up. Revolved: in the base plane's XY plane. Ruled: in the XY plane of 'profilePlane'.

profilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'profile', in base plane coordinates.

revolutionAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the profile is turned through, in radians. 2*pi (a full turn) by default.

secondProfile.description: Ruled only, required: the second profile polyline, in the XY plane of 'secondProfilePlane'.

secondProfilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'secondProfile', in base plane coordinates.

segmentsByCircle.description: Revolved only: the number of segments a full circle is resolved into.

shapePlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the profile's plane, in radians.

shellClass.description: Extruded: 'profile' swept along 'extrusionVector'. Revolved: 'profile' turned around 'axis'. Ruled: a surface ruled between 'profile' and 'secondProfile'.

slantAngle.description: Extruded and Revolved: slant of the extrusion vector or of the profile, in radians.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic shell; a Composite shell takes its thickness from the composite.

CreateSkylights.description: Creates Skylight elements with a roof or shell owner and a floor plan anchor position. It takes the same settings as ModifySkylights (anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display, pens, line types, section fill, surface and the library part flags) and optionally a library part; the settings not given come from the Skylight tool defaults or a favorite. Surface placement is handled by Archicad and has not yet been verified for this command.
CreateSkylights.name: CreateSkylights

skylightsData.description: Array of data to create Skylights.

items.description: The parameters of the new Skylight. The settings not given are the Skylight tool defaults' or the favorite's.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

anchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Skylight favorite to base the new element on.

fixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

libraryPartName.description: Optional localized name of a skylight library part to place instead of the tool default's.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

ownerId.description: The roof (single- or multi-plane) or shell the skylight is placed in.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectMaterials.description: Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

CreateSlabs.description: Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same surfaces (top, side, bottom), cut fill pens and floor fill as ModifySlabs, besides the outline, holes, level and structure; settings not given come from the Slab tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27; of the floor fill orientation Archicad applies only the type through the API.
CreateSlabs.name: CreateSlabs

slabsData.description: Array of data to create Slabs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Slab.

bottomMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.

buildingMaterialId.description: Building material of a Basic slab. Cannot be combined with compositeId.

compositeId.description: Composite attribute of a Composite slab. Cannot be combined with buildingMaterialId.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorFill.description: The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

level.description: The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the slab.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the edge of the slab.

referencePlaneLocation.description: For a basic (homogeneous) slab only 'Top' or 'Bottom' are valid.

sideMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.

structureType.description: Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.

thickness.description: Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

topMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.

CreateSolidElementLinks.description: Creates solid element operation links between target and operator elements.
CreateSolidElementLinks.name: CreateSolidElementLinks

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to create.

CreateSolidOperations.description: Runs a solid operation (subtraction, intersection, addition) on two morphs and returns the resulting morphs, one item per operation. Unlike CreateSolidElementLinks this is not a link: the target and the operator morph are replaced by the result. Morphs only; the operations run in one undo step.
CreateSolidOperations.name: CreateSolidOperations

operations.description: The solid operations to run, each on two morphs. The target and the operator morph are replaced by the resulting morph.

results.description: One item per operation, in the order of the input: the resulting morphs, or an error.

elements.description: The morphs created by the operation.

CreateSplines.description: Creates Spline elements based on the given parameters.
CreateSplines.name: CreateSplines

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

splinesData.description: Array of data to create Splines. Only auto-smoothed curves are supported (bezier handle positions are calculated automatically by Archicad from the point positions).

items.description: The parameters of the new Spline.

closed.description: Is this a closed curve? Optional, defaults to false.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the spline points. Do not repeat the first point at the end even for a closed spline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the spline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

CreateStairs.description: Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters, optionally with the segment type of each baseline edge and the turn at each baseline point (landings and winders). Accepts the same settings as ModifyStairs: the step values with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra treads, the walking line, the numbering, the walking direction, and the tread, riser and structure settings of the flights and the landings; settings not given come from the Stair tool defaults or the favorite.
CreateStairs.name: CreateStairs

stairsData.description: Array of data to create Stair elements.

items.description: The parameters of the new Stair.

baseLineEdges.description: Optional. The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (baseLinePoints.length - 1 items; edge i runs from point i to point i + 1). A U-shaped stair with a half landing is Flight, Landing, Flight with landing turns at both inner points. When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineVertices is given, every edge is a flight. Combinations Archicad cannot build fail like any other invalid stair.

segmentType.description: Flight: steps. Landing: a landing segment, the edge between two landing turns of a U-shaped stair. DividedLanding: a divided landing segment.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates of the stair baseline polyline. Whether the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight is the Stair tool's baseline position, taken from baselinePosition, or else from the tool defaults or favoriteName: with the baseline on the left edge, the flight lies to the right of it, looking from the first point to the last. The first point is kept; the length of the flight comes from the riser count and going, so the flight does not necessarily end at the last point given. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

baseLineVertices.description: Optional. The turn at each baseline point, one item per point (baseLinePoints.length items). When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineEdges is given, the first and last points get no turn and every other point a landing turn. Winders use Archicad's default winder settings.

minLandingEndEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal trail edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer after the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingEndEdgeOffset).

minLandingStartEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal lead edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer before the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much, to fit the steps (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingStartEdgeOffset).

turnType.description: The turn at this point. The first and last points take None.

baselineOffset.description: Optional. The offset of the baseline from the flight edge that baselinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center. Without it the offset of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is kept.

baselinePosition.description: Optional. Where the baseline runs on the flight, looking from the first point to the last. Left: along the left edge, the flight lies to the right of the baseline. Right: along the right edge, the flight lies to the left of it. Center: along the middle of the flight. Without it the baseline position of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is used.

extraBottomTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.

extraTopTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

inputDirection.description: The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).

numberingType.description: Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser. Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not use this riser height.

risers.description: The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

stepNum.description: Number of risers (steps). Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not have this many risers.

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown.

structures.description: The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed.

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

totalHeightLocked.description: Whether the total height is locked.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread. Pinned as a fixed going in the stair rules, so the run length follows from the number of treads; the standard's combined riser/going rules (2R+G, R+G, R/G) are not applied to this stair.

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.

treads.description: The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

uniformDrainings.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.

uniformFinish.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.

uniformMonolithAttributes.description: Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.

walkingLineOffset.description: The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.

walkingLinePosition.description: Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

CreateSurfaces.description: Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateSurfaces.name: CreateSurfaces

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Surface if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

surfaceDataArray.description: Array of data to create new surfaces.

items.description: Data to create a surface.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing surface with the given name will be overwritten.

CreateTexts.description: Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.
CreateTexts.name: CreateTexts

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

textsData.description: Array of data to create Texts.

items.description: The parameters of the new Text element.

angle.description: Optional rotation angle in radians. Equivalent to style.angle.

coordinate.description: The placement position of the text. The z value is used to determine the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

height.description: The character height in millimeters. Optional; defaults to the Text tool default. Equivalent to style.height.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index. If omitted, the Text tool default layer is used.

pen.description: Optional pen attribute index. Equivalent to style.penIndex.

runs.description: Multi-style text content: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

style.description: height/pen/angle/justification above take precedence over the same fields here if both are given.

text.description: The text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

width.description: Optional box width in mm (paper size, like height). Turns word wrap on: the text wraps within this width ('Wrap Text' in the Text settings, nonBreaking false). When omitted the text is auto-width (word wrap off) and grows with its content. Read back by GetDetailsOfElements as style.boxWidth, with style.nonBreaking false.

CreateViewMapFolder.description: Creates a new folder in the View Map.
CreateViewMapFolder.name: CreateViewMapFolder

folderName.description: Name of the new folder to create in the View Map.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the parent View Map folder. Optional; defaults to the View Map root.

CreateViewsInViewMap.description: Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items.
CreateViewsInViewMap.name: CreateViewsInViewMap

viewsData.description: Array of views to create as independent (non-clone) items in the View Map.

name.description: Name for the new view. Optional; defaults to the source item name.

navigatorItemId.description: Source navigator item whose database and settings are copied: a Project Map item, or a View Map view (e.g. a story view). A View Map view is created from its Project Map source (sourceNavigatorItemId in GetNavigatorItemTree), then gets the view's own view settings, name and ID.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: View Map folder to place the new view in. Required - the underlying Archicad API used to create the item leaves it undeletable and unmovable afterwards when it is attached directly to the View Map root, so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

CreateWallThicknessDimensions.description: Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls.
CreateWallThicknessDimensions.name: CreateWallThicknessDimensions

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.
