marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

CreateWalls.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls, applied by the same code, except geometryType and profileType, which the new wall takes from the favorite or the Wall tool defaults (its plan outline is always Straight), and bottomOffset, which comes from zCoordinate. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'.
CreateWalls.name: CreateWalls

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Background pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

cutFillPen.description: Pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.

flipped.description: Optional. True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped). When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's side is kept, which for a Profile wall mirrors its whole cross section.

floorIndex.description: Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.

height.description: Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

linkToSettings.description: When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

offset.description: Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

referenceLineLocation.description: Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' for the same wall: whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

structureType.description: Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.

thickness.description: Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.

CreateWindows.description: Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters.
CreateWindows.name: CreateWindows

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Window favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Window tool defaults before the create.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a window library part. Set on the created window only, with its A and B from `width` and `height` (or the tool default's width and height); the Window tool defaults are not changed.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

CreateWorksheetMarkers.description: Places Worksheet markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Worksheet viewpoint, like the Worksheet tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.
CreateWorksheetMarkers.name: CreateWorksheetMarkers

angle.description: Rotation of the marker symbol in radians. Default is that of the tool defaults.

clipPolygon.description: The boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

floorIndex.description: Story of the marker when it is placed on a floor plan. Default is the current story.

id.description: Reference ID shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker. Default is that of the tool defaults.

markerCoordinate.description: Where the marker symbol is placed. Default is the first point of clipPolygon.

name.description: Name of the new viewpoint. Default is that of the tool defaults.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

CreateWorksheets.description: Creates independent Worksheet databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new worksheet.
CreateWorksheets.name: CreateWorksheets

databases.description: One item per input item, in the same order.

CreateZoneCategories.description: Creates or overwrites Zone Category attributes based on the given parameters.
CreateZoneCategories.name: CreateZoneCategories

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Zone Category if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

zoneCategoryDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Zone Categories.

items.description: Data to create a Zone Category.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Zone Category to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Zone Category to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Zone Category with the given name will be overwritten.

stampMainGuid.description: Main GUID of the zone stamp library part to use, e.g. the value returned by GetZoneCategories for an existing Zone Category or shown as MainGuid in an Attribute Manager XML export. If omitted, the stamp is copied from the Zone Category being overwritten, or from an existing Zone Category of the project when creating a new one.

stampName.description: Document name of the zone stamp library part (GSM) to use, e.g. the value returned by GetZoneCategories or shown as StampDocumentName in an Attribute Manager XML export. Only used together with stampMainGuid/stampRevGuid; ignored otherwise.

stampRevGuid.description: Revision GUID of the zone stamp library part to use, e.g. the value shown as RevGuid in an Attribute Manager XML export. Required together with stampMainGuid.

CreateZones.description: Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same zone settings as ModifyZones (name, number, category, zone stamp, levels, contour line and cover fill), applied by the same helpers; the polygon or reference point is only set here. An item whose area would overlap an existing Zone on the same story fails with an error naming that Zone instead of opening Archicad's modal overlap warning, unless its allowOverlap is true.
CreateZones.name: CreateZones

zonesData.description: Array of data to create Zones.

items.description: The parameters of the new Zone.

allowOverlap.description: Optional, defaults to false. Archicad answers a new zone whose area overlaps an existing zone on the same story with a modal warning dialog that blocks the API until it is dismissed, so by default such an item fails with an error naming the overlapping zone and no element is created for it. Set it to true to skip this check and create the zone anyway; the dialog may then appear. Zones that only touch (a shared edge or corner) do not overlap; curved edges are checked by their chords, and an automatic zone counts as overlapping when its referencePosition lies inside an existing zone.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

contourLine.description: Optional contour line of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

coverFill.description: Optional cover fill of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.

floorThickness.description: Optional thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

height.description: Optional height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height); when omitted, the height and top link of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults are kept. Do not combine with relativeTopStory.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

name.description: Name of the zone.

relativeTopStory.description: Optional top link: non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not combine with height.

stampAngle.description: Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

topOffset.description: Optional offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations.description: Turns off the given design options in the given combinations, leaving their other options as they are. Available from Archicad 29.
DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations.name: DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations

DeleteAnalyticalLoadCases.description: Deletes the given structural analysis load cases in one undo step.
DeleteAnalyticalLoadCases.name: DeleteAnalyticalLoadCases

DeleteAnalyticalLoadCombinations.description: Deletes the given structural analysis load combinations in one undo step.
DeleteAnalyticalLoadCombinations.name: DeleteAnalyticalLoadCombinations

DeleteAnalyticalLoadGroups.description: Deletes the given structural analysis load groups in one undo step.
DeleteAnalyticalLoadGroups.name: DeleteAnalyticalLoadGroups

DeleteAndReplaceAttributes.description: Deletes fills, line types, surfaces or building materials and replaces each by another attribute of the same type wherever it was used, like Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager. Every reference is rewritten to the replacement, the way ReindexAttributes rewrites them: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, their memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Elements on a hidden or locked layer are changed too: their layers are shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards (in the current window). If an element cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not deleted. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the deleted attribute (named in the warnings). If a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule cannot be rewritten to the replacement, it keeps a copy of the deleted attribute with its name and a new attribute id, named in the warnings. The whole call is one undo step. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks gets wouldDelete and lists every reference a real run would rewrite (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules). Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteAndReplaceAttributes.name: DeleteAndReplaceAttributes

attributeType.description: The type of the attributes to delete and of their replacements.

attributes.description: The attributes to delete, each with the attribute that takes its place, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The attribute to delete.

replacementAttributeId.description: The attribute of the same type that replaces it wherever it is used. It must be another attribute than the one to delete.

attributes.description: One item per requested attribute, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The deleted attribute (with dryRun, the attribute that would be deleted).

attributes.description: The other attributes that referred to the deleted attribute: composites (skins and separators), building materials (cut fill, cut surface), surfaces (hatching fill), MEP systems (fill) and profiles (skins and edges). Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

elements.description: The elements that referred to the deleted attribute, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout: in their own fields, their library part parameters or their memo data (side surfaces, roof levels, morph faces, cutting planes). They refer to the replacement now, unless dryRun is true.

favorites.description: The names of the Favorites that referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

hotlinkElements.description: Elements from hotlinked modules that refer to the deleted attribute. They cannot be changed; replace the attribute in their module file.

layersShown.description: The hidden or locked layers of the elements that were shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards. Not present with dryRun.

overrideRules.description: The names of the graphic override rules that referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

replacementAttributeId.description: The attribute that took its place.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

warnings.description: What still refers to the deleted attribute: elements from hotlinked modules, a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule that could not be written. What could not be rewritten to the replacement keeps a copy of the deleted attribute, whose attribute id the last warning names.

wouldDelete.description: Only on a dry run: the attribute and its replacement passed the checks, and a real run would delete the attribute and rewrite the references listed here to the replacement.

DeleteAttributeFolders.description: Deletes attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, together with all the subfolders and deletable attributes they contain (a folder holding an attribute that cannot be deleted is kept). The root folder cannot be deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted: the response has dryRun set to true, and each folder that exists and is not the root folder gets wouldDelete. Available from Archicad 26.
DeleteAttributeFolders.name: DeleteAttributeFolders

executionResults.description: One result for each input folder, in the order of the input. On a dry run a folder that is not the root folder and exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete a folder that passes these checks.

DeleteAttributes.description: Deletes the given attributes. Returns an execution result for each input item. With dryRun true nothing is deleted: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks made before deleting (valid attribute type, attribute exists) gets wouldDelete.
DeleteAttributes.name: DeleteAttributes

executionResults.description: One result for each input attribute, in the order of the input. On a dry run an attribute that passes the checks made before deleting (valid attributeType, attribute found) gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete an attribute that passes them.

DeleteClassificationItems.description: Deletes the given Classification Items. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each classification item that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeleteClassificationItems.name: DeleteClassificationItems

executionResults.description: One result for each input classification item, in the order of the input. On a dry run a classification item that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete one that exists.

DeleteClassificationSystems.description: Deletes the given Classification Systems. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each classification system that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeleteClassificationSystems.name: DeleteClassificationSystems

executionResults.description: One result for each input classification system, in the order of the input. On a dry run a classification system that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete one that exists.

DeleteDesignOptionCombinations.description: Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteDesignOptionCombinations.name: DeleteDesignOptionCombinations

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to delete.

DeleteDesignOptionSets.description: Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteDesignOptionSets.name: DeleteDesignOptionSets

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to delete.

DeleteDesignOptions.description: Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteDesignOptions.name: DeleteDesignOptions

DeleteElectricalCircuits.description: Removes electrical circuits from their panels. Available from Archicad 30.
DeleteElectricalCircuits.name: DeleteElectricalCircuits

electricalCircuits.description: The circuits to remove from their panels.

DeleteElementSets.description: Deletes the given element sets. The elements of a set are not deleted. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On can be deleted; sets created by other add-ons are reported as failed. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element set that a real run would delete gets wouldDelete.
DeleteElementSets.name: DeleteElementSets

elementSets.description: The element sets to delete, as returned by CreateElementSets or GetElementSetsOfElements. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On can be deleted. The elements of a deleted set are not deleted.

elementSetId.description: The identifier of an element set.

executionResults.description: One result for each input element set, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element set that exists and was created by the Tapir Add-On gets wouldDelete.

DeleteElements.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before deleting gets wouldDelete, so a script can preview a deletion before making it.
DeleteElements.name: DeleteElements

elements.description: The elements to delete. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.

executionResults.description: One result for each input element, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that passes every check made before deleting (it exists, its layer is not locked, it is editable) gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems.description: Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems.name: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems

embeddedLibraryItems.description: A list of embedded library items to delete.

DeleteFavoriteFolder.description: Deletes a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Archicad deletes the folder's Favorites and subfolders with it, so a folder that is not empty is deleted only if recursive is true. The root folder cannot be deleted. Returns the deleted folder. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteFavoriteFolder.name: DeleteFavoriteFolder

path.description: The path of the folder to delete, in the format GetFavoriteFolders returns: the folder names from the root down. The root folder cannot be deleted.

recursive.description: Archicad deletes a folder together with everything in it: its Favorites and its subfolders with their Favorites. A folder that is not empty is deleted only if this is true. Default: false.

DeleteFavoritesWithManager.description: Deletes the given Favorites through the Favorite manager, each found by name, optionally only in the given folder. One execution result for each. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteFavoritesWithManager.name: DeleteFavoritesWithManager

DeleteGhostRecords.description: Deletes the trace (ghost) record of each given parent database, which removes the trace reference shown in that database's window. A database without a trace reference gets a failed execution result. Not undoable.
DeleteGhostRecords.name: DeleteGhostRecords

databases.description: The parent databases whose trace (ghost) record is deleted, as returned by GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId or GetContainingDatabases.

DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations.description: Deletes graphic override combinations. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations

graphicOverrideCombinationIds.description: The graphic override combinations to delete. Their rules are kept.

DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: Deletes graphic override rule groups, found by name. A group that still contains rules is kept unless its rules are moved to another group or deleted with it. Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups

deleteRules.description: Delete the rules of the deleted groups too. Without this or moveRulesToGroup, a group that still contains rules is not deleted.

moveRulesToGroup.description: The name of the rule group the rules of the deleted groups are moved to, so they are kept. Created when no rule group has this name.

ruleGroupNames.description: The names of the rule groups to delete.

DeleteGraphicOverrideRules.description: Deletes graphic override rules. They are also removed from the combinations that contain them. Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteGraphicOverrideRules.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRules

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The graphic override rules to delete.

DeleteHotlinkNodes.description: Deletes hotlink nodes together with their placed instances, as the Hotlink Manager's Delete does.
DeleteHotlinkNodes.name: DeleteHotlinkNodes

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to delete, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. Each node is removed together with its placed instances and their elements, as the Hotlink Manager's Delete does; use BreakHotlinkNodes instead to keep the elements. In Teamwork the Hotlink and XRef management has to be reserved first (ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement).

DeleteIssue.description: Deletes the specified issue. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and wouldDelete when the issue exists.
DeleteIssue.name: DeleteIssue

acceptAllElements.description: Accept all creation/deletion/modification of the deleted issue. By default false.

returns.description: The result of the execution: success, with error when it failed. A dry run also answers dryRun, and wouldDelete when the issue exists.

DeleteKeynoteFolders.description: Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28.
DeleteKeynoteFolders.name: DeleteKeynoteFolders

DeleteKeynoteItems.description: Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.
DeleteKeynoteItems.name: DeleteKeynoteItems

DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems.description: Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29.
DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems.name: DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems

physicalSystems.description: The physical systems to remove from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted.

DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.description: Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27.
DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.name: DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows

keys.description: The keys of the rows to delete. Segment tables, and the elbow tables of Archicad 28, have a row for each reference id, which is emptied instead. Archicad 27: the indices are those before the call; the rows are deleted from the highest index down.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

DeleteModulData.description: Deletes the module data with the given names. Deleting module data is not an undoable step.
DeleteModulData.name: DeleteModulData

names.description: The names of the module data to delete; the empty name is the default section.

DeleteNavigatorItems.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets, View Map folders that are not empty, the other Project Map items and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted; the failed execution result says which case applies. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. dryRun reports the result of the checks made before deleting (item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty) without deleting anything.
DeleteNavigatorItems.name: DeleteNavigatorItems

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is deleted: each execution result says what the deletion would do for that item, from the checks made before deleting (corrupt id, item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them: a Project Map item other than an independent worksheet, detail or viewpoint created by the Tapir Add-On, a marker-linked worksheet or detail, or in a Teamwork project an item that is not reserved. Default is false.

DeleteProjectData.description: Deletes the project data with the given names.
DeleteProjectData.name: DeleteProjectData

names.description: The names of the project data to delete.

DeleteProjectInfoFields.description: Deletes one or more custom project info fields, by their autotext keys or, from Archicad 30, by the ids of the fields of the Project Info groups. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted.
DeleteProjectInfoFields.name: DeleteProjectInfoFields

projectInfoFieldIds.description: List of fields of the Project Info groups to delete, by the ids GetProjectInfoGroups returns. Available from Archicad 30. Their results follow the results of projectInfoIds.

projectInfoIds.description: List of project info field ids (autotext keys, as GetProjectInfoFields returns them) to delete. Only custom fields can be deleted. On Archicad 30 a key is matched to the field by its name, so it fails when more than one field has the name; delete such a field by its projectInfoFieldId instead.

DeleteProjectInfoGroups.description: Deletes Project Info groups. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 30.
DeleteProjectInfoGroups.name: DeleteProjectInfoGroups

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to delete. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted.

DeletePropertyDefinitions.description: Deletes the given Custom Property Definitions. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each property that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeletePropertyDefinitions.name: DeletePropertyDefinitions

propertyIds.description: The identifiers of properties to delete.

executionResults.description: One result for each input property, in the order of the input. On a dry run a property that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete one that exists (for example a built-in property).

DeletePropertyGroups.description: Deletes the given Custom Property Groups. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each property group that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeletePropertyGroups.name: DeletePropertyGroups

propertyGroupIds.description: The identifiers of property groups to delete.

executionResults.description: One result for each input property group, in the order of the input. On a dry run a property group that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete one that exists (for example a built-in group).

DeleteSelectedElements.description: Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true and lists the selected elements, with wouldDelete when there is at least one, or fails when one of them cannot be edited (Archicad then deletes none of them).
DeleteSelectedElements.name: DeleteSelectedElements

returns.description: The result of the execution. A real run answers success, with error when it failed; a dry run also answers dryRun, and the elements it would delete.

elements.description: Only on a dry run: the selected elements (for a marquee, the ones it touches). A real run deletes them, together with the other members of their groups when Suspend Groups is off and the elements linked to them (labels, dimensions, ...).

wouldDelete.description: Only on a dry run that passed the checks: true when at least one element is selected.

DeleteUserDataOfAttributes.description: Removes the user data of attributes, every key at once. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. With dryRun true nothing is removed: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeleteUserDataOfAttributes.name: DeleteUserDataOfAttributes

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order. On a dry run an attribute that exists gets wouldDelete.

DeleteUserDataOfElements.description: Deletes the user data this add-on stored on the given elements. Archicad keeps the user data of an element per add-on, so the data of other add-ons is left as it is. All deletions are one undo step. The output has one execution result per element, aligned with the input array of elements. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that exists gets wouldDelete.
DeleteUserDataOfElements.name: DeleteUserDataOfElements

executionResults.description: One result per element, aligned with the input. On a dry run an element that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete its user data.

DeselectAll.description: Clears the selection in the current window.
DeselectAll.name: DeselectAll

DetachElementsFromIssue.description: Detaches elements from the specified issue.
DetachElementsFromIssue.name: DetachElementsFromIssue

DistributeElements.description: Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still distributed.
DistributeElements.name: DistributeElements

direction.description: horizontal distributes the elements along X, vertical along Y. They are not moved in the other direction.

elements.description: At least 3 elements to distribute: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database. Their order does not matter: they are distributed in the order of the middles of their plan bounding boxes along the direction.

mode.description: centers makes the distances between the middles of the plan bounding boxes equal, gaps makes the empty space between neighbouring bounding boxes equal (the gap is negative, so the boxes overlap, when the elements are wider together than the space between the two outermost elements).

DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations.description: Duplicates the given design option combinations and returns the identifiers of the new combinations. Available from Archicad 29.
DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations.name: DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to duplicate.

designOptionCombinationIdsOrErrors.description: The identifiers of the new combinations, in the order of the input, or an error for each combination that could not be duplicated.

EditHierarchicalElement.description: Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Limitation: while the editing mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command, this add-on's included, with error 4001 (ongoing user input), FinishHierarchicalEditing included, so the mode can only be left in Archicad, with the button of its edit mode palette (reported for Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
EditHierarchicalElement.name: EditHierarchicalElement

elementId.description: The hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) to open in hierarchical editing mode.

ElevateElements.description: Moves elements vertically by a given offset in meters, like Edit > Move > Elevate. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.
ElevateElements.name: ElevateElements

elementsWithElevations.description: The elements with elevation offset pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be elevated. By default it's false.

elevation.description: The vertical offset in meters to move the element by, like Edit > Move > Elevate. A positive value moves the element up, a negative value moves it down. The home story of the element does not change.

ExportFavorites.description: Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format). With overwrite false an export to a single file refuses to replace an existing file.
ExportFavorites.name: ExportFavorites

format.description: prefs (the default) works in every Archicad version. xml exports each Favorite to its own file in the folder, and legacyPRF exports to a Favorites file of earlier Archicad versions; these two require Archicad 29 or newer.

names.description: Optional subset of Favorites to export. Default: export all.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default: an existing file is overwritten. false refuses to export when a file already exists at path, and writes nothing. It needs an export to a single file (prefs format with a .prefs path, or legacyPRF format); with an export to a folder it is an error, as the names of the files written there are Archicad's.

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: if extension matches the Favorite binary format (.prefs), writes a single file; otherwise treats as folder. With the xml format: the folder to write the Favorite files to. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file to write.

ExportIssuesToBCF.description: Exports specified issues to a BCF file. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.
ExportIssuesToBCF.name: ExportIssuesToBCF

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

exportPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false.

issues.description: Leave it empty to export all issues.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. false refuses to export when a file already exists at exportPath, and writes nothing.

useExternalId.description: Use external IFC ID or Archicad IFC ID as referenced in BCF topics.

FilterElements.description: Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices), element type (elementTypes) and hotlink (fromHotlink, hotlinkIds). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.
FilterElements.name: FilterElements

elementTypes.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.

filters.description: Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.

floorIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

fromHotlink.description: Optional. true keeps only the elements that came in through a placed hotlink (they are read-only), false only the project's own elements.

hotlinkIds.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it came in through one of these placed hotlink instances (the hotlinkId field of GetDetailsOfElements, elements of type Hotlink).

layerIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

FindDimensionStandard.description: Finds a dimension standard (Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions) by its name and returns its index, name and guid. Available from Archicad 27.
FindDimensionStandard.name: FindDimensionStandard

name.description: The name of the dimension standard, as listed in Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions.

dimensionStandardId.description: The guid of the dimension standard.

index.description: The index of the dimension standard.

name.description: The name of the dimension standard.

FindLibraryParts.description: Finds loaded library parts with the Library Manager: all of them, GDL objects, images or text files, optionally only those whose name contains a text. Returns the name, path and index of each. Available from Archicad 28.
FindLibraryParts.name: FindLibraryParts

firstOnly.description: Optional. When true, only the first matching library part is returned. By default false.

nameContains.description: Optional. Only library parts whose name contains this text, ignoring case.

libraryParts.description: The matching library parts.

FindModelViewOption.description: Finds a model view option combination by id or by name and returns its index, id, name and flags. The index is the one SetViewOptions takes to switch the model view options of a window to the combination. Available from Archicad 27.
FindModelViewOption.name: FindModelViewOption

parameters.description: The model view option combination to find, given by id or by name.

name.description: The name of the model view option combination, as shown in Document > Model View > Model View Options.

returns.description: The model view option combination found.

flags.description: The flags of the model view option combination, as Archicad returns them.

index.description: The index of the model view option combination.

name.description: The name of the model view option combination.

FinishHierarchicalEditing.description: Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this command cannot leave a mode opened by EditHierarchicalElement or in Archicad (reported for Archicad 29); leave it in Archicad instead. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
FinishHierarchicalEditing.name: FinishHierarchicalEditing

accept.description: True to accept the changes made in the hierarchical editing mode (OK), false to discard them (Cancel).

FitInWindow.description: Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window.
FitInWindow.name: FitInWindow

GenerateDocumentation.description: Generates files for the documentation. Used by Tapir developers only.
GenerateDocumentation.name: GenerateDocumentation

destinationFolder.description: Destination folder for the generated documentation files.

Get2DBoundingBoxes.description: Get the 2D bounding box of elements as Archicad draws them, in the coordinates of the database the element is in: the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout or a master layout. Works for 2D elements (Line, PolyLine, Arc, Hatch, Text, Label, Dimension, Drawing ...) as well as for model elements; a Text's box covers its drawn lines, a Drawing's box its frame with the title. The current window does not need to show the element. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.
Get2DBoundingBoxes.name: Get2DBoundingBoxes

Get3DBoundingBoxes.description: Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. An element without 3D geometry of its own gets an error item instead of a bounding box. Walls, Slabs, Roofs, Zones and Stairs are measured on their 3D model, so the box of a Wall includes its connections to other walls. The current window does not need to show the element: it works with a layout or a section open as well.
Get3DBoundingBoxes.name: Get3DBoundingBoxes

Get3DCutPlanes.description: Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on and the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.
Get3DCutPlanes.name: Get3DCutPlanes

cutPlanes.description: The cut planes, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes: pa*x + pb*y + pc*z + pd = 0, pd in meters.

isCutPlanes.description: Whether the 3D cut planes are switched on.

useCustom.description: Whether the custom cut settings are used.

Get3DCutawayStatus.description: Returns whether 3D Cutaway is on and whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
Get3DCutawayStatus.name: Get3DCutawayStatus

cutawayEnabled.description: Whether 3D Cutaway is on in the 3D window.

cuttingPlanesVisible.description: Whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window.

Get3DDocumentSettings.description: Gets the settings of a 3D Document, given by its navigator item: the element and story filter, the 3D cut, the projection, the window and zoom, the uniform cut and uncut surface attributes, the source and the boundary contours, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType.
Get3DDocumentSettings.name: Get3DDocumentSettings

navigatorItemId.description: The navigator item of the 3D Document, from the Project Map or the View Map.

settings.description: The settings of the 3D Document, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType.

attributeOptions.description: The uniform attributes of cut and uncut surfaces (API_UniformAttributeOptions). Pens and uniformLineType are indices; the enums fillCutSurfacesWith, uncutSurfaceFillType, hiddenEdgeVisibility and onCutPlaneVisibility are their integer values.

hiddenEdgeLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

shadFill.description: A fill. Missing when there is none.

boundaryLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

cutSetting.description: The 3D cut of the 3D Document (API_3DCutPlanesInfo). The cut planes themselves are not included.

customMater.description: The surface of the cut. Missing when there is none.

docSrc.description: Whether the 3D Document comes from the 3D window or from the floor plan.

filterAndCutSettings.description: Which elements and stories the 3D Document shows (API_3DFilterAndCutSettings). The marquee filter is not included.

allStories.description: Whether all stories are shown; if false, firstStory3D to lastStory3D.

elemTypeFilter.description: Whether each element type is shown. On Set only the listed element types are changed.

hiddenLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

projectionSetting.description: The projection of the 3D Document (API_3DProjectionInfo). persp is present when isPersp is true, axono otherwise. Changing isPersp starts the new projection from zero, give persp or axono with it.

actCamSet.description: The active Camera Set. Missing when there is none.

tranmat.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix, row by row.

camGuid.description: The Camera the projection comes from. Missing when there is none.

skeletonOptions.description: API_SkeletonOptions of a 3D Document made from the floor plan. viewSrc is the integer value of API_ViewSourceID.

Get3DFilterAndCutSettings.description: Gets the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window: the stories shown, the filter mode and which element types are shown. Available from Archicad 27.
Get3DFilterAndCutSettings.name: Get3DFilterAndCutSettings

Get3DGeometryOfElements.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.
Get3DGeometryOfElements.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements

geometries3D.description: The 3D geometry of each element, aligned with the input: the solid bodies of its 3D model, or an error.

Get3DModelCounts.description: Gets the number of components of each type (bodies, polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices, normal vectors, materials and lights) in the 3D model Archicad currently holds. Bodies, materials and lights are counted with ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum; the polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices and normal vectors, which that function refuses to count, are summed over the bodies. A type that cannot be counted gets an error item. Available from Archicad 27.
Get3DModelCounts.name: Get3DModelCounts

counts.description: The number of components of each type in the 3D model Archicad currently holds, one item per type, or an error for a type that could not be counted.

Get3DProjectionSettings.description: Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the projection type, azimuth and transformation matrix of an axonometry, and the sun position of either (date and time or azimuth and altitude).
Get3DProjectionSettings.name: Get3DProjectionSettings

activeCameraSetElementId.description: The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.

axonometric.description: The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

sun.description: The sun position of the axonometry.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).

cameraElementId.description: The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.

isPersp.description: True for a perspective projection, false for an axonometric one.

perspective.description: The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.

Get3DStyleDetails.description: Gets the settings of 3D styles by name (an empty name or no names means the current 3D style): rendering engine, model type, monochrome and background colors, contours, shadows and hatching. Available from Archicad 27.
Get3DStyleDetails.name: Get3DStyleDetails

names.description: The names of the 3D styles. An empty name means the current 3D style. When omitted, the current 3D style is returned.

styles.description: The details of the 3D styles, in the order of the input names.

Get3DStyles.description: Gets the names of the 3D styles of the project and the name of the current one, which the 3D window uses.
Get3DStyles.name: Get3DStyles

currentStyleName.description: The name of the current 3D style, the one the 3D window uses.

styleNames.description: The names of the 3D styles of the project.

Get3DWindowSettings.description: Gets the 3D window settings: the pixel size of the 3D window and the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection.
Get3DWindowSettings.name: Get3DWindowSettings

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.description: Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.
GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.name: GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination

returns.description: The graphic override combination applied to the current window. Empty when the current window has no combination applied.

combinationId.description: The identifier of the graphic override combination.

name.description: The name of the graphic override combination. Missing when the combination cannot be read, e.g. it was deleted.

GetAddOnVersion.description: Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.
GetAddOnVersion.name: GetAddOnVersion

version.description: Version number in the form of "1.1.1".

GetAddOnViewpointChildren.description: Returns the direct children of an add-on viewpoint root or group. Available from Archicad 27.
GetAddOnViewpointChildren.name: GetAddOnViewpointChildren

viewpointId.description: The add-on viewpoint root or group to list the children of.
The identifier of an add-on viewpoint item.

GetAddOnViewpointRoots.description: Returns the roots of the add-on viewpoints: the Project Map items created through the Archicad API by an add-on, as Archicad lists them to Tapir. Available from Archicad 27.
GetAddOnViewpointRoots.name: GetAddOnViewpointRoots

viewpointId.description: The identifier of an add-on viewpoint item.

GetAddOnViewpoints.description: Returns the details of the given add-on viewpoint items: their parent, type (Root, Group or Leaf), ID, name, view settings flags and attached data (base64 encoded). The output is aligned with the input array; an item that cannot be read gets an error. Available from Archicad 27.
GetAddOnViewpoints.name: GetAddOnViewpoints

viewpointId.description: The identifier of an add-on viewpoint item.

viewpoints.description: The details of each given add-on viewpoint item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that cannot be read.

GetAllAutoTextKeys.description: Retrieves every autotext key Archicad knows (not only the property-based ones returned by GetAutoTextKeys) with its current value, resolved without an element context.
GetAllAutoTextKeys.name: GetAllAutoTextKeys

key.description: The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>'.

value.description: The autotext's current value, as Archicad resolves it without an element context.

GetAllClassificationSystems.description: Returns the classification systems of the project with their guid, name, description, source, version and date. Same output as the official GetAllClassificationSystems command, so scripts can rely on Tapir commands only.
GetAllClassificationSystems.name: GetAllClassificationSystems

classificationSystems.description: The classification systems of the project.

GetAllElements.description: Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.
GetAllElements.name: GetAllElements

GetAllElementsOfGroups.description: Gets all the elements of each given group, including the elements of its nested groups.
GetAllElementsOfGroups.name: GetAllElementsOfGroups

groups.description: The groups to get all the elements of.

elementsOfGroups.description: All the elements of each given group, including the elements of its nested groups, or an error.

GetAllFavorites.description: Returns every Favorite of the project, or only those of the given element type, with its name and element type. Available from Archicad 29.
GetAllFavorites.name: GetAllFavorites

elementType.description: Only the Favorites of this element type are returned. Omit it to get every Favorite.

GetAllProperties.description: Returns all user defined and built-in properties. Optionally only the given properties or property types, and without the availability lists.
GetAllProperties.name: GetAllProperties

includeAvailability.description: Adds the availability list (the classification items a custom property is available for) to each custom property. Default is true.

properties.description: Returns only the definitions of these properties. Identifiers not found in the project are left out of the response. All properties are returned when omitted.

propertyTypes.description: Returns only the properties of these types. All types are returned when omitted.

propertyGroups.description: Every property group, including empty ones.

GetAnalyticalLinks.description: Retrieves the settings, the connected member parts and the geometry of the given analytical links. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalLinks.name: GetAnalyticalLinks

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model the geometry is read from. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

links.description: The link and its geometry for each element, in the order of the input. An element that is not an analytical link, or whose link cannot be got, is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalLoadCases.description: Retrieves the structural analysis load cases of the given load group, or of the project when no load group is given, with all their fields.
GetAnalyticalLoadCases.name: GetAnalyticalLoadCases

loadGroupId.description: The identifier of the load group to list the load cases of. Every load case of the project is listed when it is omitted.

loadCases.description: The load cases. A load case that cannot be read is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalLoadCombinations.description: Retrieves the structural analysis load combinations of the project with all their fields and load factors.
GetAnalyticalLoadCombinations.name: GetAnalyticalLoadCombinations

loadCombinations.description: The load combinations of the project. A load combination that cannot be read is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalLoadGroups.description: Retrieves the structural analysis load groups of the project with all their fields.
GetAnalyticalLoadGroups.name: GetAnalyticalLoadGroups

loadGroups.description: The load groups of the project. A load group that cannot be read is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalLoads.description: Retrieves the settings, the loaded member part, the custom data (the curve of an edge load, the contour of a surface load) and the geometry of the given analytical point, edge and surface loads. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalLoads.name: GetAnalyticalLoads

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model the geometry is read from. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

loads.description: The load of each element, in the order of the input, with its geometry in the Structural Analytical Model and, for an edge or a surface load, its custom data (the curve or contour stored with the element). An element that is not an analytical point, edge or surface load, or whose load cannot be got, is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalMemberDetails.description: Retrieves the curve, surface or segmented surface member of the given elements in a Structural Analytical Model, with their connections. Cross sections, curves, nodes and surfaces are returned with every field the Archicad version has.
GetAnalyticalMemberDetails.name: GetAnalyticalMemberDetails

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; before Archicad 27 it is required.

segmentationCentralAngle.description: When given, surface members are read as segmented surface members (for curved walls), each segment spanning at most this central angle, in radians.

analyticalMembers.description: The analytical member of each element, in the order of the input. An element that is no member of the model, or whose member cannot be read, is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalMemberPartGeometries.description: Retrieves the node of the given analytical member vertices and the curve of the given member edges. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalMemberPartGeometries.name: GetAnalyticalMemberPartGeometries

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

memberPartRefs.description: The member parts to get the geometry of: vertices (BegVertex, EndVertex, CustomVertex) give a node, edges (Edge, RatioEdge, CustomEdge) a curve.

geometries.description: The node or curve of each member part, in the order of the input. A member part the geometry cannot be got for, a surface among them, is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalMemberTypesOfElements.description: Retrieves the analytical member type (Beam, Column, Roof, Slab, Wall or Unknown) of the given elements.
GetAnalyticalMemberTypesOfElements.name: GetAnalyticalMemberTypesOfElements

memberTypesOfElements.description: The analytical member type of each element, in the order of the input. An element the type cannot be got for is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalMembers.description: Lists the elements of the curve and surface members of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given (the model is required before Archicad 27).
GetAnalyticalMembers.name: GetAnalyticalMembers

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; before Archicad 27 it is required.

curveMembers.description: The elements of the curve members (beams, columns) of the model.

surfaceMembers.description: The elements of the surface members (walls, slabs, roofs) of the model.

GetAnalyticalModel.description: Retrieves the Structural Analytical Model of the given variation, as returned by GetAnalyticalModelVariation.
GetAnalyticalModel.name: GetAnalyticalModel

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model of the variation.

GetAnalyticalModelCheckTypeId.description: Retrieves the type identifier of the Structural Analytical Model check. Available from Archicad 29.
GetAnalyticalModelCheckTypeId.name: GetAnalyticalModelCheckTypeId

modelCheckTypeId.description: The type identifier of the Structural Analytical Model check.

GetAnalyticalModelVariation.description: Retrieves the variation of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given (the model is required before Archicad 27). The fields of the variation depend on the Archicad version.
GetAnalyticalModelVariation.name: GetAnalyticalModelVariation

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; before Archicad 27 it is required.

GetAnalyticalReleases.description: Retrieves the releases of the given analytical members. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalReleases.name: GetAnalyticalReleases

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

releases.description: The release of each element, in the order of the input. An element the release cannot be got for is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalSupports.description: Retrieves the settings, the supported member part and the geometry of the given analytical supports. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalSupports.name: GetAnalyticalSupports

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model the geometry is read from. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

supports.description: The support and its geometry for each element, in the order of the input. An element that is not an analytical support, or whose support cannot be got, is represented by an error object.

GetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings.description: Retrieves the visibility settings of the Structural Analytical Model. Available from Archicad 26.
GetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings.name: GetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings

visibilitySettings.description: The Structural Analytical Model visibility settings, with every field.

GetArcFromUser.description: Asks the designer to draw an arc in the current window - its center, its start point (which sets the radius) and its end point - with a rubber-band circle shown while drawing, and returns its center, radius, start and end angles, the angle it turns through, its direction and its start and end points. Archicad waits for the clicks or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.
GetArcFromUser.name: GetArcFromUser

centerPrompt.default: Click the center of the arc
centerPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the center of the arc. Single-byte text: the control box takes a char field.

constraint.description: Constrains every click: the center, the start point and the end point. With fromLastPoint the start point is measured from the center (type Distance fixes the radius, type Angle the direction of the start point) and the end point from the start point. Default: no constraint.

endPrompt.default: Click the end point of the arc
endPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the end point of the arc. Archicad draws the arc while the cursor moves; the direction the cursor goes around the center decides whether the arc is clockwise.

showRubberArcFeedback.description: If true, also draws the whole circle of the arc while the start and end points are chosen: its radius follows the cursor until the start point is clicked. Drawn in 2D windows only; the 3D window shows Archicad's default feedback.

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to for the center and the start point. Archicad's arc input has no snap filter, so the end point snaps as usual. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the arc
startPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the start point of the arc, which also sets its radius.

arcAngle.description: The angle the arc turns through from its start to its end, in radians: positive (up to 2*pi) for a counterclockwise arc, negative (down to -2*pi) for a clockwise one.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (Escape); no other field is returned then.

clockwise.description: True if the arc was drawn clockwise from its start to its end.

endAngle.description: The direction of the end point from the center, in radians from the x axis, counterclockwise, between -pi and pi.

endPoint.description: The end point of the arc: the point of its circle in the direction of the third click (its z is the clicked z).

radius.description: The radius of the arc: the distance of the start point from the center in the x-y plane.

startAngle.description: The direction of the start point from the center, in radians from the x axis, counterclockwise, between -pi and pi.

startPoint.description: The start point of the arc, as clicked.

GetArchicadLicenseInfo.description: Retrieves the license the running Archicad runs on: its type (Full, Education, Trial, Demo, Start or BIMcloud Team Client), the raw protection mode with its bits by name, and the highest Software Service Agreement (SSA) level of the license, so a script can warn before it uses a feature the license lacks. The SSA level is not available in Archicad 25.
GetArchicadLicenseInfo.name: GetArchicadLicenseInfo

licenseFlags.description: The bits set in protectionMode, by name: Site (more licenses), NotForResale, School, PayPerUse, Network (network licensing), Teamwork (Teamwork functionality is on), Education (education key), Start (Start edition), Solo (SOLO edition), LiveSubscription, OEM (Archicad 27 or later), SSA (SSA license, Archicad 25 only), and without a hardware or software key EducationWithoutKey, Demo, Trial and BIMcloudTeamClient.

licenseType.description: The kind of license Archicad runs on, read from protectionMode: Trial, Demo, Education (an education license with or without a key), BIMcloudTeamClient, Start (the Start edition), otherwise Full.

protectionMode.description: The raw protection mode bit mask reported by Archicad (the APIPROT_*_MASK bits of the Archicad API).

ssaLevel.description: The highest Software Service Agreement (SSA) level the license has: NoSSA, SSA or Forward. A script needing a level checks that this is at least that level, in this order. Missing in Archicad 25, which cannot report it.

GetArchicadLocation.description: Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.
GetArchicadLocation.name: GetArchicadLocation

archicadLocation.description: The location of the Archicad executable in the filesystem.

GetArchicadReleaseInfo.description: Retrieves the main version, release version and build number of the running Archicad, with the caption of its window.
GetArchicadReleaseInfo.name: GetArchicadReleaseInfo

buildNumber.description: The build number of the running Archicad.

caption.description: The caption of the Archicad application window. Missing when Archicad does not report it.

mainVersion.description: The main version of the running Archicad, e.g. 29.

releaseVersion.description: The release (update) version of the running Archicad.

GetArchicadVisibility.description: Returns whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden. Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
GetArchicadVisibility.name: GetArchicadVisibility

isVisible.description: True when the Archicad application is shown, false when it is hidden.

GetAttributeIndexes.description: Reports for each given attribute type how many attributes there are, the first valid and the highest index in use, and the free indexes between them (for example those of deleted attributes). Available from Archicad 27.
GetAttributeIndexes.name: GetAttributeIndexes

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to report the indexes of.

attributeIndexes.description: One item per requested attribute type, in the order of attributeTypes.

count.description: The number of attributes of the type.

firstIndex.description: The index of the first valid attribute of the type, as Archicad reports it. Left out when the type has no attribute.

freeIndexes.description: The indexes between firstIndex and lastIndex that no attribute uses, for example those of deleted attributes, in ascending order. Archicad 29 gives a new Layer the lowest free index.

lastIndex.description: The highest index in use. Left out when the type has no attribute.

GetAttributesByType.description: Returns the details of every attribute of the given type, including the path of the attribute folder holding it (Archicad 26 and newer). From Archicad 30 an attribute that Archicad keeps a creation record of also carries creationInfo: how (method), from where (source), by whom and when it was created.
GetAttributesByType.name: GetAttributesByType

GetAttributesFromProject.description: Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Archicad does not read Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem attributes from a file that is not open: these types get an error item instead of an empty list. Available from Archicad 27.
GetAttributesFromProject.name: GetAttributesFromProject

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to read. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem cannot be read from a file that is not open; they get an error item.

projectFilePath.description: The absolute path of the project or template file (for example .pln or .tpl) to read the attributes from.

GetAutoGroupMode.description: Gets the current state of the Auto Group mode.
GetAutoGroupMode.name: GetAutoGroupMode

autoGroup.description: True if the Auto Group mode is currently on.

GetAutoIntersect.description: Gets whether Auto-Intersection (Options > Auto-Intersection) is on. It changes what the wall and beam creation commands produce: with it on, the new elements are joined at their intersections.
GetAutoIntersect.name: GetAutoIntersect

isOn.description: True if Auto-Intersection is currently on.

GetAutoTextKeys.description: Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.
GetAutoTextKeys.name: GetAutoTextKeys
