editable.description: Whether the default value of the property definition can be modified.

GetPropertyExpressionReferences.description: Returns the strings that refer to the given properties in property expressions.
GetPropertyExpressionReferences.name: GetPropertyExpressionReferences

references.description: One item for each property, in the order of the input: its expression reference, or an error.

reference.description: The string that refers to the property in a property expression.

GetPropertyObjectsOfElements.description: Gets the property objects of the given elements: the library parts of the old listing system (used by projects migrated from older Archicad versions) linked to each element by criteria or individually, with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetPropertyObjectsOfElements.name: GetPropertyObjectsOfElements

propertyObjectsOfElements.description: The property objects of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes.description: Returns the property values of the attributes for the given property. With includeStatus it also returns whether each property is available, editable and visible for the attribute (from 1.7.3).
GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes.name: GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes

includeStatus.description: If true, each item also tells whether the property is available, editable and visible for the attribute, and a property without an available value is returned with its status and without a value instead of as an error. The default is false.

propertyValuesForAttributes.description: The order of the outer list is that of the given attributes. The order of the inner lists are that of the given properties.

GetPropertyValuesOfElementComponents.description: Returns the property values of the given element components for the given properties, in the shape of GetPropertyValuesOfElements. Use GetComponentsOfElements to list the components of an element.
GetPropertyValuesOfElementComponents.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElementComponents

propertyValuesForElementComponents.description: The order of the outer list is that of the given element components. The order of the inner lists are that of the given properties. The items have the shape of GetPropertyValuesOfElements.

GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults.description: Returns the values of the given properties in the current tool default of an element type, which new elements of that type get. It reads the native tool default of the generic variation of the type, not a Favorite that is not applied. A property that is not available for the tool default is reported as an error.
GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults

elementType.description: The element type whose current tool default is read. This is the native tool default of the generic variation of the type, a Favorite counts only after it was applied.

propertyValues.description: The order is that of the given properties. A property that is not available for the tool default is an error item.

GetPropertyValuesOfElements.description: Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element.
GetPropertyValuesOfElements.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElements

includeAvailability.description: Adds isAvailable to each property value or error, telling whether the property is available for the element (for example by its classification). Default is false.

useSIUnits.description: Returns precise, locale-independent numeric strings in SI units, except degrees for angles. Default is false.

propertyValuesForElements.description: The order of the outer list is that of the given elements. The order of the inner lists are that of the given properties.

GetPublisherSets.description: Returns the publisher sets of the project with their saved output: the local or LAN path, the Teamwork file server path, or the Internet host and directory name.
GetPublisherSets.name: GetPublisherSets

publisherSets.description: The publisher sets of the project, in the order of the Publisher Sets map.

dirName.description: The saved directory name on the host, when the set is published to the Internet.

host.description: The saved host name, when the set is published to the Internet.

name.description: The name of the publisher set.

path.description: The saved local or LAN output path, when the set is published to files. When it is also uploaded to a Teamwork file server, this is the temporary local path.

rootNavigatorItemId.description: The navigator item ID of the root of the publisher set.

twFileServerPath.description: The saved output path on the Teamwork file server, when the set is published to files onto a file server.

GetQuantitiesOfElements.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call.
GetQuantitiesOfElements.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements

calculateInOneCall.description: Optional. When true, Archicad calculates the quantities of all the supported elements in one call instead of one call per element, which can be faster for many elements. The output has the same format. If that one call fails, every supported element gets the same error. Default value is false.

minOpeningSize.description: Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted when the conditional values (for example volumeConditional of a Wall) are calculated. Archicad only uses it for walls. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.

quantitiesOfElements.description: The quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Lengths are in meters, areas in square meters and volumes in cubic meters.

GetRelationsOfElements.description: Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26.
GetRelationsOfElements.name: GetRelationsOfElements

otherElementType.description: Optional filter: only relations to elements of this type are returned.

relations.description: Type-specific relations of each element, aligned with the input.

GetRenderingScenes.description: Gets the names of the rendering scenes of the project (the Scene list of the PhotoRendering Settings palette), the most recently used first, and the name of the current scene.
GetRenderingScenes.name: GetRenderingScenes

currentSceneName.description: The name of the current rendering scene, the one selected in the PhotoRendering Settings palette: the first of sceneNames. Left out when the project has no rendering scene.

sceneNames.description: The names of the rendering scenes of the project (the Scene list of the PhotoRendering Settings palette), in the order of recent usage: the most recently used scene, the current one, first.

GetRenovationFilters.description: Gets the renovation filters of the project, and the one the current window uses (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter). A renovationFilterId has the same shape as the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings, so a filter listed here can be set on saved views too.
GetRenovationFilters.name: GetRenovationFilters

activeRenovationFilterId.description: Identifier of the renovation filter of the current window. Absent when the current window has none or it could not be read.

renovationFilters.description: Every renovation filter of the project.

GetRenovationStatusNames.description: Gets the names the running Archicad shows for the renovation statuses Existing, New and Demolished (localized). Available from Archicad 27.
GetRenovationStatusNames.name: GetRenovationStatusNames

renovationStatuses.description: The renovation statuses an element can have, in the order Existing, New, Demolished.

GetReservationStatusOfElements.description: Returns the Teamwork reservation status of elements without reserving them: whether each element is free, reserved by the current user or reserved by another user, with the reserving user. New elements stay reserved by the user who created them until they are released.
GetReservationStatusOfElements.name: GetReservationStatusOfElements

reservationStatuses.description: One item per input element, in the same order.

GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme.description: Retrieves the custom fields of changes (the change custom scheme): the key and the name of each field. The keys are the customSchemeKey values in the customSchemeData of changes.
GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme.name: GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme

GetRevisionChangesOfElements.description: Retrieves the changes belong to the given elements.
GetRevisionChangesOfElements.name: GetRevisionChangesOfElements

customScheme.description: The custom scheme fields of the revision issues (key and name). Present only when the project defines any.

GetRoofPlanes.description: Gets the single planes of roofs, without changing the roofs. A multi-plane roof is decomposed by Archicad into its planes, each returned with its part identifier and its details as a single-plane roof (slope, pivot line, level, outline with arcs and holes); a single-plane roof is returned as its only plane. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetRoofPlanes.name: GetRoofPlanes

roofPlanesOfElements.description: The planes of each roof, aligned with the input, or an error.

planes.description: The single planes of the roof: the planes Archicad decomposes a multi-plane roof into, or the roof itself for a single-plane roof.

details.description: The plane as a single-plane roof: slope, pivot line, level and outline.

partId.description: Archicad's identifier of the plane within the multi-plane roof (API_ElemPartId). Missing for a single-plane roof.

main.description: The main part of Archicad's identifier of the plane (API_ElemPartId main).

sub.description: The sub part of Archicad's identifier of the plane (API_ElemPartId sub).

GetRoomImage.description: Returns the room image of the given zone.
GetRoomImage.name: GetRoomImage

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the generated image. Default is white (1.0, 1.0, 1.0).

format.description: The image format. Default is png.

height.description: The height of the preview image in pixels. Default is 256.

offset.description: Offset of the clip polygon from the edge of the zone. Default is 0.001.

scale.description: Scale of the view (e.g. 0.005 for 1:200). Default is 0.005.

width.description: The width of the preview image in pixels. Default is 256.

GetSchedules.description: Returns the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map: navigator item id, name, ID and the folders they are in. Archicad's API does not give the rows of a schedule nor export it; to export one, put it in a publisher set with a spreadsheet format in Archicad and run PublishPublisherSet.
GetSchedules.name: GetSchedules

schedules.description: The Interactive Schedules of the Project Map, in navigator order.

folderPath.description: The names of the Project Map items the schedule is in, from the top down, without the project itself (e.g. Schedules, Element). Archicad's API does not say whether a schedule lists elements, components or surfaces; the default Project Map shows it by these folders.

name.description: The name of the schedule.

uiId.description: The ID of the schedule, shown before its name in the navigator.

GetScriptUIResult.description: Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from a Script UI window's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the window is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it. The window is picked by uiId or scriptId; without them the first window is used.
GetScriptUIResult.name: GetScriptUIResult

scriptId.description: Any text that identifies the calling script, so it uses its own window: ShowScriptUI gives a script without a window a free one, preferring the closed windows. The Tapir palette gives each script it starts its own id in the TAPIR_SCRIPT_ID environment variable, which aclib passes here automatically; that script's window is titled with its name and is freed when it ends. Without uiId and scriptId the first window is used.

uiId.description: The window to use, as returned by ShowScriptUI (1 to 8). Takes precedence over scriptId.

hasResult.description: True if the Script UI page has submitted a result since the last call.

isOpen.description: True while the Script UI palette is open. False before the first ShowScriptUI call and once the user closed the palette with its close box, the page called window.ACAPI.ClosePalette or Archicad closed it; stays true while Archicad only temporarily hides all palettes (e.g. during a modal dialog). Lets a waiting script stop polling when the user closes the palette.

result.description: The submitted content (as passed to window.ACAPI.SubmitResult). Only present when hasResult is true.

uiId.description: The window the result was read from (1 to 8). Missing when scriptId was given and that script has no window.

GetSectionElements.description: Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.
GetSectionElements.name: GetSectionElements

databases.description: The section, elevation or interior elevation databases to list the section elements of. If omitted, the current database is used.

sectionElements.description: The elements drawn in the given databases, each with the owner element it was generated from.

ownerElementId.description: The identifier of the owner element the section element was generated from - this is what every other listing command returns.

ownerElementType.description: The type of the owner element. Only present when the owner's header is readable from the section database.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of the section element itself, accepted by CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection as sectionElementId.

GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails.description: Gets every configurable setting of the given Section and Elevation elements, with their name and reference ID.
GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails.name: GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails

GetSelectedElements.description: Gets the list of the currently selected elements.
GetSelectedElements.name: GetSelectedElements

GetShapePrimitivesOfElements.description: Returns the 2D drawing primitives of each given floor plan element in the same format as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements, but drawn as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrims draws it by default (on the current story, clipped as Archicad clips it) instead of on every story and unclipped. With includeMarkers the objects attached to the elements (window and door markers, drawing titles, ...) are drawn with them or left out; Archicad's setting is changed back afterwards. An element on another story gets an error item. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetShapePrimitivesOfElements.name: GetShapePrimitivesOfElements

includeMarkers.description: Whether the objects attached to the elements (window and door markers, drawing titles, ...) are drawn with them. When omitted, Archicad's current setting is used. The setting is changed back after the drawing.

shapePrimitivesOfElements.description: The drawing primitives of each element, in the order of the input elements.

GetSkylightHolePolygons.description: Gets the polygon of the hole each given Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell: the outline and any holes of it as 2D coordinates. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element that is not a Skylight gets an error item.
GetSkylightHolePolygons.name: GetSkylightHolePolygons

skylightHolePolygons.description: The hole each Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell, aligned with the input: its polygon, or an error (for example for an element that is not a Skylight).

GetSnapPointsOfElements.description: Gets the snap points (hotspots) of the given elements, of any element type: the points of an element that the cursor snaps to and dimensions attach to (for example the endpoints of a Wall's reference line or the vertices of a Slab), in world coordinates, each with the neig kind and subindex identifying which point of the element it is. For the 2D hotspots of library part instances see GetHotspotsOfElements. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetSnapPointsOfElements.name: GetSnapPointsOfElements

snapPointsOfElements.description: The snap points (hotspots) of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

snapPoints.description: The snap points (hotspots) of the element: the points Archicad snaps to and dimensions attach to, in world coordinates (meters, absolute Z). Empty when the element has none.

inIndex.description: Subindex of the point within its kind (API_Neig inIndex), for example the vertex index in the element's polygon.

neigId.description: Which kind of point of the element the hotspot is, as the DevKit's API_NeigID enumerator value of its neig (for example the begin or end point of a Wall's reference line, or a vertex of a Slab's polygon).

GetSolidElementLinks.description: Returns solid element operation links for each queried element, grouped by role (target or operator).
GetSolidElementLinks.name: GetSolidElementLinks

elements.description: Elements to query. Returns all solid links where each element is a target or an operator.

solidLinks.description: For each input element, the solid links where it acts as target and where it acts as operator.

GetSpecialFolders.description: Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.).
GetSpecialFolders.name: GetSpecialFolders

folderTypes.description: The types of the special folders to retrieve.

GetSplineMaxDistances.description: Measures how far the given 2D coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element, between two of its fit points, with its own Bezier handles: returns the largest distance, for example to check how well a polyline follows the spline. The output is aligned with the input array. Changes nothing in the project.
GetSplineMaxDistances.name: GetSplineMaxDistances

splines.description: The spline segments to measure and the coordinates to measure from them.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates to measure from the segment.

elementId.description: A Spline element.

segmentIndex.description: The segment of the spline between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1, from 0 to the number of fit points - 2 (the fit points are the coordinates GetDetailsOfElements returns for the spline).

results.description: The result of each input item, in the same order, or an error.

maxDistance.description: The largest distance of the given coordinates from the spline segment.

GetStories.description: Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.
GetStories.name: GetStories

skipNullFloor.description: Floor indices above ground-floor level may start with 1 instead of 0.

GetStoryControlPrimitives.description: Returns the 2D drawing primitives of the story levels (story lines and their markers) drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation database, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_DrawStoryControl draws them, in the same format as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements. The databaseId can be obtained with GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId.
GetStoryControlPrimitives.name: GetStoryControlPrimitives

databaseId.description: A section, elevation or interior elevation database, for example as GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId returns it.

primitives.description: The primitives of the story levels drawn in the database, in the order Archicad draws them. The Ctrl_* items mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts (texts, ...).

GetStructureDisplay.description: Gets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, and whether it is the 3D window. This is the setting of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 27.
GetStructureDisplay.name: GetStructureDisplay

returns.description: The Partial Structure Display of the current window.

is3D.description: True when the setting belongs to the 3D window.

GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements.description: Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements.
GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements.name: GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements

items.description: Subelements grouped by type.

externalSubelements.description: The subelements of an external hierarchical element (for example an MEP element or an element of another add-on). Available from Archicad 28.

GetSunSettings.description: Gets the project's date and time (Options > Project Preferences > Location Settings), the sun position Archicad calculates for them at the project location, and the sun and ambient light settings.
GetSunSettings.name: GetSunSettings

sunLight.description: The sun and ambient light settings of the project. Missing when Archicad cannot report them.

ambientIntensity.description: The intensity of the ambient light in percent.

sunIntensity.description: The intensity of the sun light in percent.

sunPosition.description: The sun position for the project's date, time and location.

timeZoneInMinutes.description: The time zone of the project location in minutes, as Archicad stores it.

timeZoneOffset.description: The time zone offset of the project location in minutes, as Archicad stores it.

GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.description: Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.name: GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements

coverElements.description: Optional covering elements: the area where one of them overlaps a surface of an element is subtracted from that surface, so for example a slab on a wall takes its footprint off the top surface of the wall. When omitted, every Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Stair and Curtain Wall of the project is a covering element. Pass an empty array to get the whole surfaces with nothing subtracted. An element never covers itself.

elements.description: The elements to get the surface quantities of.

surfaceQuantitiesOfElements.description: The surface quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Areas are in square meters.

GetSurfaceTypesOfElements.description: Gets the surface type of every polygon of the 3D model of the given elements, as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it: for each element its polygons with their body index, polygon index, polygon id and the numeric API_SurfaceTypeID value. The model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.
GetSurfaceTypesOfElements.name: GetSurfaceTypesOfElements

surfaceTypes.description: The polygons of the 3D model of each element with their surface types, aligned with the input, or an error.

polygons.description: Every polygon of every body of the element's 3D model, generated with separate components. Empty when the element has no 3D model.

bodyIndex.description: The index of the body in the element, starting from 0.

polygonId.description: The identifier of the polygon in the 3D model (ModelerAPI::Polygon::GetPolygonId).

polygonIndex.description: The index of the polygon in the body, starting from 0.

surfaceType.description: The surface type of the polygon: the numeric value of API_SurfaceTypeID as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it.

GetSurfaces.description: Returns the details of the given Surface attributes.
GetSurfaces.name: GetSurfaces

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Surface. If omitted, every field is returned.

surfaces.description: A list of surfaces or errors.

GetSurveyPointTransformation.description: Gets the 3x4 matrix that transforms points from the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row, and its inverse when it is invertible. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.
GetSurveyPointTransformation.name: GetSurveyPointTransformation

projectToSurvey.description: The 3x4 matrix that transforms a point given in the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row (12 numbers): x' = m[0]*x + m[1]*y + m[2]*z + m[3], y' = m[4]*x + m[5]*y + m[6]*z + m[7], z' = m[8]*x + m[9]*y + m[10]*z + m[11].

surveyToProject.description: The inverse of projectToSurvey in the same row by row layout: it transforms a point given in the Survey Point coordinate system into the Project Origin coordinate system. Missing when projectToSurvey is not invertible.

GetSuspendGroupsMode.description: Gets the current state of the Suspend Groups mode.
GetSuspendGroupsMode.name: GetSuspendGroupsMode

suspendGroups.description: True if the Suspend Groups mode is currently on.

GetTeamworkAccessRights.description: Returns whether the role of the current user has the given Teamwork access rights (API_TWAccessRights names without the API prefix, e.g. LayersCreate), all of them when no names are given.
GetTeamworkAccessRights.name: GetTeamworkAccessRights

accessRights.description: The names of the access rights to check, the API_TWAccessRights enumerators without the API prefix, e.g. LayersCreate or LibraryPartDeleteModify. All rights available in this Archicad version are checked when omitted.
The rights of the current user, in the requested order.

hasRight.description: Whether the role of the current user has this right.

GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases.description: Returns the Teamwork owner (user id and name) of each given database, e.g. of a layout or a view database. The user id is 0 when nobody owns the database.
GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases.name: GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases

owners.description: The Teamwork owner of each given database, in the order of the input. userId is 0 when nobody owns the database.

GetTeamworkProjectInfo.description: Tells whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and whether it is online, and returns its BIMcloud server, project name and the current user (id and name).
GetTeamworkProjectInfo.name: GetTeamworkProjectInfo

isOnline.description: True, if the Teamwork project is connected to its BIMcloud server. False in a solo project or when the Teamwork project works offline.

isTeamwork.description: True, if the opened project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project. When false, every other Teamwork field is left out.

projectName.description: The name of the Teamwork project on the server.

serverUrl.description: The address of the BIMcloud server of the Teamwork project.

userId.description: The Teamwork user identifier of the current user, as the Teamwork commands report users.

userName.description: The name of the current Teamwork user.

GetTeamworkRightsOfObjects.description: Returns for each given object, for example an element, whether the current Teamwork user has the right to create objects of its kind and to delete or modify it.
GetTeamworkRightsOfObjects.name: GetTeamworkRightsOfObjects

objectIds.description: The objects to check, by guid, for example element guids.

rights.description: One item per input object, in the same order.

canCreate.description: Whether the current user has the right to create objects of this kind.

canDeleteModify.description: Whether the current user has the right to delete or modify the object.

GetTeamworkStatus.description: Returns whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and is online, the members of the shared project and who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Works in a solo project too, then isShared and isOnline are false.
GetTeamworkStatus.name: GetTeamworkStatus

hotlinkCacheManagementOwner.description: The user who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Only present when somebody has reserved it.

isOnline.description: Whether there is a live connection to the Teamwork server. Always false for a project that is not shared.

isShared.description: Whether the opened project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project.

users.description: The members of the shared project. Only present when the project is shared.

GetTextureCoordinates.description: Gets the texture coordinates (u, v) of the faces of the 3D model of the given elements: per solid body, per face, at the first vertex of the face. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetTextureCoordinates.name: GetTextureCoordinates

textureCoordinates.description: The texture coordinates of each element, aligned with the input: per solid body of its 3D model, or an error.

GetToolboxItems.description: Lists the tools of the Toolbox, the tools of add-ons included, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts, and the active tool. includeHidden also lists the tools without an icon, e.g. the Slab Accessory.
GetToolboxItems.name: GetToolboxItems

includeHidden.description: Also list the tools that have no icon in the Toolbox but can be active, e.g. the Slab Accessory. Default: false.

currentTool.description: The tool active in the Toolbox, as GetCurrentTool returns it. Empty for the Arrow and the Marquee.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

toolboxItems.description: The tools installed in the Toolbox, the tools of add-ons included, each in the form SetCurrentTool accepts.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

GetURLReferencesOfElements.description: Gets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.
GetURLReferencesOfElements.name: GetURLReferencesOfElements

urlReferences.description: The web link of each given element, or an error. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.

oneOf.description: The web link of an element.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com.

oneOf.title: URLReference

GetUnusedAttributes.description: Lists the unused layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories (index, id and name), for the given types or all of them. The Archicad API has no function that tells which attributes are unused (only how many per type), so every reference is collected: the elements of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too), with their library part parameters and memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules, the way ReindexAttributes finds them; for layers the layer of each element, tool default and Favorite; for composites and profiles the walls, slabs, roofs, shells, column and beam segments whose structure type uses them; for pen tables the current pen table and the drawings set to a pen table of their own. An attribute that only an unused attribute refers to counts as used. Indices typed into GDL scripts and the pen tables saved with views are not found. Each type also reports Archicad's own count of the attributes in use (archicadUsedCount, see GetUsedAttributes), so a difference shows. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.
GetUnusedAttributes.name: GetUnusedAttributes

types.description: The attribute types to check. All of them when omitted.

archicadReport.description: Archicad's usedAttributes report as it came, e.g. 'Layer: 16, LineType: 9, Fill: 17'. Missing when the query failed.

attributeTypes.description: One item per checked attribute type, in the order layer, fill, surface, buildingMaterial, composite, profile, lineType, penTable, zoneCategory.

archicadUsedCount.description: The number of attributes of this type in use as Archicad itself counts them, from the usedAttributes JSON query (see GetUsedAttributes). When it differs from usedCount, Archicad counts references this command does not see, or the other way round, so check the list before deleting. Missing when Archicad's report does not name the type.

attributeCount.description: The number of attributes of this type in the project.

unusedAttributes.description: The attributes of this type that no reference found by the command points at.

warnings.description: What could not be checked. Missing when everything was checked.

GetUnusedLibraryParts.description: Lists the loaded library parts that no element of the project is placed from. Read only. The Archicad API does not tell which library parts are used, so every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout is checked: objects, lamps, doors, windows, skylights, zone stamps, symbol labels, drawing titles, curtain wall parts, and the markers of doors, windows, skylights, sections, elevations, details and worksheets. A library part used only in another way (called as a macro, linked as a property object, as an interior elevation marker, in stairs and railings, in the tool defaults or in Favorites) is listed as unused. Library parts that cannot be placed (e.g. macros) are only listed with includeNotPlaceable.
GetUnusedLibraryParts.name: GetUnusedLibraryParts

filterByTypeId.description: Optional. Only list the unused library parts of this type (the typeId of GetAvailableLibraryParts).

includeNotPlaceable.description: Also list the library parts that cannot be placed (macros, pictures, property objects, list schemes and the like), which are never placed on their own. Default: false.

complete.description: False when a view or layout database or a library part could not be read (see warnings): then a listed library part may still be used.

scannedElementCount.description: The number of elements checked, in the floor plan and every view and layout database.

unusedLibraryParts.description: The loaded library parts that no element of the project is placed from, in index order.

usedLibraryPartCount.description: The number of different loaded library parts that are placed in the project.

GetUsedAttributes.description: Gets how many attributes of each type are in use (layers, lines, fills, composites, surfaces, ...), as Archicad reports them for the usedAttributes JSON query: the counts in usedAttributes, the report as text in raw. Available from Archicad 27.
GetUsedAttributes.name: GetUsedAttributes

returns.description: How many attributes of each type are in use, as Archicad reports them for the usedAttributes JSON query.

raw.description: The report as Archicad wrote it, e.g. 'Layer: 16, LineType: 9, Fill: 17'.

usedAttributes.description: The number of attributes in use per attribute type. The keys are the attribute types of Tapir (Layer, Line, Fill, Composite, Surface, LayerCombination, ZoneCategory, Profile, MEPSystem, OperationProfile, BuildingMaterial) where they exist, otherwise Archicad's own names (e.g. City, DimStand, MarkupStyle, GraphicOverride). Archicad lists only the types it found in use. Missing when the report could not be read.

GetUserDataOfAttributes.description: Reads the key-value pairs stored on attributes by SetUserDataOfAttributes. An attribute without user data returns no pairs; one holding user data in another layout returns an error.
GetUserDataOfAttributes.name: GetUserDataOfAttributes

userDataOfAttributes.description: One item per attribute, in the input order: the pairs stored on the attribute (none when it holds no user data), or an error when the attribute was not found or holds user data in another layout.

GetUserDataOfGroups.description: Gets the user data an add-on attached to each given group: its version, platform sign, flags and bytes (base64 encoded), and, when its version is 1 (the layout SetUserDataOfGroups writes), its key-value pairs. Returns an error for groups that have no user data.
GetUserDataOfGroups.name: GetUserDataOfGroups

groups.description: The groups to get the user data of.

userDataOfGroups.description: The user data attached to each given group, or an error for groups that have none.

userData.description: The user data an add-on attached to the group.

data.description: The bytes of the user data, base64 encoded. Empty when the user data has no bytes.

dataVersion.description: The version of the user data, as set by the add-on that attached it.

flags.description: The flags of the user data (APIUserDataFlag_FillWith and APIUserDataFlag_Pickup bits), as set by the add-on that attached it.

pairs.description: The key-value pairs of the user data, decoded from data. Only present when dataVersion is 1, the layout SetUserDataOfGroups writes.

platformSign.description: The platform sign of the user data, which tells the byte order the data was written in.

GetUserGSID.description: Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
GetUserGSID.name: GetUserGSID

organizationIds.description: The list of organization IDs the user belongs to. Empty if not part of any organization or if the information cannot be retrieved.

userId.description: The stable GSID User ID of the logged-in user.

GetView2DTransformations.description: Get zoom and rotation of 2D views
GetView2DTransformations.name: GetView2DTransformations

GetViewOptions.description: Gets the model view options and on-screen view options of the current plan window, and the index and name of the model view option combination it applies.
GetViewOptions.name: GetViewOptions

modelViewOptionIndex.description: The index of the model view option combination the window applies, 0 when its options are not a stored combination (Custom). It is the index FindModelViewOption and GetModelViewOptionDetails return, which is not always the position in the list of GetModelViewOptions.

modelViewOptionName.description: The name of that combination, empty when there is none. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by this name (FindModelViewOption) before switching back to it with SetViewOptions.

GetViewSettings.description: Gets the view settings of navigator items
GetViewSettings.name: GetViewSettings

GetVisibleSkinStatus.description: Checks whether elements have a visible skin in a given Partial Structure Display mode (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly), e.g. a finish-only slab has none in CoreOnly. The current window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetVisibleSkinStatus.name: GetVisibleSkinStatus

structureDisplay.description: The Partial Structure Display mode to check the elements in. The current window is not changed.

visibleSkinStatuses.description: Whether each element has a visible skin in the given Partial Structure Display mode, aligned with the input, or an error.

GetZoneBoundaries.description: Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.
GetZoneBoundaries.name: GetZoneBoundaries

zoneElementId.description: The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.

zones.description: A list of Zones. Only one of zoneElementId and zones can be given.

GetZoneCategories.description: Returns the details of the given Zone Category attributes.
GetZoneCategories.name: GetZoneCategories

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Zone Category. If omitted, every field is returned.

zoneCategories.description: A list of zone categories or errors.

GetZoneLabelingSettings.description: Returns whether the automatic labeling of Zones is on and the name of the Label Favorite it places. Available from Archicad 28.
GetZoneLabelingSettings.name: GetZoneLabelingSettings

isAutomaticLabelingOn.description: Whether the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) is on.

selectedFavoriteName.description: The name of the Label Favorite that is placed on each new Zone. Missing when no Favorite is selected.

GetZoneReductions.description: Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.
GetZoneReductions.name: GetZoneReductions

elements.description: A list of Zones.

reductionsOfZones.description: The area reductions of each Zone, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

GrantElements.description: Hands over the reservation of elements to another Teamwork user, given by user id, without a dialog. Available from Archicad 27.
GrantElements.name: GrantElements

userId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user to hand the elements over to, as GetTeamworkProjectInfo, GetReservationStatusOfElements and the conflicts of ReserveElements report users.

GrantProjectData.description: Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user.
GrantProjectData.name: GrantProjectData

names.description: The names of the project data, reserved by the current user, to grant.

toUserId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user who gets the project data, for example the userId of a user returned by GetProjectDataKeys or ReserveProjectData.

HighlightElements.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights. On Archicad 25 nonHighlightedColor is ignored.
HighlightElements.name: HighlightElements

highlightedColors.description: A list of colors to highlight elements.

items.description: Color of the highlighted element as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

nonHighlightedColor.description: Optional parameter. Color of the non highlighted elements as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range. Ignored on Archicad 25.

wireframe3D.description: Optional parameter. Switch non highlighted elements in the 3D window to wireframe.

IFCFileOperation.description: Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing file.
IFCFileOperation.name: IFCFileOperation

elementsToExport.description: Only for the save method, and only together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.

fileType.description: The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.

ifcFilePath.description: The target IFC file to use. The save method overwrites an existing file, unless overwrite is false.

method.description: The file operation method to use.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. Only for the save method: false refuses to save when a file already exists at ifcFilePath, and writes nothing.

storyIndex.description: Only for the merge method: the story the first storey of the IFC file is placed on, the IFC's other storeys follow on the stories above it. Without it Archicad uses the active story of the floor plan. The active story and the current window are restored after the merge. See GetStories for the valid story indices.

translatorName.description: Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).

ImportAttributesFromProject.description: Imports Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination attributes from another project or template file into the open project, with their complete definition (symbol and percent fills included), like Append or Overwrite by name in Archicad's Attribute Manager. The lines and fills a composite or profile uses are matched by name; its building materials and surfaces, and the layers of a layer combination, keep their index only with referencesByIndex, since Archicad does not read these types from a closed file. An attribute with a reference that cannot be mapped is not imported. A new attribute gets a new guid: Archicad does not hand out the guids stored in the source file. An attribute whose name already exists is skipped, or overwritten in place with overwriteExisting. dryRun reports what would happen without changing anything. The names are the legacy 8-bit names of the source file. Available from Archicad 27.
ImportAttributesFromProject.name: ImportAttributesFromProject

attributeNames.description: Import only the attributes with these names. All attributes of the given types are imported when it is omitted.

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to import, in this order. Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination can be imported. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem fail with an error item: Archicad does not read them from a closed file. A Composite, Profile or LayerCombination refers to other attributes, see referencesByIndex; list Line and Fill before them to import the lines and fills they use.

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is changed: the response reports what an import would do.

overwriteExisting.description: What happens to an attribute whose name already exists in the open project. false (default): it is skipped and the existing attribute is kept. true: the existing attribute is overwritten with the imported definition and keeps its index and guid.

projectFilePath.description: The absolute path of the project or template file (for example .pln or .tpl) to import the attributes from.

referencesByIndex.description: How the BuildingMaterial, Surface and Layer references of an imported Composite, Profile or LayerCombination are mapped. Archicad does not read these attributes from a closed file, so their names are unknown and they cannot be matched by name. false (default): an attribute with such a reference is not imported (result failed). true: the reference keeps its index and refers to the attribute with that index in the open project, which is right only when both files share these attributes at the same indexes, for example because they come from the same template. Line and Fill references are always matched by name.

attributesByType.description: One item per requested attribute type, in the order of attributeTypes.

attributes.description: One item per imported (or, with dryRun, importable) attribute of the source file.

attributeId.description: The attribute in the open project. Missing when it was not created (failed, or created with dryRun).

name.description: The name of the attribute in the source file.

references.description: For a Composite, Profile or LayerCombination that is created or overwritten (or would be, with dryRun): the attributes it refers to, each once, and how they were mapped to the open project.

attributeId.description: The attribute of the open project referred to after the import. Missing when not mapped, or when it is created by the same dry run.

attributeType.description: The type of the attribute referred to.

mappedBy.description: name: an attribute of the open project with the same name. index: the attribute of the open project with the same index (referencesByIndex). none: not mapped, so the attribute was not imported.

sourceIndex.description: Its index in the source file.

sourceName.description: Its name in the source file. Only for Line and Fill: Archicad does not read the other types from a closed file.

result.description: created: new in the open project. overwritten: an attribute of the same name was overwritten. skipped: an attribute of the same name exists and overwriteExisting is false. failed: see error, for example a reference that cannot be mapped. With dryRun the result is what an import would do.

sourceIndex.description: The index of the attribute in the source file. Archicad hands out a new guid for the attributes of another file on every read, so they are identified by name and index.

ImportClassificationsXml.description: Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed.
ImportClassificationsXml.name: ImportClassificationsXml

xml.description: A Classification Manager export (XML) to import.

ImportFavorites.description: Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew. In a Teamwork project the Favorites lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet).
ImportFavorites.name: ImportFavorites

fileNames.description: Only with the xml format: the names of the Favorite files in the folder to import. Default: every Favorite file of the folder.

importFolders.description: Only with the prefs format: if true and `path` is a folder, the folder structure is preserved.

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: a Favorites file (.prefs) or folder. With the xml format: the folder of Favorite files, as ExportFavorites writes it. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file.

targetFolder.description: Folder hierarchy under which to import. Empty = root. With the xml and legacyPRF formats the folder must exist, and omitting it keeps the folders stored with the Favorites.

firstConflictName.description: Set when conflictPolicy=Error and a name collided; absent otherwise.

ImportIssuesFromBCF.description: Imports issues from the specified BCF file.
ImportIssuesFromBCF.name: ImportIssuesFromBCF

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

importPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name.

ImportMarkupsFromPDF.description: Imports the markups of the specified PDF file as issues, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups, without any dialog and without opening the Issue Manager palette, and reports the issues it created. Available from Archicad 29.
ImportMarkupsFromPDF.name: ImportMarkupsFromPDF

pdfFilePath.description: The os path to the PDF file with the markups, including it's name.

issues.description: The issues the import created. Empty when the import failed.

ImportPropertiesXml.description: Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed.
ImportPropertiesXml.name: ImportPropertiesXml

xml.description: A Property Manager export (XML) to import.

InterpretAutoTexts.description: Resolves one or more autotexts (e.g. '<LAYOUTID>') to their values, optionally in the context of an element, so a key can be tested before it is written into a Text or Label.
InterpretAutoTexts.name: InterpretAutoTexts

autoTexts.description: The autotexts to resolve, either as they are written in the content of a Text or Label element, e.g. '<LAYOUTID>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>', or as bare keys without the surrounding '<' and '>', e.g. 'LAYOUTID'.

elementId.description: Optional. The element in whose context the autotexts are resolved, e.g. a Text on a layout for layout autotexts. When omitted, they are resolved without an element context.

values.description: One result per input autotext, in the same order.

value.description: The resolved value of the autotext.

InterpretGDLScript3D.description: Runs a GDL 3D script, given as text or as the master and 3D scripts of a loaded library part with its default parameters, with the settings of the GDL editor, and returns whether it ran without a GDL error, how many 3D model elements it generated and their bounding box. The API returns no GDL error message or line number.
InterpretGDLScript3D.name: InterpretGDLScript3D

libraryPartName.description: A loaded library part, by its fileName (with extension) or documentName as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns them. Its default parameters are used; without script, its master script followed by its 3D script is run.

script.description: The GDL 3D script to run. Either script or libraryPartName is required.

boundingBox3D.description: The bounding box of the generated 3D model, in the local coordinates of the library part, when it has elements.

elementCount.description: The number of 3D model elements the script generated, when success is true; 0 for a script that generates no 3D model.

error.description: The error code the interpreter returned, when success is false.

success.description: Whether the script ran to its end. False when the GDL interpreter stopped with an error; the API gives no message or line number of the GDL error.

IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf.description: Checks for each of the given library parts whether the given ancestor is anywhere up its subtype hierarchy (e.g. whether a part is a kind of furniture), independent of its name. A library part is not a subtype of itself. With matchAncestorByMainId any revision of the ancestor matches.
IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf.name: IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf

ancestor.description: The subtype to check against. Given by unId, it is used as it is, without checking that such a library part is loaded.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to check.

matchAncestorByMainId.description: Optional, false by default. When true, only the main GUID of the ancestor's unique ID is compared, so any revision of the ancestor matches; when false, the full unique ID (main and revision GUID) must match.

ancestorUnId.description: The full unique ID of the ancestor the library parts were checked against.

results.description: One result for each library part, in the order of the input.

isSubtypeOf.description: True if the ancestor is anywhere up the subtype hierarchy of the library part. False for the ancestor itself: a library part is not a subtype of itself.

unId.description: The full unique ID of the checked library part.

IsUsableGDLString.description: Checks whether each of the given strings is usable in GDL, e.g. before writing it into a GDL parameter or script. Returns one boolean for each string.
IsUsableGDLString.name: IsUsableGDLString

results.description: One item for each given string, in the same order: true if Archicad accepts the string for use in GDL, false otherwise.

LinkElements.description: Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.
LinkElements.name: LinkElements

links.description: The links to create, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

LockElements.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!
LockElements.name: LockElements

MakePropertyAvailableForElements.description: Makes a property definition available for all the given elements. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.
MakePropertyAvailableForElements.name: MakePropertyAvailableForElements

elements.description: The elements to make the property available for.

MakePropertyUnavailableForElements.description: Makes a property definition unavailable for all the given elements. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.
MakePropertyUnavailableForElements.name: MakePropertyUnavailableForElements

elements.description: The elements to make the property unavailable for.

MeasureTexts.description: Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.
MeasureTexts.name: MeasureTexts

texts.description: The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.

fontIndex.description: The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements and GetFontsByName report it in fontIndex. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

fontName.description: Name of the font as Archicad's font list carries it (GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName), which is not always the operating system's font name; GetFontsByName tells whether a name is found. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive, then Archicad's font search as GetFontsByName does, so a family name such as 'Arial' finds 'Arial Western'); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

height.description: The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.

inModelUnits.description: When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

slant.description: The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.

text.description: The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.

measurements.description: One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

MergeElements.description: Merges the given construction elements (the Merge command of Archicad, which cleans up the junctions of slabs, beams, walls and similar elements). Undoable. The element types are not filtered: Archicad reports the ones it cannot merge. The merge is read back: when Archicad records no merge between the given elements (it decides which elements and type combinations it merges), the result is a failure, not a success.
MergeElements.name: MergeElements

elements.description: The construction elements to merge together. At least two.

MirrorElements.description: Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.
MirrorElements.name: MirrorElements

ModelToScreen.description: Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29.
ModelToScreen.name: ModelToScreen

coordinates.description: Model coordinates in the current database (meters). In a 3D window they are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded.

screenPoints.description: One item per input coordinate, in the same order: the pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), or an error.

ModifyAssociativeDimensions.description: Changes the settings of existing linear dimensions (the Dimension tool's elements, also in sections): the dimension type, the elevation origin, the line pen, the marker type and pen, the text height, pen and frame and the witness line form and value, with the same keys as the dimension creation commands. The text and witness line settings are applied to every witness point. Not written: the witness points, the dimension line position and direction (use MoveElements), the marker size, the text content and position, the witness extension line, the layout and the hole and composite wall dimensioning settings.
ModifyAssociativeDimensions.name: ModifyAssociativeDimensions

dimensionsWithDetails.description: The linear dimensions to change (the Dimension tool's elements, also those placed in sections), each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed.

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.

marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

ModifyBeams.description: Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters. CreateBeams takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill, and the same absolute zCoordinate of the reference line (with an optional floorIndex). Not written: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.
ModifyBeams.name: ModifyBeams

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the beam to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the beam in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with level to set the offset relative to it).

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

holes.description: Replaces all holes currently placed on the beam.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

level.description: Elevation of the reference line relative to the home story.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the beam's reference line, as in CreateBeams. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; level, when given too, is applied after it.

ModifyColumns.description: Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters. CreateColumns takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill. Not written: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.
ModifyColumns.name: ModifyColumns

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the column to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the column in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with bottomOffset to set the offset relative to it).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - see the note on relativeTopStory below.

isFlipped.description: Has no visible effect on a circular column (circleBased cross section) - Archicad ignores it there.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the column's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

veneer.description: Veneer of the column (type, thickness, building material); only the given fields change, thickness 0 removes it. Applied to all segments.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the column's bottom. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative bottomOffset.

ModifyCurtainWallFrames.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Modifies single Curtain Wall Frames by their GUID: the frame contour (a1, a2, b1, b2), the frame class and the frame type. ACAPI_Element_Change does not take a frame on its own, so the change is written through the memo of the owner curtain wall, and read back to check that Archicad applied it.
ModifyCurtainWallFrames.name: ModifyCurtainWallFrames

framesWithDetails.description: Curtain Wall Frames to modify (the GUIDs from GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements), with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed. EXPERIMENTAL.

classIndex.description: The frame class (classID) of the frame: 0 to 3 for the built-in classes, 4 and up for the frame classes of the owner curtain wall.

frameContour.description: The contour of the frame, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Only the given keys are changed.

type.description: The type of the frame (API_CWFrameObjectTypeID).

ModifyCurtainWalls.description: Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls.
ModifyCurtainWalls.name: ModifyCurtainWalls

curtainWallsWithDetails.description: Array of Curtain Wall elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the others, and the frames and panels not affected by them, are left as they are. The fields are those of CreateCurtainWalls, so a curtain wall can be changed in place instead of being deleted and recreated, keeping its GUID, properties and classifications.

cells.description: Assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit of every segment, as in CreateCurtainWalls. Without a pattern change, a cell not listed here keeps its current assignment; with one, it takes the assignment of the first current cell.

coordinates.description: The new 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates is one straight segment, so the number of coordinates must be the current number of segments plus one: the segments can be moved and resized, but not added or removed (a curved segment becomes straight).

floorIndex.description: The new home story index. On its own it moves the curtain wall to that story, keeping its bottom offset from the story; with zCoordinate it pins the story the bottom elevation is measured from.

height.description: The new height of the curtain wall. It is applied before the other fields and read back: when Archicad does not apply it, the item fails and the curtain wall is left unchanged.

primaryPattern.description: The new column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segments (the primary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

secondaryPattern.description: The new row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

zCoordinate.description: The new Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given too.

ModifyDetailMarkers.description: Changes the name, the reference ID, the clip polygon, the boundary's pen and line type, the marker symbol's angle, always-horizontal setting and pen of Detail and Worksheet markers. Not written: the base point (Archicad places it at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box when the marker is created), the viewpoint the marker refers to, and the marker symbol's other settings, which are parameters of the library part placed as the marker (markerId in GetDetailsOfElements). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.
ModifyDetailMarkers.name: ModifyDetailMarkers

angle.description: The new rotation of the marker symbol, in radians (API_DetailType::angle).

clipPolygon.description: The new boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

elementId.description: A Detail or a Worksheet marker.

id.description: The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker.

isHorizontalMarker.description: Whether the marker symbol is always horizontal (API_DetailType::horizontalMarker).

lineTypeIndex.description: Attribute index of the new line type of the boundary (API_DetailType::ltypeInd).

markerPenIndex.description: The new pen of the marker symbol, the library part placed as the marker (its markerId in GetDetailsOfElements).

name.description: The new name of the viewpoint.

penIndex.description: The new pen of the boundary (API_DetailType::pen).

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the new boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

ModifyDoors.description: Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyDoors.name: ModifyDoors

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

ModifyElectricalCircuits.description: Modifies the description, voltage, wiring type and used phases of electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.
ModifyElectricalCircuits.name: ModifyElectricalCircuits

electricalCircuitsData.description: Array of data to modify electrical circuits. Only the given fields are changed.

ModifyElectricalDevices.description: Modifies the apparent power, load classification and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical devices. Available from Archicad 30.
ModifyElectricalDevices.name: ModifyElectricalDevices

electricalDevicesData.description: Array of data to modify electrical devices. Only the given fields are changed.

ModifyElectricalPanels.description: Modifies the name, circuit naming and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical panels. Available from Archicad 30.
ModifyElectricalPanels.name: ModifyElectricalPanels

electricalPanelsData.description: Array of data to modify electrical panels. Only the given fields are changed.

ModifyElectricalProjectSettings.description: Modifies the electrical project settings: sets the default voltage and clears, adds or removes wiring types and load classifications. Available from Archicad 30.
ModifyElectricalProjectSettings.name: ModifyElectricalProjectSettings

clearLoadClassifications.description: If true, every load classification is removed before loadClassificationsToAdd is applied; loadClassificationsToRemove is then not needed and is ignored.

clearWiringTypes.description: If true, every wiring type is removed before wiringTypesToAdd is applied; wiringTypesToRemove is then not needed and is ignored.

loadClassificationsToRemove.description: The names of the load classifications to remove.

wiringTypesToRemove.description: The names of the wiring types to remove.

ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations.description: Modifies the name and/or the rules of graphic override combinations. Omitted fields are kept. Available from Archicad 27.
ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations.name: ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations

graphicOverrideCombinations.description: The graphic override combinations to modify.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The new rules of the combination, in priority order. They replace the current rules. The current rules are kept when omitted.

name.description: The new name of the combination, unique within the project. The current name is kept when omitted.

ModifyGraphicOverrideRules.description: Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27.
ModifyGraphicOverrideRules.name: ModifyGraphicOverrideRules

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules to modify.

criterion.description: The new criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.

criterionXML.description: The new criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements.

name.description: The new name of the rule.

ModifyKeynoteFolders.description: Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyKeynoteFolders.name: ModifyKeynoteFolders

foldersData.description: Array of data to modify keynote folders. Only provided fields are changed.

ModifyKeynoteItems.description: Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyKeynoteItems.name: ModifyKeynoteItems

itemsData.description: Array of data to modify keynote items. Only provided fields are changed.
