ModifyLabels.description: Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyLabels.name: ModifyLabels

labelsWithDetails.description: Array of Label elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The label's class (Text/Symbol) cannot be changed after creation. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the label's text auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

ModifyLamps.description: Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyLamps.name: ModifyLamps

lampsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

lightColor.description: Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

ModifyLevelDimensions.description: Changes existing Level Dimension elements: the position of the marker and the settings CreateLevelDimensions takes (pen, text height and pen, marker type and size, plus sign, angle, origin), with the same keys. Not written: the parent element and the static level (delete and recreate the dimension to change them), the text content and the hide-with-base-element setting.
ModifyLevelDimensions.name: ModifyLevelDimensions

levelDimensionsWithDetails.description: The Level Dimensions to change, each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

position.description: The new location of the marker on the floor plan. An associative level dimension then shows the height of its element at the new position. Optional parameter.

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size), applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text, applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

ModifyLibraryList.description: Adds libraries by path and removes loaded libraries by name or path, in one change of the library list. Returns the result of each addition and removal. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyLibraryList.name: ModifyLibraryList

add.description: Library folders or container files to add, by absolute path.

remove.description: Loaded libraries to remove, each by its name or by its path.

ModifyMEPElements.description: Modifies placed MEP elements: the anchor point, orientation and library part of terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings and flexible segments, the control points, polyline (Piping, from Archicad 28), and width and height of flexible segments. Only the given fields are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element; an item with a field that does not fit its element changes nothing. Archicad reports a 'libraryPartId' it does not find only after the item's other changes were made, so that item's error says which changes stayed. Available from Archicad 27.
ModifyMEPElements.name: ModifyMEPElements

elements.description: The MEP elements to modify, each with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed.

ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems.description: Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29.
ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems.name: ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to modify physical systems. Only the given fields are changed.

ModifyMEPPorts.description: Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyMEPPorts.name: ModifyMEPPorts

portsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP ports. Only provided fields are changed.

ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.description: Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, deletes reference ids from the reference set, and adds and deletes angles of the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.name: ModifyMEPPreferenceTables

anglesToAdd.description: Angles in degrees, between 1 and 90, to add to the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, so that elbow and branch rows can have them. They are added before the tables are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

anglesToDelete.description: Angles to delete from the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Available from Archicad 29.

domain.description: The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.

referenceIdsToDelete.description: Reference ids to delete from the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain.

tables.description: The tables of the domain to change, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Each table is changed in one undoable step.

tablesToAdd.description: New tables to add to the domain, before the other changes.

tablesToDelete.description: The guids of the tables of the domain to delete, after the other table changes.

addedTables.description: One item for each item of tablesToAdd: the guid of the new table, or the error.

deletedTables.description: One result for each item of tablesToDelete.

tables.description: One result for each item of tables.

ModifyMEPRoutingElements.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, insulation thickness of the whole route (segments, elbows and transitions), and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.
ModifyMEPRoutingElements.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.

ModifyMEPSystemGroups.description: Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.
ModifyMEPSystemGroups.name: ModifyMEPSystemGroups

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to modify system groups.

ModifyMeshes.description: Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyMeshes.name: ModifyMeshes

ModifyMorphs.description: Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyMorphs.name: ModifyMorphs

body.description: When given, discards the Morph's ENTIRE existing geometry and rebuilds it from this (mirrors CreateProfiles' replaceSkins) - not a partial edit.

rotationDegreesZ.description: Turns the Morph about the vertical axis through its origin, counterclockwise seen from above, in degrees. Added to the current rotation.

xAxis.description: Replaces the rotation part of the placement transform outright. Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together. If rotationDegreesZ is also given in the same call, it is applied first and this then overwrites its result.

ModifyObjects.description: Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyObjects.name: ModifyObjects

objectsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

ModifyOpenings.description: Modifies Opening elements: the width, the height and the base point CreateOpenings takes. Needs Archicad 28 or earlier; in Archicad 29 and later every item fails with a message pointing to SetOpeningDetails, which changes the size and the position of an opening there.
ModifyOpenings.name: ModifyOpenings

basePoint.description: New base point of the opening: its bottom left corner in world space, the same point CreateOpenings takes.

height.description: New height of the opening. The bottom edge stays where it is, the opening grows or shrinks upwards.

width.description: New width of the opening.

ModifyPens.description: Changes the color, width and description of single pens of the Pen Table in effect for the model views (the default) or the layouts, keeping every other pen as it is. Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet).
ModifyPens.name: ModifyPens

pens.description: The pens to change in the active Pen Table. Only the given fields (color, width, description) of a listed pen are changed; every other pen of the table is left as it is.

target.description: Which active Pen Table to change: the one in effect for the model views (the default) or the one in effect for the layouts. The two can be the same Pen Table.

ModifyPropertyValueOfElements.description: Sets one property value on all the given elements in a single step. If the property is not available for any of the elements, none of them is changed.
ModifyPropertyValueOfElements.name: ModifyPropertyValueOfElements

elements.description: The elements to set the value on. The property must be available for every one of them.

ModifyRailings.description: Modifies Railing elements in place: the height of their segments, the bottom offset and the home story. The reference line, the nodes and segments, and the posts, rails and panels stay as they are. Each railing is read back after the change, and a value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.
ModifyRailings.name: ModifyRailings

bottomOffset.description: The new base height of the railing relative to its home story.

floorIndex.description: The new home story index (as returned by GetStories). The bottom offset is kept, or set from bottomOffset when that is given too, so the railing moves with the story.

height.description: The new height of the railing segments (the height GetDetailsOfElements returns), applied to every segment of the railing.

ModifyRevisionIssues.description: Modifies the ID, the short description and the custom scheme data of the given revision issues. Only the given fields are changed. Issued revision issues may refuse the change.
ModifyRevisionIssues.name: ModifyRevisionIssues

revisionIssues.description: The revision issues to modify. Only the given fields are changed.

customSchemeData.description: The custom scheme fields to set. A field is addressed by its key (as GetRevisionIssues returns it) or by its name; the fields not listed keep their values.

description.description: The new short description of the revision issue.

id.description: The new ID of the revision issue.

ModifyRoofs.description: Modifies single-plane and multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters. The plan outline, level, thickness and structure apply to both; angle, pivotLine and edgeTrims (the cut of each polygon edge) only to single-plane roofs; levels, eavesOverhang and pivotEdges only to multi-plane roofs.
ModifyRoofs.name: ModifyRoofs

angle.description: Single-plane roofs only: the angle of the plane to the XY plane.

edgeTrims.description: Single-plane roofs only: the cut of each edge of the roof's polygon, one item per edge in the order GetDetailsOfElements reports them in edgeTrims (the outline, then each hole). Only the given fields change; an empty item keeps its edge. Cannot be combined with polygonOutline.

angle.description: The angle of the edge cut in radians, as GetDetailsOfElements reports it. Only CustomAngle uses it.

trimType.description: Vertical, Perpendicular to the roof plane, Horizontal, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle).

floorIndex.description: Home story of the roof. With level, the roof gets this home story at the absolute elevation level; without level, it moves to this story and keeps its offset from the story.

level.description: Absolute elevation of the roof's pivot line (the zCoordinate GetDetailsOfElements returns). The roof is put on the story floorIndex when given, else on the story at this elevation.

pivotEdges.description: Multi-plane roofs only: the roof planes of each edge of the pivot polygon, one item per edge in the order GetDetailsOfElements reports them (the outline, then each hole). Only the given fields change; an item without levels keeps its edge. Cannot be combined with polygonOutline.

levels.description: The roof plane of the edge on each level, from the pivot polygon upwards; at most as many as the roof has levels.

angle.description: Angle of the plane to the XY plane.

angleType.description: Gable for a vertical gable plane, Sloped otherwise.

eavesOverhang.description: Extension of the eaves outside the pivot polygon.

pivotLine.description: Single-plane roofs only: the line the plane rises from. The ends are named begCoordinate and endCoordinate as in CreateRoofs, or begin and end as GetDetailsOfElements reports them.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite roof first.

ModifySections.description: Changes the name and the reference ID of Section and Elevation elements, which the Project Map and the markers show. GetDetailsOfElements reads those of a Section back as name and idStr.
ModifySections.name: ModifySections

elementId.description: A Section or an Elevation.

id.description: The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker.

name.description: The new name, shown in the Project Map.

ModifyShells.description: Modifies the structure (Basic or Composite, building material or composite) of Shell elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyShells.name: ModifyShells

ModifySkylights.description: Modifies Skylight elements: anchor position and anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display option, pens, line types, section fill and pens, surface and the use-the-library-part's-settings flags - the same settings CreateSkylights takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given settings change. Not written by this command: the owner roof or shell, the anchor level and the vertical link (Archicad places the skylight on its owner), the plane of a multi-plane roof it sits on, the dimension marker (a separate element) and the library part's own parameters (use SetGDLParametersOfElements). Archicad may set the elevation angle again from the owner.
ModifySkylights.name: ModifySkylights

skylightsWithDetails.description: The skylights to modify, each with the settings to change. The settings not given stay as they are.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

anchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

fixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectMaterials.description: Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

ModifySlabs.description: Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters. CreateSlabs takes the same surfaces, cut fill pens and floor fill. Not written: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Of the cover fill orientation, Archicad applies only the type to a Slab through the API; a given origin or distortion matrix that did not stick gets a failed execution result, while the other details are applied.
ModifySlabs.name: ModifySlabs

bottomMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

floorFill.description: The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story.

holes.description: Can be given on its own, without polygonOutline, to add/remove/clear holes in place (an empty array clears all holes) - the slab's current outline is reused unchanged.

polygonOutline.description: Replaces the slab's entire polygon, including its holes - resend the holes field too to keep them, otherwise they are removed.

sideMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite slab first.

topMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the slab's reference level. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative level.

ModifyStairs.description: Modifies Stair elements in place, keeping their baseline and position: the flight width, total height, number of steps, riser height and going with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra top and bottom treads, the walking line position and offset, the step numbering, the walking direction, the uniform finish, monolith and draining settings, and for the flights and the landings the tread and riser settings (presence, thickness, offset, nosing, riser cross section and position) and the structure of each side (presence, type, underside shape and thickness). CreateStairs accepts the same settings. Only the given settings are changed. Archicad solves the stair again within its baseline, so it may adjust the step values; read them back with GetDetailsOfElements. Not written by this command: the baseline with its landings and winders, the top link, the floor plan display (symbol and marker layout), the headroom and the stair rules; the subelements (treads, risers, structures) take the per-part settings above and cannot be written one by one through the API.
ModifyStairs.name: ModifyStairs

stairsWithDetails.description: Array of Stair elements to modify, with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the baseline, the position and the omitted settings are kept.

extraBottomTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.

extraTopTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.

inputDirection.description: The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).

numberingType.description: Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.

risers.description: The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown.

structures.description: The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed.

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

totalHeight.description: The height of the stair relative to its bottom.

totalHeightLocked.description: Whether the total height is locked.

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.

treads.description: The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

uniformDrainings.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.

uniformFinish.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.

uniformMonolithAttributes.description: Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.

walkingLineOffset.description: The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.

walkingLinePosition.description: Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).

ModifyTexts.description: Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyTexts.name: ModifyTexts

textsWithDetails.description: Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; a text that wraps keeps its wrap width through the rebuild unless the same item gives a width. The other style fields and a width leave the content as it is.

coordinate.description: The new placement position. As in CreateTexts, the z value selects the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

floorIndex.description: Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

width.description: Optional box width in mm (paper size, like height). Greater than 0 turns word wrap on: the text wraps within this width ('Wrap Text' in the Text settings, nonBreaking false). 0 turns word wrap off: the text is auto-width and grows with its content; on a wrapped text this rebuilds the content, so like a pen change it is refused for content with an autotext run. Given alone it leaves the content and its runs (and any autotext in them) as they are. When the content is rebuilt in the same item, the width is applied after the rebuild. When omitted, the current wrap setting is kept, also through a rebuild of the content. Read back by GetDetailsOfElements as style.boxWidth, with style.nonBreaking false.

ModifyWalls.description: Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as CreateWalls, applied by the same code, plus geometryType (Straight or Trapezoid), profileType and bottomOffset. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'.
ModifyWalls.name: ModifyWalls

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero makes the wall curved (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen. Not inheritable/overridable like cutFillPen, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field regardless of structureType.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Background pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

cutFillPen.description: Pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

flipped.description: True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped).

geometryType.description: Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

profileType.description: slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' for the same wall: whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch such a wall first.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

ModifyWindows.description: Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters.
ModifyWindows.name: ModifyWindows

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

ModifyZones.description: Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link, floor thickness, contour line and cover fill - the same settings as CreateZones, applied by the same helpers. Only the given fields are changed. The polygon of a manual zone cannot be changed here (the change takes no polygon memo), nor the reference point of an automatic one (SetDetailsOfElements moves it).
ModifyZones.name: ModifyZones

zonesWithDetails.description: Array of Zone elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon and the omitted fields are kept. The same fields as the ZoneSettings of SetDetailsOfElements.

bottomOffset.description: Base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

contourLine.description: Contour line of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.

coverFill.description: Cover fill of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

floorThickness.description: Thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

height.description: Height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height), so do not combine it with relativeTopStory in the same call: whichever is applied last wins.

name.description: Name of the zone.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not set together with height in the same call, see the note on height.

stampAngle.description: Rotation angle of the zone stamp in radians.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

topOffset.description: Offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

MoveAttributesAndFolders.description: Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder; an attribute or folder that is already directly in the target folder counts as moved. Available from Archicad 26.
MoveAttributesAndFolders.name: MoveAttributesAndFolders

attributeFolders.description: The folders to move, with their contents. They must have the attribute type of the target folder.

attributeIds.description: The attributes to move. They must have the attribute type of the target folder.

targetFolder.description: The folder to move the attributes and folders into. An empty path is the root folder.

attributeExecutionResults.description: One result per item of attributeIds, in the same order.

folderExecutionResults.description: One result per item of attributeFolders, in the same order.

MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet.description: Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29.
MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet.name: MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move.

MoveElements.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.
MoveElements.name: MoveElements

elementsWithMoveVectors.description: The elements with move vector pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be moved. By default it's false.

MoveElementsToDesignOptions.description: Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29.
MoveElementsToDesignOptions.name: MoveElementsToDesignOptions

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move the element into. Use NULLGuid to remove the element from any design option and move it to the main model.

MoveFavoriteFolder.description: Moves a folder of the Favorites palette, with its Favorites and subfolders, into another folder. Folders are given as their path of folder names from the root. Returns the new path of the folder. Available from Archicad 29.
MoveFavoriteFolder.name: MoveFavoriteFolder

folder.description: The folder of the Favorites palette to move, as the folder names from the root down. The root folder cannot be moved.

targetFolder.description: The folder to move it into, as the folder names from the root down. Empty = root. It cannot be the moved folder or one of its subfolders.

folder.description: The new path of the moved folder, as the folder names from the root down.

MoveFavorites.description: Moves Favorites given by their names into a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Returns an execution result for each Favorite. Available from Archicad 29.
MoveFavorites.name: MoveFavorites

targetPath.description: The path of the folder to move the Favorites into, in the format GetFavoriteFolders returns: the folder names from the root down. Empty for the root folder.

MoveGraphicOverrideRules.description: Moves graphic override rules to another rule group, or to another place in their own group. Available from Archicad 27.
MoveGraphicOverrideRules.name: MoveGraphicOverrideRules

graphicOverrideRules.description: The rules to move, processed in this order.

MoveNavigatorItem.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to.
MoveNavigatorItem.name: MoveNavigatorItem

parentNavigatorItemId.description: The new parent of the item. It can be the item's current parent, to change the order of the items in it.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: Optional child of parentNavigatorItemId that the item is placed right after. Without it an item moved within its own parent goes to the end of it.

MoveProjectInfoFields.description: Moves fields of the Project Info groups to a group, before another field of it or to its end. A subfield of a calculated field moves with its parent field. Available from Archicad 30.
MoveProjectInfoFields.name: MoveProjectInfoFields

projectInfoFields.description: The fields of the Project Info groups to move, in the order the moves are made. A subfield of a calculated field cannot be moved on its own, it moves with its parent field.

beforeProjectInfoFieldId.description: The field of the target group to move the field before. When omitted, the field is moved to the end of the group.

projectInfoGroupId.description: The group to move the field to. To reorder a field within its group, give its current group.

MoveProjectInfoGroups.description: Moves Project Info groups before another group, or to the end of the group list when no other group is given. Available from Archicad 30.
MoveProjectInfoGroups.name: MoveProjectInfoGroups

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to move, in the order the moves are made.

NewProject.description: Starts a new, untitled project from the template set in Archicad's New Project settings, as File > New does; with newAndReset also the working environment is reset, as New and Reset All does. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded, as with OpenProject.
NewProject.name: NewProject

newAndReset.description: Optional. Also reset the working environment to the template's, as File > New > New and Reset All does, instead of keeping the current one as File > New does. Defaults to false.

OpenLibraryPartInEditor.description: Opens a loaded library part, given by its fileName or documentName as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts, in Archicad's library part editor. Available from Archicad 27.
OpenLibraryPartInEditor.name: OpenLibraryPartInEditor

name.description: The name of the loaded library part to open: its fileName (with extension, e.g. 'My Object.gsm') or its documentName, as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

OpenProject.description: Opens the given project. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded without asking: Archicad has no query for them, so call SaveProject first when they must be kept.
OpenProject.name: OpenProject

projectFilePath.description: The target project file to open.

OpenSettingsDialog.description: Opens Archicad's settings dialog of the selected elements or the current tool (Archicad 28 and later), or the default settings dialog of the given element type, waits for the user and reports whether the dialog was closed with OK or Cancel.
OpenSettingsDialog.name: OpenSettingsDialog

elementType.description: Opens the default settings dialog of this tool. Without it, Archicad 28 and later open the settings of the selected elements, or of the current tool when nothing is selected; Archicad 25 to 27 open the default settings of the current tool.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel, false when with OK.

PhotoRender.description: Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). The image size, resolution and quality come from the scene; a width, height or resolution given here is used for this render only, the scene is not changed. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.
PhotoRender.name: PhotoRender

format.description: Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).

height.description: Optional. The height of the image in pixels (the Size field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the height of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.

imageFilePath.description: Absolute path of the image file to write. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. false refuses to render when a file already exists at imageFilePath, and writes nothing.

resolution.description: Optional. The resolution of the image in dpi (the Resolution field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the resolution of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.

sceneName.description: Optional. The rendering scene to render with, one of the names GetRenderingScenes returns. It is made the current scene first, as SetCurrentRenderingScene does, and stays current afterwards. Omitted, the current scene is used.

width.description: Optional. The width of the image in pixels (the Size field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the width of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.

PickAttribute.description: Opens a small dialog with Archicad's attribute picker for the given attribute type (layer, building material, composite, profile or surface; fill and line from Archicad 27), waits for the user and returns the chosen attribute, or cancelled. Available from Archicad 26.
PickAttribute.name: PickAttribute

attributeId.description: The attribute selected when the dialog opens. Without it the picker starts empty and OK is enabled once the user has picked an attribute.

attributeType.description: The type of the attribute to pick. Fill and Line need Archicad 27 or newer. Composite lists the composites only.

title.description: The title of the dialog. Default: Pick Attribute.

attributeId.description: The chosen attribute. Only when not cancelled.

attributeType.description: The type of the chosen attribute, the attributeType of the input. Only when not cancelled.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel, false when with OK.

PickAttributeFolder.description: Opens a small dialog with Archicad's attribute folder picker for the given attribute type, waits for the user and returns the chosen folder as its path from the root folder, or cancelled. Available from Archicad 26.
PickAttributeFolder.name: PickAttributeFolder

attributeType.description: The type of the attributes whose folders the picker lists. Fill and Line need Archicad 27 or newer.

title.description: The title of the dialog. Default: Pick Attribute Folder.

attributeFolder.description: The chosen folder; its path works as the targetFolder of MoveAttributesAndFolders. Only when not cancelled.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel, false when with OK.

PickLibraryFolder.description: Opens Archicad's dialog for choosing or creating a library folder, waits for the user and returns the location of the folder, or reports that the user cancelled. The folder is not added to the libraries of the project.
PickLibraryFolder.name: PickLibraryFolder

defaultName.description: The default name the dialog offers for a new library folder. Default: New Library.

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled the dialog.

path.description: The location of the chosen or created folder. It is not added to the libraries of the project; use AddLibraries for that. Only when cancelled is false.

PickLibraryPart.description: Opens Archicad's Object, Lamp, Window or Door Settings dialog, optionally limited to a library part subtype, lets the user pick a library part and set its parameters, and returns the chosen library part with its GDL parameters, or that the user cancelled. Places nothing.
PickLibraryPart.name: PickLibraryPart

elementType.description: Whose settings dialog to open: the Object, Lamp, Window or Door tool's. Without a subtypeUnID the dialog lists the library parts of that tool. Object by default.

subtypeUnID.description: Limits the dialog to the library parts of this subtype: the unique ID of the subtype library part, its main and revision GUID in the form {main}-{revision}.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel; then nothing else is returned.

libPart.description: The library part the user chose. Absent when it could not be read.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the chosen library part, with the values set in the dialog. Present when the user pressed OK.

subtypeUnID.description: The unique ID of the chosen library part's subtype, as Archicad returned it.

PickLibraryPartFile.description: Opens Archicad's Open Library Part dialog, waits for the user and returns the location of the chosen library part, or reports that the user cancelled.
PickLibraryPartFile.name: PickLibraryPartFile

generalGDLObjectsOnly.description: Sets the dialog's file filter to General GDL Objects. Default: false.

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled the dialog or chose no valid library part.

openedInExternalEditor.description: True when Archicad opened the chosen file in an external editor (Archicad 26 and later; always false in Archicad 25). Only when cancelled is false.

path.description: The location of the chosen library part. Only when cancelled is false.

PickLibraryPartSaveLocation.description: Opens Archicad's Save Library Part dialog (object, door or window), waits for the user and returns the location chosen to save the library part to, or reports that the user cancelled. Nothing is saved.
PickLibraryPartSaveLocation.name: PickLibraryPartSaveLocation

browseForFolder.description: Lets the user save outside the embedded library. Default: false.

defaultPath.description: The location (library folder and file name) the dialog starts from. Default: <libraryPartType>.gsm in the embedded library of the project.

libraryPartType.description: Which Save Library Part dialog to open. Default: Object.

title.description: The title of the dialog. Default: Archicad's own title.

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled the dialog.

path.description: The location the user chose to save the library part to. Nothing is saved there. Only when cancelled is false.

PickPictureFile.description: Opens Archicad's Open Picture dialog (the one of the texture settings), waits for the user and returns the location of the chosen picture, or reports that the user cancelled. Archicad adds the chosen picture to the embedded library when it is not in it yet.
PickPictureFile.name: PickPictureFile

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled the dialog or chose no valid picture.

path.description: The location of the chosen picture. Archicad adds the picture to the embedded library when it is not in it yet. Only when cancelled is false.

PickZoneStampOrLabelFile.description: Opens Archicad's dialog for opening a zone stamp or label library part, waits for the user and returns the location of the chosen file, or reports that the user cancelled.
PickZoneStampOrLabelFile.name: PickZoneStampOrLabelFile

objectType.description: The type of library part the dialog lets the user open. Default: Label.

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled the dialog or chose no valid zone stamp or label.

path.description: The location of the chosen zone stamp or label. Only when cancelled is false.

PlaceOpenings.description: Places openings with the Opening tool settings at points of their parent elements. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface. Each opening can be given its own extrusion and floor plan settings, which change only that opening and not the tool's settings. Available from Archicad 29.
PlaceOpenings.name: PlaceOpenings

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

constraint.description: How the opening's orientation is constrained.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

height.description: The opening's height. See linkedStatus.

limitType.description: How far the opening's extrusion reaches.

linkedStatus.description: Whether the opening's width and height are linked. While they are linked, giving both width and height makes a square of the height; give NotLinked with them to get a different width and height.

shapeType.description: The shape of the opening's polygon.

width.description: The opening's width. See linkedStatus.

floorPlanParameters.description: The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.

clearCutSymbol.description: Removes the cut symbol. Cannot be given together with cutSymbolLibPartId.

clearUnCutSymbol.description: Removes the uncut symbol. Cannot be given together with unCutSymbolLibPartId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

dividedOpeningMode.description: How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.

floorPlanDisplayMode.description: How the opening is shown on the floor plan.

openEdgeStyle.description: How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

parentElementId.description: The element to place the opening in.

point.description: Where to place the opening. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface.

fixText.description: Use fixed text size. The default is false.

grid.description: Print the grid. The default is false.

printArea.description: The area to print. The default is 'currentView'.

PublishPublisherSet.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published.
PublishPublisherSet.name: PublishPublisherSet

outputPath.description: Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set.

selectedNavigatorItemIds.description: Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set.

QuitArchicad.description: Performs a quit operation on the currently running Archicad instance.
QuitArchicad.name: QuitArchicad

ReadFavoritesFile.description: Read the Favorites of a .prefs file or folder without importing them, returning the name, element type and folder of each. Nothing in the project changes, so the result can be compared with the project's Favorites before ImportFavorites.
ReadFavoritesFile.name: ReadFavoritesFile

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host to a Favorites file (.prefs) or folder.

RebuildCurrentDatabase.description: Rebuilds the current database, the one the API works on (see ChangeWindow). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
RebuildCurrentDatabase.name: RebuildCurrentDatabase

regenerate.description: Regenerate the view. The default is false, meaning the view will not be regenerated, but rebuilt.

RedrawCurrentDatabase.description: Redraws the current database, even when its window is in the background. Only the visible region of its window is updated.
RedrawCurrentDatabase.name: RedrawCurrentDatabase

RefreshElements.description: Refreshes (rebuilds) the given elements, for example placed Objects, Windows and Doors that still show the old geometry after their library part's script or embedded file changed. Set force to true to run the parameter script of GDL-based elements too. The elements are looked up in the current database (floor plan, section or detail window). Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone.
RefreshElements.name: RefreshElements

force.description: Forces the rebuild of GDL-based elements, which runs their parameter script. The default is false.

RegularizePolygons.description: Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.
RegularizePolygons.name: RegularizePolygons

polygons.description: The polygons to regularize, in the format of CreateSlabs (polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs, holes). For CreateHatches, pass the outline of a result as its coordinates and arcs.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

RegularizePolylines.description: Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.
RegularizePolylines.name: RegularizePolylines

polylines.description: The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

ReindexAttributes.description: Moves fills, line types, surfaces, building materials and zone categories to new indices, the way ReindexLayers moves layers. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so the attribute is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary attributes, which are deleted again) and every reference to the old index is rewritten to the new one: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, the memo data of roofs, slabs, meshes, morphs, curtain walls, beams, columns, stairs and interior elevations, the tool defaults, the Favorites (with their sub-elements: a curtain wall's frame and panel classes, a stair's structures), the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Only then is the old attribute deleted. The new attribute has a new attribute id (Archicad does not keep a given id); its name, definition and attribute folder are the old ones. Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so their layers are shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (in the current window, as Archicad keeps these flags per window). If an element still cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed; their module file has to be reindexed on its own. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the old index (Archicad does not take them from ACAPI_Favorite_Change, so such Favorites are left as they are and named in the warnings). dryRun lists every reference without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Pens, layers (see ReindexLayers) and the other attribute types are not supported. Available from Archicad 27.
ReindexAttributes.name: ReindexAttributes

attributeType.description: The type of the attributes to move. Layers are moved by ReindexLayers; pens and the other attribute types cannot be moved.

attributes.description: The attributes to move to a new index, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The attribute to move.

newIndex.description: The index the attribute gets. It must not be used by another attribute of the type.

dryRun.description: Only list every reference to each attribute (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules) without changing anything. The default is false.

maxPlaceholders.description: Every free index below newIndex is filled with a temporary attribute first, so a newIndex far above the highest index in use takes long. An attribute that needs more temporary attributes than this is not moved. The default is 1000.

attributes.description: One item per requested attribute, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The attribute at its new index. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute in place, so this is a new attribute with a new id; with dryRun it is the attribute's current id.

attributes.description: The other attributes that refer to the attribute: composites (skins and separators), building materials (cut fill, cut surface), surfaces (hatching fill), MEP systems (fill) and profiles (skins and edges). Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

elements.description: The elements that refer to the attribute, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout: in their own fields, their library part parameters or their memo data (side surfaces, roof levels, morph faces, cutting planes). Rewritten to the new index unless dryRun is true.

favorites.description: The names of the Favorites that refer to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

hotlinkElements.description: Elements from hotlinked modules that refer to the attribute. They cannot be changed and keep the old index until their module file is reindexed.

layersShown.description: The hidden or locked layers of the elements that were shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards. Not present with dryRun.

overrideRules.description: The names of the graphic override rules that refer to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

placeholders.description: The number of temporary attributes needed for the free indices below newIndex.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default refers to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

warnings.description: What keeps the old index or did not work after the attribute was moved: elements from hotlinked modules, a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule that could not be written, the name or the attribute folder.

ReindexLayers.description: Moves layers to new indices. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so each layer is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary layers, which are deleted again), gets the old layer's state in every layer combination, and then every element of the old layer is moved to it, in the floor plan and in every view and layout database, with the tool defaults on that layer. Only when the old layer is empty everywhere is it deleted, and the new layer gets its name, flags and folder. If an element cannot be moved (it is locked, not reserved in Teamwork, or comes from a hotlinked module), that layer is left as it was. The new layer has a new attribute id; Favorites that use the layer are not updated. Archicad keeps the shown, locked and wireframe state of a layer per open window: the new layer gets the old one's state in the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the other open windows. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show of the layer come back on the new layer when those views are rebuilt (listed as viewsToRebuild). dryRun lists the elements and tool defaults on each layer without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from Archicad 27.
ReindexLayers.name: ReindexLayers

dryRun.description: Only list what would change (the elements on each layer, the tools whose default layer it is, the elements that block the move) without changing anything. The default is false.

layers.description: The layers to move to a new index, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The layer to move.

newIndex.description: The index the layer gets. It must not be used by another layer. Index 1 (the Archicad Layer) cannot be used or moved.

maxPlaceholders.description: Every free index below newIndex is filled with a temporary layer first (about 20 ms each), so a newIndex far above the highest index in use takes long. A layer that needs more temporary layers than this is not moved. The default is 1000.

layers.description: One item per requested layer, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The layer at its new index. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute in place, so this is a new attribute with a new id; with dryRun it is the layer's current id.

blockedElements.description: Only with dryRun: elements on the layer that cannot be moved, because they come from a hotlinked module. Without dryRun such a layer is not moved.

elements.description: The elements on the layer, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout. Moved to the new layer unless dryRun is true. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show are not listed (see viewsToRebuild).

placeholders.description: The number of temporary layers needed for the free indices below newIndex.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default is on this layer. They are set to the new layer unless dryRun is true.

viewsToRebuild.description: The sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents that show elements of the layer. The model elements they show are deleted with the old layer and come back on the new layer when the view is rebuilt: Archicad does that when the view is opened, unless it is set to be rebuilt manually. To rebuild one at once, call ChangeWindow with its databaseId and then RebuildCurrentDatabase.

warnings.description: What did not work after the layer was moved: its name and flags, or the move into its attribute folder.

ReleaseElementState.description: Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits.
ReleaseElementState.name: ReleaseElementState

stateId.description: The state to free, as returned by CaptureElementState.

ReleaseElements.description: Releases elements in Teamwork mode. Fails, naming them, when any of the given GUIDs is not an element; the other elements are released.
ReleaseElements.name: ReleaseElements

ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement.description: Releases the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode.
ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement.name: ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement

ReleaseLockableObjectSet.description: Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode.
ReleaseLockableObjectSet.name: ReleaseLockableObjectSet

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

ReleaseProjectData.description: Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork.
ReleaseProjectData.name: ReleaseProjectData

names.description: The names of the project data to release.

host.description: The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.

port.description: The port number of the notification client.

RemoveElementTrims.description: Removes the trim between an element and the roof or shell trimming it. The Archicad API removes the trimming connection between the two elements, so when they trim each other (two roofs or shells) both directions are removed; trim the other direction again with TrimElements to keep it. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each pair whose element is trimmed by its trimming element gets wouldDelete.
RemoveElementTrims.name: RemoveElementTrims

elementPairs.description: The trimmed element and the roof or shell trimming it, per pair. The trimming connection between the two is removed: when they trim each other, both directions are removed.

executionResults.description: One result for each input pair, in the order of the input. On a dry run a pair whose element is trimmed by the trimming element gets wouldDelete.

RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfEleme.description: Removes IFC classification references stored on elements, given by the name of their classification and optionally their identification; without identification every stored reference of that classification is removed. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has a matching stored reference gets wouldDelete.
RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfEleme.name: RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

elementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references to remove from the elements. Only references stored on the elements (the ones GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements returns with storedOnly) can be removed.

executionResults.description: One result for each input item, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that has a stored IFC classification reference of the given classification (and identification, when given) gets wouldDelete.

RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements.description: Removes local IFC properties, given by property set and property name, from elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has the local IFC property gets wouldDelete.
RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements.name: RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements

elementIFCProperties.description: The local IFC properties to remove.

executionResults.description: One result for each input item, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that has the local IFC property gets wouldDelete.

RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud.description: Removes libraries, given by name, from a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29.
RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud.name: RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud

libraryNames.description: The names of the libraries on the server to remove.

parentPath.description: The path of the folder on the server that holds the libraries, as shown in BIMcloud Manager.

serverUrl.description: The URL of the BIMcloud or Teamwork server, e.g. 'https://bimcloud.example.com:22000'.

executionResults.description: One result per library, in the order of the input.

RemovePropertyFromAttributes.description: Makes a custom property unavailable for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and wouldDelete when the property and every attribute exist.
RemovePropertyFromAttributes.name: RemovePropertyFromAttributes

attributeIds.description: The attributes (for example Building Materials) to make the property unavailable for.

returns.description: The result of the execution: success, with error when it failed. A dry run also answers dryRun, and wouldDelete when the property and every attribute exist.

RemoveSolidElementLinks.description: Removes solid element operation links between target and operator elements. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each link that exists gets wouldDelete.
RemoveSolidElementLinks.name: RemoveSolidElementLinks

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to remove.

executionResults.description: One result for each input link, in the order of the input. On a dry run a link that exists (the operator is linked to the target) gets wouldDelete.

RenameAttributeFolders.description: Renames attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, to the given new names. The root folder cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 26.
RenameAttributeFolders.name: RenameAttributeFolders

attributeFolders.description: The folders to rename, each given by attribute type and path together with its new name.

RenameAttributes.description: Renames attributes of any type (layers, layer combinations, composites, surfaces, ...). Each attribute keeps its index, its id and its settings. A new name that another attribute of the same type already has is refused, and so is renaming the attributes Archicad does not allow to change (the built-in Archicad Layer, the Solid and Empty fills).
RenameAttributes.name: RenameAttributes

attributes.description: The attributes to rename, of any type.

newName.description: The new name of the attribute. It must not be empty or the name of another attribute of the same type.

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order.

RenameDesignOptionCombinations.description: Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.
RenameDesignOptionCombinations.name: RenameDesignOptionCombinations

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to rename, each with the new name.

name.description: The new name of the design option combination.

RenameDesignOptionSets.description: Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.
RenameDesignOptionSets.name: RenameDesignOptionSets

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to rename, each with the new name.

name.description: The new name of the design option set.

RenameDesignOptions.description: Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.
RenameDesignOptions.name: RenameDesignOptions

designOptions.description: The design options to rename, each with the new name and/or id. At least one of them must be given.

id.description: The new string id of the design option. The id is kept when it is not given.

name.description: The new name of the design option. The name is kept when it is not given.

RenameFavoriteFolder.description: Renames a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. The root folder cannot be renamed. Returns the renamed folder. Available from Archicad 29.
RenameFavoriteFolder.name: RenameFavoriteFolder

newName.description: The new name of the folder.

path.description: The path of the folder to rename, in the format GetFavoriteFolders returns: the folder names from the root down. The root folder cannot be renamed.

RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: Renames graphic override rule groups, found by name. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.
RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.name: RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups

ruleGroups.description: The rule groups to rename. Their rules and the combinations that contain them are kept.

RenameNavigatorItem.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Renaming the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing also sets the custom name of the Drawing. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.
RenameNavigatorItem.name: RenameNavigatorItem

customName.description: Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.

newId.description: The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on a Project Map section, elevation, interior elevation, detail or worksheet it is the reference ID of the element behind the item; on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).

newName.description: The new name of the item. On the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing it is also set as the custom name of the Drawing (nameType CustomName).

RenameProjectInfoFields.description: Renames custom fields of the Project Info groups. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 30.
RenameProjectInfoFields.name: RenameProjectInfoFields

projectInfoFields.description: The fields of the Project Info groups to rename, each with its new name. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed.

name.description: The new name of the field. It must not be used by another field.

RenameProjectInfoGroups.description: Renames Project Info groups. Available from Archicad 30.
RenameProjectInfoGroups.name: RenameProjectInfoGroups

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to rename, each with its new name.

ReorderDesignOptionSets.description: Moves the given design option sets before another set or to the end of the list. Available from Archicad 29.
ReorderDesignOptionSets.name: ReorderDesignOptionSets

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to move, in the order the moves are done.

beforeDesignOptionSetId.description: The design option set to move it before. When it is not given, the set is moved to the end.

designOptionSetId.description: The design option set to move.

ReorderDesignOptionsInSet.description: Moves the given design options before another design option of the same set or to the end of their set. Available from Archicad 29.
ReorderDesignOptionsInSet.name: ReorderDesignOptionsInSet

designOptions.description: The design options to move, in the order the moves are done.

beforeDesignOptionId.description: The design option of the same set to move it before. When it is not given, the design option is moved to the end of its set.
