designOptionId.description: The design option to move within its set.

ReorderNavigatorItems.description: Reorders the children of a navigator item to match the given order. Works around MoveNavigatorItem being unable to reposition an item within its current parent, by bouncing it through a sibling.
ReorderNavigatorItems.name: ReorderNavigatorItems

orderedNavigatorItemIds.description: The complete, desired order of every child of parentNavigatorItemId. Every current child must be listed.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: The folder whose children should be reordered.

RequestProjectData.description: Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message.
RequestProjectData.name: RequestProjectData

mailText.description: The message sent with the request. The default is empty.

names.description: The names of the project data to request from the users who have reserved them.

ReserveElements.description: Reserves elements in Teamwork mode. GUIDs that are not elements (navigator items, layouts, databases) cannot be reserved with it: they are returned in notElements and the execution result fails.
ReserveElements.name: ReserveElements

notElements.description: The given GUIDs that are not elements, e.g. navigator items, layouts or databases. They were not reserved, and executionResult fails because of them even if the other elements were reserved. Left out when every GUID is an element.

ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement.description: Reserves the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode, which is needed before changing hotlink nodes.
ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement.name: ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement

conflicts.description: The user whose reservation prevented reserving the Hotlink and XRef management.

ReserveLockableObjectSet.description: Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'.
ReserveLockableObjectSet.name: ReserveLockableObjectSet

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

conflicts.description: The users whose reservation prevented reserving the object set.

ReserveProjectData.description: Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it.
ReserveProjectData.name: ReserveProjectData

names.description: The names of the project data to reserve.

conflicts.description: The project data that could not be reserved because another user has reserved it.

ResetLibraries.description: Resets the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library reset.
ResetLibraries.name: ResetLibraries

ResetZoom.description: Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back.
ResetZoom.name: ResetZoom

numberOfStepsBack.description: The number of steps to go back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back. The default is 1.

ResolveNames.description: Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only.
ResolveNames.name: ResolveNames

maxCloseMatches.description: The most close matches returned for one word, best first. The default is 5.

names.description: The words or phrases to look up in the open project, for example taken from a user's question.

kind.description: The kind of item the word names. When it is left out, every kind is searched.

name.description: The word or phrase.

results.description: One result for each of the given names, in the same order.

closeMatches.description: When nothing is named exactly so: the nearest items, best first. Empty when the status is found or notFound.

found.description: The items named exactly so (the same characters), with match 'exact'. More than one when items of different kinds, or several stories, have the name.

name.description: The given word or phrase.

status.description: found: an item of the project has exactly this name (see found). closeMatches: no item has exactly this name, but some are close (see closeMatches). notFound: nothing in the project is close to it; the project has no such item, so it must not be guessed.

RotateCopyElements.description: Copies elements rotated around a center on the floor plan by an angle in radians, like rotating a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is rotated by n times the angle, which makes a circular array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.
RotateCopyElements.name: RotateCopyElements

angle.description: The angle in radians the first copy is rotated by from its element, counterclockwise.

center.description: The center of the rotation on the floor plan.

count.description: Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is rotated by n times the angle, so more than one makes a circular array. By default it's 1.

elements.description: The elements to copy.

copies.description: One item for each given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.

error.description: Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

RotateElements.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.
RotateElements.name: RotateElements

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a copy of the element is rotated. By default it's false.

beginPoint.description: Starting point of the rotation arc.

endPoint.description: End point of the rotation arc.

RunActionCenterChecks.description: Runs the given checks of the Action Center (by default the hotlink check). A successful result means the check ran, not that nothing was found: Archicad does not report the outcome to the caller, it shows the Action Center tab when the check found an issue.
RunActionCenterChecks.name: RunActionCenterChecks

checks.description: The Action Center checks to run, in this order. Omitted means ["Hotlinks"]. "Hotlinks" is available on every Archicad version; "All", "Libraries", "Drawings" and "Licenses" only on Archicad 25, later versions return an error for them in their execution result.

RunParameterScriptOfElements.description: Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.
RunParameterScriptOfElements.name: RunParameterScriptOfElements

SaveAsModuleFile.description: Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.
SaveAsModuleFile.name: SaveAsModuleFile

elements.description: Optional. The elements that go into the module; omitted, the current selection does, as Save Selection as Module would. Pass GetAllElements for the whole project. Archicad 25 and 26 support the selection form only.

moduleFilePath.description: Absolute path of the .mod file to write. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false. The current window must be a floor plan, section, elevation or detail.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. false refuses to save when a file already exists at moduleFilePath, and writes nothing.

SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.description: Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format. Master layout windows are not supported: save a layout that uses the master layout instead. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.
SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.name: SaveCurrentWindowAsImage

colorDepth.description: Optional, trueColor by default. The color depth of the image, as in the Save as picture dialog.

dithered.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the image is dithered when its color depth drops colors.

entireDrawing.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the image covers the entire drawing of a 2D window instead of its current zoom, as the Entire Drawing option of the Save as picture dialog does.

format.description: Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).

imageFilePath.description: Absolute path of the image file to write. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. false refuses to save when a file already exists at imageFilePath, and writes nothing.

imageFilePath.description: The path of the written image file.

rotation.description: The orientation of the window in radian, as GetView2DTransformations reports it. Absent for the 3D window.

zoom.description: The zoom of the window the image shows, as GetView2DTransformations reports it. Absent for the 3D window.

SaveProject.description: Saves the currently opened project, in place or to a given path. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file at the path.
SaveProject.name: SaveProject

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. Only together with projectPath: false refuses to save when a file already exists at projectPath, the project's own file included, and writes nothing.

projectPath.description: Optional. Full path of a .pln file to save the project to, as File > Save As does: the open project then refers to that file. This saves an untitled project, or one opened from an older Archicad version, which cannot be saved in place. An existing file at the path is overwritten, unless overwrite is false. When omitted, or when it is the project's own file, the project is saved in place, which keeps the refusal of a project opened read-only.

SaveProjectAsArchive.description: Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.
SaveProjectAsArchive.name: SaveProjectAsArchive

archiveFilePath.description: Absolute path of the .pla archive to write. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false. The archive becomes the open project, as Save As does.

includeBackgroundPicture.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the background picture goes into the archive.

includeLibraryParts.description: Optional, true by default. Whether the library parts the project uses go into the archive, which makes the archive usable as a linked library of another project.

includeProperties.description: Optional, true by default. Whether the properties go into the archive.

includeTextures.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the linked textures go into the archive.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. false refuses to save when a file already exists at archiveFilePath, and writes nothing.

ScaleElements.description: Scales elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view by a factor around a center point with Archicad's Resize edit, in one undo step. Resize scales X and Y by the same ratio, so factorY, if given, must equal factor. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch and Hotspot. An element of another type (library parts such as objects, lamps, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain walls, shells, morphs, texts, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still scaled.
ScaleElements.name: ScaleElements

center.description: The fixed point of the scaling on the floor plan; every point of the elements moves away from it (factor > 1) or towards it (factor < 1).

elements.description: The elements to scale: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch or Hotspot, in the current database.

factor.description: The scale factor, greater than 0: 2 doubles the distances from the center, 0.5 halves them.

factorY.description: Optional scale factor in Y. Archicad's Resize scales X and Y by one ratio, so it must be the same as factor (or left out); a different value is refused.

ScreenToModel.description: Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel.
ScreenToModel.name: ScreenToModel

screenPoints.description: Pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates).

coordinates.description: One item per input screen point, in the same order: the 2D model coordinate in the current database (meters), or an error. This is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and in a 3D window the result is not a point of the model.

SearchFavorites.description: Searches project favorites by keyword (matching favorite name or folder) and/or element type.
SearchFavorites.name: SearchFavorites

elementType.description: Optional filter by element type. If omitted, searches across all element types.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching favorites to return.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to search in favorite name or folder hierarchy.

favorites.description: The matching Favorites, each with its element type and folder.

SearchLibraryParts.description: Finds the loaded library parts derived from an ancestor library part (by its unique ID) whose name matches a pattern with * wildcards. Archicad returns at most 50 of them.
SearchLibraryParts.name: SearchLibraryParts

ancestorUnId.description: The unique ID of the ancestor library part, '{main GUID}-{revision GUID}', as GetLibraryPartIdentities returns it. Only the library parts derived from it are found.

pattern.description: The name pattern to match, with * as wildcard, for example 'Chair*'. Use '*' to find every library part derived from the ancestor.

libraryParts.description: The library parts found. Archicad returns at most 50.

SearchProperties.description: Searches properties by name or group substring with optional filtering by property type, value type, and collection type.
SearchProperties.name: SearchProperties

collectionType.description: Optional filter by property collection type.

includeAvailability.description: If true, includes classification availability. Default is false to minimize token footprint.

includeEnumValues.description: If true, includes possibleEnumValues for enumeration properties. Default is false to minimize token footprint.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching properties to return.

propertyGroup.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter by property group name.

propertyType.description: Optional filter by property definition type.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to search in property name or property group name.

valueType.description: Optional filter by property value type.

properties.description: A list of property details matching the search criteria.

Set3DCutPlanes.description: Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.
Set3DCutPlanes.name: Set3DCutPlanes

cutPlanes.description: The cut planes. An empty array switches the 3D cut off. The side of a plane its normal vector points to is cut away and the other side is kept (to be confirmed in Archicad). pd is in meters.

Set3DCutawayStatus.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
Set3DCutawayStatus.name: Set3DCutawayStatus

cutawayEnabled.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on or off. Left unchanged when omitted.

cuttingPlanesVisible.description: Shows or hides the cutting planes. Left unchanged when omitted.

Set3DDocumentSettings.description: Changes the given settings of a 3D Document, given by its navigator item, in the form Get3DDocumentSettings returns; the settings not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change.
Set3DDocumentSettings.name: Set3DDocumentSettings

navigatorItemId.description: The navigator item of the 3D Document, from the Project Map or the View Map.

settings.description: The settings to change, in the form Get3DDocumentSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed; arrays other than elemTypeFilter are replaced.

attributeOptions.description: The uniform attributes of cut and uncut surfaces (API_UniformAttributeOptions). Pens and uniformLineType are indices; the enums fillCutSurfacesWith, uncutSurfaceFillType, hiddenEdgeVisibility and onCutPlaneVisibility are their integer values.

hiddenEdgeLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

shadFill.description: A fill. Missing when there is none.

boundaryLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

cutSetting.description: The 3D cut of the 3D Document (API_3DCutPlanesInfo). The cut planes themselves are not included.

customMater.description: The surface of the cut. Missing when there is none.

docSrc.description: Whether the 3D Document comes from the 3D window or from the floor plan.

filterAndCutSettings.description: Which elements and stories the 3D Document shows (API_3DFilterAndCutSettings). The marquee filter is not included.

allStories.description: Whether all stories are shown; if false, firstStory3D to lastStory3D.

elemTypeFilter.description: Whether each element type is shown. On Set only the listed element types are changed.

hiddenLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

projectionSetting.description: The projection of the 3D Document (API_3DProjectionInfo). persp is present when isPersp is true, axono otherwise. Changing isPersp starts the new projection from zero, give persp or axono with it.

actCamSet.description: The active Camera Set. Missing when there is none.

tranmat.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix, row by row.

camGuid.description: The Camera the projection comes from. Missing when there is none.

skeletonOptions.description: API_SkeletonOptions of a 3D Document made from the floor plan. viewSrc is the integer value of API_ViewSourceID.

settings.description: The settings of the 3D Document, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType.

attributeOptions.description: The uniform attributes of cut and uncut surfaces (API_UniformAttributeOptions). Pens and uniformLineType are indices; the enums fillCutSurfacesWith, uncutSurfaceFillType, hiddenEdgeVisibility and onCutPlaneVisibility are their integer values.

hiddenEdgeLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

shadFill.description: A fill. Missing when there is none.

boundaryLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

cutSetting.description: The 3D cut of the 3D Document (API_3DCutPlanesInfo). The cut planes themselves are not included.

customMater.description: The surface of the cut. Missing when there is none.

docSrc.description: Whether the 3D Document comes from the 3D window or from the floor plan.

filterAndCutSettings.description: Which elements and stories the 3D Document shows (API_3DFilterAndCutSettings). The marquee filter is not included.

allStories.description: Whether all stories are shown; if false, firstStory3D to lastStory3D.

elemTypeFilter.description: Whether each element type is shown. On Set only the listed element types are changed.

hiddenLineType.description: A line type. Missing when there is none.

projectionSetting.description: The projection of the 3D Document (API_3DProjectionInfo). persp is present when isPersp is true, axono otherwise. Changing isPersp starts the new projection from zero, give persp or axono with it.

actCamSet.description: The active Camera Set. Missing when there is none.

tranmat.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix, row by row.

camGuid.description: The Camera the projection comes from. Missing when there is none.

skeletonOptions.description: API_SkeletonOptions of a 3D Document made from the floor plan. viewSrc is the integer value of API_ViewSourceID.

Set3DFilterAndCutSettings.description: Changes the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window; only the given fields and the listed element types change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27.
Set3DFilterAndCutSettings.name: Set3DFilterAndCutSettings

rebuild.description: If true, Archicad drops the partial conversion data, so the next rebuild of the 3D window is a full one. Default: false.

settings.description: The settings to change, in the form Get3DFilterAndCutSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed.

allStories.description: Whether all stories are shown; if false, firstStory3D to lastStory3D.

elemTypeFilter.description: Whether each element type is shown. On Set only the listed element types are changed.

Set3DProjectionSettings.description: Sets a perspective or an axonometric projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter but sun is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. An axonometry changes only the values given: the projection type, the azimuth, the transformation matrix and the sun. The sun of either changes only the values given in it and is kept when sun is missing. The 3D window shows the change after a rebuild (RebuildView), e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.
Set3DProjectionSettings.name: Set3DProjectionSettings

axonometry.description: Makes the projection axonometric. Only the given values change, in sun too; the others are kept from the current axonometry, or from the last one when the projection is a perspective.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

sun.description: The sun position of the axonometry. Only the values given change.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers), as Get3DProjectionSettings returns it. Its 3x3 part must be invertible.

Set3DWindowSettings.description: Changes the pixel size of the 3D window and/or the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection; the values not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Archicad may need a rebuild of the 3D window (RebuildView) before it shows the change, e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.
Set3DWindowSettings.name: Set3DWindowSettings

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations.description: Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29.
SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations.name: SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations

activeDesignOptions.description: The list of active design options in the combination.

SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.description: Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30.
SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.name: SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination

parameters.description: The graphic override combination to apply, given by id or by name.

combinationId.description: The identifier of the graphic override combination, as returned by GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.

name.description: The name of the graphic override combination, as shown in Document > Graphic Overrides > Graphic Override Combinations.

SetActiveRenovationFilter.description: Sets the renovation filter of the current window (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter), given by its renovationFilterId from GetRenovationFilters or by its name. Saved views keep their own filter: change that with SetViewSettings.
SetActiveRenovationFilter.name: SetActiveRenovationFilter

name.description: Name of the renovation filter. An exact match wins over a case-insensitive one.

renovationFilterId.description: Identifier of the renovation filter, as listed by GetRenovationFilters. Takes precedence over name when both are given.

SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule.description: Sets the generation settings of the current Structural Analytical Model to no rules. Available from Archicad 27.
SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule.name: SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule

SetAnalyticalReleases.description: Replaces the releases of the given analytical members, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26.
SetAnalyticalReleases.name: SetAnalyticalReleases

releases.description: The element and its new release, as GetAnalyticalReleases returns it. The release replaces the element's release as a whole.

SetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings.description: Changes the given fields of the Structural Analytical Model visibility settings; the others keep their value. Available from Archicad 26.
SetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings.name: SetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings

visibilitySettings.description: The fields to change. The fields left out keep their current value.

SetArchicadVisibility.description: Hides or shows the Archicad application, e.g. to keep it out of the way while a batch runs. A script that hides Archicad must show it again, also when the script fails (e.g. in a finally block). Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
SetArchicadVisibility.name: SetArchicadVisibility

isVisible.description: True shows the Archicad application, false hides it.

SetAutoIntersect.description: Turns Auto-Intersection on or off. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project; remember to restore the previous state afterwards.
SetAutoIntersect.name: SetAutoIntersect

SetBuiltInPropertyValuesOfAttributes.description: Sets built-in property values of attributes, writing the values of each attribute together. Custom properties are refused; set them with SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes. Returns one execution result per value.
SetBuiltInPropertyValuesOfAttributes.name: SetBuiltInPropertyValuesOfAttributes

attributes.description: The attributes and the built-in property values to set on each.

executionResults.description: One result per given property value, attribute by attribute, in the order of the input. The values of one attribute are written together, so an error of that write is the result of each of them.

SetCategoryValuesOfElements.description: Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value in the category now (oldValue) and the value a real run would set (newValue).
SetCategoryValuesOfElements.name: SetCategoryValuesOfElements

elementCategoryValues.description: The category values to set: one element and one category per item. The same element can appear in several items, one per category.

executionResults.description: One result per item of the input, in the same order. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the category and the value exist, the element exists and has the category) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value in the category now and newValue the value a real run would set, both as GetCategoryValuesOfElements gives them (type, categoryId, categoryValueId and name; oldValue has only type and categoryId when the element has no value in the category). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

SetClassificationsOfAttributes.description: Sets the classifications of attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.). The given item replaces the attribute's current item in the same classification system. In order to set the classification of an attribute to unclassified in a system, omit the classificationItemId field.
SetClassificationsOfAttributes.name: SetClassificationsOfAttributes

attributeClassifications.description: The classifications to set, one per attribute and classification system.

SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.description: Sets the classifications of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types. In order to set a default to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field.
SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.name: SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults

elementDefaultClassifications.description: The classifications to set on the tool defaults (the settings new elements get).

SetClassificationsOfElements.description: Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's classification in the system now (oldValue) and the one a real run would set (newValue).
SetClassificationsOfElements.name: SetClassificationsOfElements

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementClassifications, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the classification item and its system exist, the element's classification in that system can be read) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's classificationId in the system now and newValue the one a real run would set, both as GetClassificationsOfElements gives them (without classificationItemId when the element is or would be unclassified in the system). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

SetCurrent3DStyle.description: Meant to make the given 3D style, one of the names Get3DStyles returns, the current one. Not available yet: it checks the name, then refuses, because Archicad's API function for it crashes Archicad.
SetCurrent3DStyle.name: SetCurrent3DStyle

styleName.description: The name of an existing 3D style, as Get3DStyles returns it.

SetCurrentRenderingScene.description: Makes the given rendering scene the current one, as selecting it in the PhotoRendering Settings palette does.
SetCurrentRenderingScene.name: SetCurrentRenderingScene

sceneName.description: The name of the rendering scene to make current, one of the names GetRenderingScenes returns.

SetCurrentTool.description: Activates a tool in the Toolbox, given as GetCurrentTool or GetToolboxItems returns it; an empty input activates the Arrow. Archicad switches the tool once it processes its events, so GetCurrentTool may still return the previous tool right after this command.
SetCurrentTool.name: SetCurrentTool

parameters.description: The tool to activate, in the form GetCurrentTool and GetToolboxItems return. An empty object activates the Arrow.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.description: Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable.
SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.name: SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale

rebuild.description: Rebuild the window after the scale changed (the API's zoom flag). Default: false.

scale.description: The denominator of the new drawing scale: 100 for 1:100, 20 for 1:20. Archicad accepts scales between 1 and 30000.

SetCustomCurveMemberStretch.description: Sets the lengths added to the start and end of the given curve members, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 29.
SetCustomCurveMemberStretch.name: SetCustomCurveMemberStretch

stretches.description: The element of the curve member and the lengths to add to it.

SetDefaultDesignOption.description: Sets the given design option as the default, or the Main Model when no design option is given. Available from Archicad 29.
SetDefaultDesignOption.name: SetDefaultDesignOption

designOptionId.description: The design option to set as the default. When it is not given, the Main Model becomes the default.

SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews.description: Sets the design option combination the given views show, or makes them show only the main model. Available from Archicad 27.
SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews.name: SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews

navigatorItemIdsWithCombination.description: The views (View Map navigator items), each with either a 'designOptionCombinationId' or 'mainModelOnly': true.

designOptionCombinationId.description: The design option combination the view should show.

mainModelOnly.description: Set it to true to make the view show only the main model, without any design option.

SetDetailsOfElements.description: Sets the details of the given elements. Every element type: Element ID (id), story (floorIndex), layer (layerIndex) and display order (drawIndex). In typeSpecificDetails: Wall - start and end point, height, base offset, and the start and end thickness of a trapezoid wall; Zone - the ZoneSettings fields (the same as ModifyZones); Line - start and end point, pen, line type, room separator; Arc and Circle - origin, radius, angle, ratio, start and end angle (arcs only), reflected, pen, line type, room separator; Polyline - points and arcs, pen, line type, room separator; Spline - pen, line type, room separator; Hatch - outline, holes, contour pen, fill pen and background pen or colors, fill or building material, area display, room special and fill orientation; Hotspot - position, height, pen; Text - text, position, angle, height, justification; Label - the text of a text label; Drawing - position, angle, ratio, model offset, clip polygon (isCutWithFrame), name, ID and numbering, scale in Autotext, border, title library part, pen table (penTableUsageMode, penTableIndex), colorMode, isTransparentBackground, rasterizeDPI and the anchor (anchorPoint, useOwnOriginAsAnchor). Not written, because the Archicad API does not take them: the geometry of a Spline, the source of a Drawing (use ChangeDrawingLink), the Drawing Manager's update type and stored in project, and often a placed Drawing's drawingScale, which comes from its source view (the element's result then names the kept value). Other wall, slab, column, beam, stair and object settings are written by their Modify commands. An element Archicad does not let you edit (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not reserved by you in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason; a Drawing setting Archicad kept unchanged is named in a failed execution result too.
SetDetailsOfElements.name: SetDetailsOfElements

id.description: The Element ID (the ID field of the element's Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels). The same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id.

SetDialogAutoClose.description: Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it.
SetDialogAutoClose.name: SetDialogAutoClose

enabled.description: True turns the dialog auto close on: Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user. False turns it off.

SetDocumentFrom3DDefaults.description: Sets the defaults a newly created 3D Document starts with. Only the given fields are changed; existing 3D Documents are not affected. The fields are the ones returned by GetDocumentFrom3DDefaults.
SetDocumentFrom3DDefaults.name: SetDocumentFrom3DDefaults

parameters.description: Only the given fields are changed, the rest keep their current default.

boundaryLineType.description: The index of the line type of the boundary contours, used with OverrideContours.

boundaryPen.description: The pen of the boundary contours, used with OverrideContours.

cMater.description: The index of the uniform surface (material), used when materialFrom3D is false.

materialFrom3D.description: Use the surfaces of the 3D model; when false, cMater is used for every element.

name.description: The name of a new 3D Document.

refId.description: The reference ID of a new 3D Document.

SetElementInfoStrings.description: Sets the info string of the given elements: the Element ID shown in the Info Box, which GetDetailsOfElements returns as id. Returns one execution result per element.
SetElementInfoStrings.name: SetElementInfoStrings

SetElementNotificationClient.description: Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.
SetElementNotificationClient.name: SetElementNotificationClient

elementTypesToObserve.description: Only modifications/deletions of elements of these types are observed and notified to this client. Optional parameter, by default every element (including the parts of curtain walls, stairs and railings, which are most of the elements of large projects). Registering the same client again with other types changes them; only the elements of types no client observed before get an observer then. Does not limit the other notifications.

host.description: The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.

notifyOn3DSettingsChanges.description: Notify when the settings of the 3D window change (projection, Filter and Cut Elements in 3D, 3D window settings). The message is {"view3DSettingsChanged": {}}; read the new settings with the commands of the 3D window. The changes made while navigating in 3D are not notified. Available from Archicad 30: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeChanges.description: Notify when attributes (layers, fills, composites, surfaces, building materials, ...) are created, modified or deleted. The message is {"attributesChanged": {"event": ..., "attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and attributeIds are the attributes, as in the response of GetAttributesByType (a deleted attribute no longer exists). Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeReplacement.description: Notify when attributes are deleted and replaced by other attributes of the same type (for example Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager). The message is {"replacedAttributes": [{"attributeType": ..., "oldIndex": ..., "newIndex": ..., "newAttributeId": ...}, ...]}: attributeType is one of the type names of GetAttributesByType ("Layer", "Line", "Fill", "Composite", "Surface", "LayerCombination", "ZoneCategory", "Profile", "PenTable", "MEPSystem", "OperationProfile", "BuildingMaterial", or "Unknown"), oldIndex is the index of the replaced attribute and newIndex the index of the attribute that replaces it, newAttributeId is the attributeId of that attribute, missing when it cannot be found. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnClassificationChanges.description: Notify when classification systems or classification items are created, modified or deleted. The messages are {"classificationSystemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationSystemIds": [{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"classificationItemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationItemIds": [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllClassificationSystems and GetAllClassificationsInSystem. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnLockableReservationChanges.description: Notify when a Teamwork lockable object set (the non-element things Teamwork reserves: the attributes of a type, favorites, model view options, project info, project preferences, ...) is reserved or released, by anyone, including the current user. The message is {"lockableReservationChanged": {"event": ..., "objectSetId": {"guid": ...}, "objectSetName": ..., "reservedBy": ..., "reservedByUserId": ...}}: event is "Reserved" or "Released", objectSetId is the guid of the object set, objectSetName its name as objectSetName of ReserveLockableObjectSet (for example "Composites", "LayerSettingsDialog" or "Favorites"), missing when it is not one of the documented sets, and reservedBy and reservedByUserId are the name and the Teamwork user id of the member who reserved it, only for "Reserved". Element reservations are notified by notifyOnReservationChanges. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnMarqueeChange.description: Notify when the marquee is drawn, changed or removed. The message is {"marqueeChanged": {"type": ..., "multiStory": ...}}: type is "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon" or, when the marquee was removed, "none", as type of GetMarquee, which returns the shape of the marquee; multiStory is missing for "none". Available from Archicad 27: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnModificationOfAnElement.description: Notify on modification/deletion of an element. The observed elements are the ones ACAPI_Element_GetElemList returns, for API_ZombieElemID or, with elementTypesToObserve, for each of those types, when the first client asking for these notifications of them is registered, and every element of the observed types created after that. Archicad does not report the changes made by Tapir's own commands, so Tapir reports them itself for SetDetailsOfElements, SetPropertyValuesOfElements, MoveElements, RotateElements, MirrorElements (not for the copies they make, which are new elements), DeleteElements, DeleteSelectedElements, the Modify<Tool> commands (ModifyWalls, ModifyBeams, ModifySlabs, ModifyColumns, ModifyWindows, ModifyDoors, ModifyOpenings, ModifyMorphs, ModifyRoofs, ModifyShells, ModifyMeshes, ModifyObjects, ModifyLamps, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels, ModifyCurtainWalls, ModifyCurtainWallFrames, ModifyZones, ModifySections, ModifyDetailMarkers, ModifyRailings, ModifyStairs), ChangeTextContent, SetGDLParametersOfElements, RunParameterScriptOfElements (only when the script changed the element), SetMarkerParametersOfElements, SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements, ChangeLibraryPartOfElements, SetClassificationsOfElements, SetCategoryValuesOfElements, ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, SetElementInfoStrings, SetURLReferencesOfElements, SetIFCAttributesOfElements, SetIFCPropertiesOfElements, RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements, SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, LockElements, UnlockElements, SetOpeningDetails, SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, SetOpeningSymbolParameters, CreateGroups and UngroupElements (the grouped elements), MoveElementsToDesignOptions, CreateSolidElementLinks, RemoveSolidElementLinks, CreateSolidOperations (the target and operator when the operation changed or deleted them; the results are new elements), TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims, MergeElements, UnmergeElements, ModifyMEPRoutingElements, ModifyMEPPorts (the element owning the port), ConnectMEPElements, ModifyMEPElements, SetMEPRoutingParameters, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalDevices and ConnectToElectricalCircuits. Of the elements these commands change, only the given ones are reported: an element deleted together with its owner (a door or window of a deleted wall) is not. UpdateZones is not reported by Tapir, because Archicad updates the Zones after the command has returned. When the user moves, rotates, mirrors, elevates, resizes or stretches elements in Archicad, each of their changedElements items also has a transformation: {"type": ..., ...}, where type is "Drag" (with displacement: {"x", "y", "z"}), "Elevate" (with displacement, only z is not 0), "Rotate" (with origin: {"x", "y"} and angle, in radians, counterclockwise), "Mirror" (with origin, a point of the mirror axis, and axisDirection: {"x", "y"}, its unit vector), "Resize" (with origin and ratio), "Stretch", "VerticalStretch", "PreservedHeightStretch", "PreservedDirectionStretch" or "General"; the changes made by Tapir's own commands and by undo or redo have no transformation. Optional parameter, by default true. Archicad attaches an observer to each element to observe (see elementTypesToObserve) when the first client asks for this, and detaches them when the last one stops, and it is blocked meanwhile: the time grows faster than the number of elements, from seconds for a few hundred elements to many minutes for a few thousand. Count the elements first (GetAllElements with IncludeSubElemObjects, or GetElementsByType) and limit the types on large projects.

notifyOnNewElement.description: Notify on creation of a new element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnProjectEvents.description: Notify on project events. The message is {"projectEvent": ...}, one of "New", "NewAndReset", "Open", "Close", "Quit", "SendChanges" (a Teamwork send is about to start) and "ReceiveChanges" (Teamwork changes were received). The client stays registered when the project is closed or another one is opened. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges.description: Notify when property groups or property definitions are created, modified or deleted (property values of elements are notified as changedElements by notifyOnModificationOfAnElement). The messages are {"propertyGroupsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyGroupIds": [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"propertyDefinitionsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllProperties. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnReservationChanges.description: Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnSelectionChange.description: Notify when the selection changes. The message is {"selectedElements": [...]}: the whole current selection, each item an elementId as in the response of GetSelectedElements, an empty list when nothing is selected. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolChange.description: Notify when the user switches to another tool in the Toolbox. The message is {"toolChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type of the new tool, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), "None" for the Arrow and the Marquee, and "Unknown" for a tool Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolDefaultChanges.description: Notify when the default settings of a tool change (for example the user changes the settings of the Wall tool with no wall selected), so a client can read the new defaults. The message is {"toolDefaultsChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type whose defaults changed, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), and "Unknown" for a type Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnViewEvents.description: Notify when an item of the Project Navigator or the Organizer is inserted (for example a view is saved or a layout is created), modified (for example renamed), deleted or opened. The message is {"viewEvent": {"event": ..., "navigatorMapId": ..., "navigatorItemId": {"guid": ...}}}: event is one of "Inserted", "Modified", "Deleted" and "Opened", navigatorMapId is the navigator map of the item, one of "ProjectMap", "PublicViewMap", "MyViewMap", "LayoutBook" and "PublisherSets" (as navigatorMapId of GetNavigatorItemTree), and navigatorItemId is the guid of the navigator item, as in the response of GetNavigatorItemTree (a deleted item no longer exists). Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnWindowChange.description: Notify when the current (active) window changes or the user switches to another story. The message is {"windowChanged": {"event": "Window" or "Floor", "windowType": ..., "databaseId": ..., "storyIndex": ...}}: windowType and databaseId describe the new current window as in the response of GetCurrentWindowType (databaseId is missing when that response has none), storyIndex is the active story, missing when it cannot be read. Optional parameter, by default false.

port.description: The port number of the notification client.

SetElementUserData.description: Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved.
SetElementUserData.name: SetElementUserData

elementUserData.description: The elements with the key-value pairs to store on them. Each item needs userData, keysToDelete or both.

keysToDelete.description: The keys to remove from the element. A key the element does not hold is ignored.

userData.description: The key-value pairs to store on the element. A key that already exists on the element gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

key.description: The key of the value. Scripts should prefix their keys (for example 'myscript.databaseId') so that different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

value.description: The value to store. Any text, for example an id, a timestamp or a JSON document the script encodes itself.

executionResults.description: One result per input item, in the input order.

SetGDLDate.description: Sets the date GDL scripts see: year, month, day, hour, minute and second, as GetGDLDate returns them. Useful to test date-dependent library parts; set the value read with GetGDLDate back to restore it.
SetGDLDate.name: SetGDLDate

date.description: The date GDL scripts should see, in the format GetGDLDate returns.

SetGDLParametersOfElements.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour, which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created: the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their old and new values.
SetGDLParametersOfElements.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementsWithGDLParameters, in the order of the input. On a dry run the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, but the element is not changed. An element that passes every check made before changing it (the element and its parameters exist, every value is valid for its parameter, the element is editable) gets wouldChange: oldValue and newValue list the parameters a real run would change - the ones given and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them - before and after, each with name, index, type and value as GetGDLParametersOfElements gives them. Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

SetGeoLocation.description: Sets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26). Omitted fields stay unchanged.
SetGeoLocation.name: SetGeoLocation

SetGhostStorySettings.description: Sets the Trace & Reference ghost story settings of the floor plan through its ghost record, which is created when the floor plan has none. Every field is optional; the ones left out keep their value, and without a story choice the current reference is kept.
SetGhostStorySettings.name: SetGhostStorySettings

parameters.description: Every field is optional; the ones left out keep their current value. A story choice (showOne, showAbove or showBelow true) replaces the current reference, whatever it is; without one the reference is kept, also when it is another view (a section, an elevation, a worksheet).

filter.description: The element types to show in the ghost story; the others are hidden.

ghostColor.description: The color to draw the ghost story in.

on.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the ghost story on the floor plan.

showAbove.description: Show the story above the current one as the ghost story.

showBelow.description: Show the story below the current one as the ghost story.

showOne.description: Show the story at storyIndex as the ghost story.

storyIndex.description: The index of the story to show when showOne is true, as GetStories reports it.

SetGraphicOverrideRuleGroupOrder.description: Sets the order of the graphic override rule groups, found by name. The groups not listed keep their order and follow the listed ones. Available from Archicad 27.
SetGraphicOverrideRuleGroupOrder.name: SetGraphicOverrideRuleGroupOrder

ruleGroupNames.description: The names of the rule groups in their new order. The groups not listed keep their order and follow the listed ones.

SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder.description: Sets the order of the rules in graphic override rule groups, found by name. The listed rules come first, in the given order; the other rules of the group keep their order after them. Available from Archicad 27.
SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder.name: SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder

graphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: The rule groups to reorder, in the shape GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups returns them.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The rules of the group in their new order. Each must be a rule of this group, listed once. The listed rules come first, in this order; the rules of the group that are not listed keep their order after them.

name.description: The name of the rule group.

SetGridSettings.description: Changes the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window; only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27.
SetGridSettings.name: SetGridSettings

settings.description: The grid settings to change, in the form GetGridSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed; a color may give only some of its components.

backColor.description: A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1. Archicad keeps 8 bits per component, so a value that is set is rounded to the nearest 1/255.

gridAngle.description: The rotation angle of the grid.

gridColor.description: A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1. Archicad keeps 8 bits per component, so a value that is set is rounded to the nearest 1/255.

gridOffsX.description: The X offset of the grid.

gridOffsY.description: The Y offset of the grid.

gridOffsZ.description: The Z offset of the grid.

nLineAuxX.description: The number of horizontal auxiliary grid lines.

nLineAuxY.description: The number of vertical auxiliary grid lines.

nLineMainX.description: The number of main horizontal grid lines.

nLineMainY.description: The number of main vertical grid lines.

snapOffsX.description: The horizontal offset of the snap grid, in meters.

snapOffsY.description: The vertical offset of the snap grid, in meters.

snapStepX.description: The horizontal spacing of the snap grid, in meters.

snapStepY.description: The vertical spacing of the snap grid, in meters.

spaceAuxX.description: The horizontal spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.

spaceAuxY.description: The vertical spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.

spaceMainX.description: The horizontal spacing of the main grid, in meters.

spaceMainY.description: The vertical spacing of the main grid, in meters.

status.description: The status of the grid, as Archicad stores it.

SetHotlinkDesignOptionTables.description: Sets the filter mode, the active combination and the active option of sets in the design option table of the given placed hotlink instances. Available from Archicad 29.
SetHotlinkDesignOptionTables.name: SetHotlinkDesignOptionTables

hotlinkInstances.description: The placed hotlink instances to change the design option table of. Every field but elementId is optional; what is omitted keeps its current value. The changes are applied in the order filterMode, activeDesignOptionCombination, activeDesignOptions.

activeDesignOptionCombination.description: The name of the combination to activate, one of designOptionCombinations from GetHotlinkDesignOptionTables. An empty string deactivates the active combination.

activeDesignOptions.description: The option to activate in each given set; the previously active option of the set is deactivated. Sets that are not listed keep their active option.

designOptionName.description: The name of the option to activate in the set. An empty string deactivates every option of the set.

filterMode.description: Which elements of the hotlinked module are shown: only its main model, the main model and the active option of each set, or the main model and the options of the active combination.

SetIFCAttributesOfElements.description: Sets the values of IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of elements. The attribute must be one GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element; its IFC value type is kept. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.
SetIFCAttributesOfElements.name: SetIFCAttributesOfElements

elementIFCAttributeValues.description: The IFC attribute values to set.

SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements.description: Stores IFC classification references (identification, name, location and the referenced classification with its name, edition, edition date, description and location) on elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.
SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements.name: SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

elementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references to store on the elements.

SetIFCPropertiesOfElements.description: Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.
SetIFCPropertiesOfElements.name: SetIFCPropertiesOfElements

elementIFCPropertyValues.description: The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.

SetLast3DDefaultLevels.description: Sets the last 3D default levels of the given element types' defaults.
SetLast3DDefaultLevels.name: SetLast3DDefaultLevels

elementTypes.description: The element types to set the last 3D default level of.

levels.description: The new last 3D default level of each element type, in the order of elementTypes, in meters.

SetLayerOfElementDefaults.description: Sets the layer of the tool defaults of the given element types, so new elements of that type are placed on it. Only the layer of the defaults is changed.
SetLayerOfElementDefaults.name: SetLayerOfElementDefaults

layersOfElementDefaults.description: The element types whose tool defaults get a new layer.

layerId.description: The layer new elements of this type will be placed on.

executionResults.description: One result per item, in the input order.

SetLayoutSettings.description: Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. In Teamwork the layout settings must be reserved first in Archicad (Layout Book > Reserve Layout Settings); the Archicad API cannot reserve them, and ReserveElements does not. GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases shows who holds a layout.
SetLayoutSettings.name: SetLayoutSettings

layoutName.description: The new name of the layout or master layout (its database name, as returned by GetDatabases and GetLayoutSettings). A custom name of its Navigator item is changed with RenameNavigatorItem instead.

masterLayoutDatabaseId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its database. Used when masterNavigatorItemId is not given.

masterLayoutName.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, by name. Used when neither masterNavigatorItemId nor masterLayoutDatabaseId is given.

masterNavigatorItemId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its Layout Book navigator item. Only layouts can be given a master layout, master layouts cannot.

SetLibraries.description: Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear.
SetLibraries.name: SetLibraries

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

SetLibraryPartCustomSection.description: Creates, replaces or deletes a custom section of a loaded library part. The content is given as base64. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartCustomSection.name: SetLibraryPartCustomSection

data.description: The new content of the section, base64 encoded. The section is created when it does not exist, otherwise replaced. Give either data or delete.

dataVersion.description: Optional. The data version stored with the section. By default 0. Only used with data.

delete.description: When true, the section is deleted. Give either data or delete.

index.description: Optional. The index of the section among the sections with the same identifier. By default 0.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

sectionId.description: The type identifier of the custom section. A four-character code is given as its integer value, the first character in the highest byte (e.g. 'ABCD' is 1094861636).

SetLibraryPartMetadata.description: Sets the author, keywords, license, license version, password and the placeable, UI default, subtype and hierarchical pages flags of loaded library parts. Only the given fields are changed. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartMetadata.name: SetLibraryPartMetadata

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify and the metadata to set in each.

SetLibraryPartParameters.description: Sets the parameter values, and optionally the parameter descriptions, of loaded library parts, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed; with merge, the changed list is merged into the parameters of the part instead of replacing them. A library part that is not editable, or with an invalid value given, is left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartParameters.name: SetLibraryPartParameters

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify and the parameter values to set in each.

descriptions.description: The new descriptions of all parameters of the library part, one for each parameter in the order of its parameter list. Defaults to the current descriptions.

merge.description: When true, the changed parameter list is merged into the parameters of the library part (MergeParameters of the Archicad API) instead of replacing them (SetParameters). Defaults to false.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

parameters.description: The GDL parameters to change, by name, in the format SetGDLParametersOfElements uses. The parameters left out are not changed.

index1.description: The 1-based first index of the one item of an array parameter to change. Only with a single value.

index2.description: The 1-based second index of the item to change, only together with index1. Defaults to 1.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

value.description: The new value, in the format the parameter list was read in. For an array parameter without index1, a list of all of its items, flat (the first index outer) or as a list of rows; resizing an array is not supported.

SetLibraryPartPictureImages.description: Sets the preview picture and the GDL pictures of a loaded library part from base64 encoded PNGs, and from Archicad 29 also their dark user interface variants. All pictures are set in one step; an invalid picture changes nothing. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartPictureImages.name: SetLibraryPartPictureImages

darkGdlPictures.description: Optional. The new GDL pictures for the dark user interface, each a base64 encoded PNG. They replace all dark GDL pictures of the library part. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

darkPreviewPicture.description: Optional. The new preview picture for the dark user interface as a base64 encoded PNG. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

gdlPictures.description: Optional. The new GDL pictures, each a base64 encoded PNG. They replace all GDL pictures of the library part.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

previewPicture.description: Optional. The new preview picture as a base64 encoded PNG.

SetLibraryPartPictures.description: Deletes the preview picture, the GDL pictures (and from Archicad 29 their dark variants) or the 2D symbol of a loaded library part, or copies the 2D symbol from another library part. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartPictures.name: SetLibraryPartPictures

copy2DSymbolFrom.description: Optional. The name of another loaded library part (fileName with extension); its 2D symbol (the drawn 2D vector image) replaces this part's 2D symbol.

delete2DSymbol.description: Optional. When true, the 2D symbol (the drawn 2D vector image) is deleted. Cannot be combined with copy2DSymbolFrom.

deleteDarkGdlPictures.description: Optional. When true, all GDL pictures for the dark user interface are deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

deleteDarkPreviewPicture.description: Optional. When true, the preview picture for the dark user interface is deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

deleteGdlPictures.description: Optional. When true, all GDL pictures are deleted.

deletePreviewPicture.description: Optional. When true, the preview picture is deleted.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

SetLibraryPartScripts.description: Sets and deletes the master, parameter, 2D, 3D, properties, interface and forward and backward migration scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty, deleteScripts removes it. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.
SetLibraryPartScripts.name: SetLibraryPartScripts

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify, with the scripts to set and to delete in each.

SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements.description: Sets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, and which one is assigned individually (0 removes the individual assignment). A link that is not given stays unchanged. All changes are made in one undoable step.
SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements.name: SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements

elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.description: The property object links to set, each for an element or for the element defaults of an element type. A link that is not given stays unchanged.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element.

elementType.description: Set the links of the element defaults of this type instead of an element.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element defaults individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element defaults.

SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.description: Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27.
SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.name: SetMEPPreferenceTableRows

rows.description: The rows to change. Only the given values are set.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

SetMEPRoutingParameters.description: Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, with one execution result per element. A changed preference table is also set on each of the route's segments and nodes and injected into them, because Archicad 29 can otherwise keep the old one; the item fails if they still report the old table. Available from Archicad 28.
SetMEPRoutingParameters.name: SetMEPRoutingParameters

elements.description: The routing parameters to change. Only the given keys are changed. An item gives either routingNodeParameters and/or routingSegmentParameters for a routing element, or elbowParameters and/or transitionParameters for a routing node.

SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements.description: Changes which library part the marker of the given Window and Door elements uses, given by its name (find the available ones with GetAvailableLibraryParts); only a marker library part for the opening's type is accepted. The marker gets the new library part's default parameters, which SetMarkerParametersOfElements can change afterwards; the opening's own settings are left as they are.
SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements.name: SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements

elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part their marker should use.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part the marker should use, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements and GetAvailableLibraryParts report it. It has to be a marker library part: Archicad's marker parent for windows or doors, or a library part derived from it. Any other library part is refused.

SetMarkerParametersOfElements.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.
SetMarkerParametersOfElements.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

markerParameters.description: The marker parameters to change, each given by name or by index. The other marker parameters and the opening's own settings are left as they are.

name.description: The name of the marker parameter.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter: a number for the numeric types (Integer, Length, Angle, RealNumber, PenColor, LineType, Material, FillPattern, BuildingMaterial, Profile, RGBColor, Intensity), a string for String and Title, true/false for Boolean and 'On'/'Off' for LightSwitch. Array parameters are not supported.

index.description: The index of the marker parameter, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements reports it.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter, see the value given with a name.

SetMarquee.description: Draws a marquee in the current window from a polygon or a box (optionally rotated), single- or multi-story. Called without polygon and box it removes the marquee.
SetMarquee.name: SetMarquee

box.description: A rectangle marquee. With rotationAngle it is a rotated rectangle, and the box is read the way Archicad stores it (see GetMarquee): in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin. Give either polygon or box.

multiStory.description: True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. The default is false.

polygon.description: The vertices of a polygon marquee, in order. The polygon is closed automatically; a repeated first vertex at the end is accepted. Give either polygon or box.

rotationAngle.description: Rotation angle (radians) of the box around the project origin. Only together with box. The default is 0: a horizontal rectangle.

SetMasterLayoutContext.description: Sets which layout's context the master layout of the current window is drawn in: its autotexts then show the values of the given layout. The current window must be a master layout, otherwise an error is returned. It does not assign a master layout to a layout. Available from Archicad 27.
SetMasterLayoutContext.name: SetMasterLayoutContext
