SetOpeningDefault.description: Changes the settings of the Opening tool defaults, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. Only the given settings change. Available from Archicad 29.
SetOpeningDefault.name: SetOpeningDefault

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

constraint.description: How the opening's orientation is constrained.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

height.description: The opening's height. See linkedStatus.

limitType.description: How far the opening's extrusion reaches.

linkedStatus.description: Whether the opening's width and height are linked. While they are linked, giving both width and height makes a square of the height; give NotLinked with them to get a different width and height.

shapeType.description: The shape of the opening's polygon.

width.description: The opening's width. See linkedStatus.

floorPlanParameters.description: The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.

clearCutSymbol.description: Removes the cut symbol. Cannot be given together with cutSymbolLibPartId.

clearUnCutSymbol.description: Removes the uncut symbol. Cannot be given together with unCutSymbolLibPartId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

dividedOpeningMode.description: How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.

floorPlanDisplayMode.description: How the opening is shown on the floor plan.

openEdgeStyle.description: How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

elementType.description: The type of the elements the changed settings are the defaults of.

SetOpeningDetails.description: Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.
SetOpeningDetails.name: SetOpeningDetails

openingsWithDetails.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.

addCutElements.description: Elements the opening should cut as well.

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

constraint.description: How the opening's orientation is constrained.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

height.description: The opening's height. See linkedStatus.

limitType.description: How far the opening's extrusion reaches.

linkedStatus.description: Whether the opening's width and height are linked. While they are linked, giving both width and height makes a square of the height; give NotLinked with them to get a different width and height.

shapeType.description: The shape of the opening's polygon.

width.description: The opening's width. See linkedStatus.

parentElementId.description: The new element the opening belongs to.

polygon.description: The new polygon of the opening, in the plane of the xAxis and yAxis returned by GetOpeningDetails.

removeCutElements.description: Elements the opening should no longer cut.

transformation.description: A transformation applied to the opening's geometry: a 3x4 matrix of 12 numbers, row by row, the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers being the translation along X, Y and Z. For example [1,0,0,1, 0,1,0,0, 0,0,1,0] moves the opening by 1 along X.

SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters.description: Changes the floor plan parameters of Opening elements returned by GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, and sets or removes their cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29.
SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters.name: SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters

floorPlanParameters.description: The floor plan parameters to change, with the names GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns. The ones left out are not changed.

clearCutSymbol.description: Removes the cut symbol of the opening. Cannot be given together with cutSymbolLibPartId.

clearUnCutSymbol.description: Removes the uncut symbol of the opening. Cannot be given together with unCutSymbolLibPartId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

dividedOpeningMode.description: How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.

floorPlanDisplayMode.description: How the opening is shown on the floor plan.

openEdgeStyle.description: How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

SetOpeningSymbolParameters.description: Changes the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed. Available from Archicad 29.
SetOpeningSymbolParameters.name: SetOpeningSymbolParameters

cutSymbolParameters.description: The GDL parameters to change, by name, in the format SetGDLParametersOfElements uses. The parameters left out are not changed.

index1.description: The 1-based first index of the one item of an array parameter to change. Only with a single value.

index2.description: The 1-based second index of the item to change, only together with index1. Defaults to 1.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

value.description: The new value, in the format the parameter list was read in. For an array parameter without index1, a list of all of its items, flat (the first index outer) or as a list of rows; resizing an array is not supported.

unCutSymbolParameters.description: The GDL parameters to change, by name, in the format SetGDLParametersOfElements uses. The parameters left out are not changed.

index1.description: The 1-based first index of the one item of an array parameter to change. Only with a single value.

index2.description: The 1-based second index of the item to change, only together with index1. Defaults to 1.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

value.description: The new value, in the format the parameter list was read in. For an array parameter without index1, a list of all of its items, flat (the first index outer) or as a list of rows; resizing an array is not supported.

SetPens.description: Changes the color, width and description of the given pens in effect in the current window, the pens GetPens returns, in one undo step. Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed; each pen gets its own execution result. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27.
SetPens.name: SetPens

pens.description: The pens to change among the pens in effect in the current window, the ones GetPens returns. Only the given fields (color, width, description) of a listed pen are changed.

SetPlaceSettings.description: Changes the place settings of the project: location (longitude, latitude, altitude, north), date, time, summer time and time zone. Only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back, with the sun position Archicad calculated for them. Available from Archicad 27.
SetPlaceSettings.name: SetPlaceSettings

placeInfo.description: The place settings read back after the change. sunAngXY and sunAngZ are the sun position Archicad calculated for the place, date and time, in radians.

SetProjectData.description: Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data.
SetProjectData.name: SetProjectData

values.description: The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

SetProjectInfoField.description: Sets the value of a project info field.
SetProjectInfoField.name: SetProjectInfoField

projectInfoId.description: The id of the project info field.

projectInfoValue.description: The new value of the project info field. An empty string clears the field.

SetProjectNotes.description: Changes the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes). Only the given fields are changed; texts longer than the field Archicad stores are truncated. architect and draftsmen are full names that Archicad keeps as name parts: a new name is stored in the given name with the other parts cleared, and the parts of a name that is not given or not changed are kept.
SetProjectNotes.name: SetProjectNotes

architect.description: Architect: the full name of the Project Info contact. Archicad keeps it as name parts (title prefix, given, middle and family name, title suffix); SetProjectNotes puts a new value into the given name and clears the other parts, so it reads back unchanged. Use SetProjectInfoField to set the parts.

dateOfIssue.description: Date of issue (free text, as typed in Project Notes).

draftsmen.description: Draftsmen: the full name of the Project Info CAD technician, kept as name parts like architect.

SetProjectPreferences.description: Changes pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units, the zones and the reference levels, and the Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings. Only the given fields change, the rest of each page keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27.
SetProjectPreferences.name: SetProjectPreferences

parameters.description: The pages to change, by name. Only the given fields of a page change, the rest keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet).

calculationUnits.description: The Calculation Units page: the units, the number of decimals and the extra accuracy of the values in element lists and schedules. GetCalculationUnits answers the same page.

decimals.description: Number of decimals to display for angle values.
Number of decimals to display for area values.
Number of decimals to display for length values.
Number of decimals to display for volume values.

dimensions.description: The Dimensions page: the dimension standard and the format (unit, decimals, extra accuracy and zero handling) of each dimension type.

angle.description: The format of the angle dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

area.description: The format of the area values the dimensions show (area calculations).

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

dimensionStandardIndex.description: The index of the dimension standard the page follows.

doorWindow.description: The format of the door, window and skylight dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

elevation.description: The format of the elevation dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

level.description: The format of the level dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

linear.description: The format of the linear dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

parapet.description: The format of the sill height (parapet) dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

radial.description: The format of the radial dimensions.

hideZeroDecimals.description: Hide the zero decimals at the end of the values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

showZeroInch.description: Show zero inches in feet and inches values.

showZeroWhole.description: Show the zero before the decimal point of values below one.

floorPlanCutPlane.description: The Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings (Document > Floor Plan Cut Plane): where the floor plan cuts the model and which range of it the floor plan shows.

absoluteDisplayLimit.description: The absolute display limit from Project Zero in meters: elements set to show on the floor plan down to the absolute display limit are shown down to this level.

bottomLevel.description: The bottom of the floor plan range: elements are shown down to this level.

offset.description: The offset of the level from that story in meters.

relativeStory.description: The story the level is measured from, relative to the current story: 0 is the current story, 1 the story above it, -1 the story below it.

cutPlaneHeight.description: The height of the cut plane from the current story in meters.

topLevel.description: The top of the floor plan range: elements are shown up to this level.

offset.description: The offset of the level from that story in meters.

relativeStory.description: The story the level is measured from, relative to the current story: 0 is the current story, 1 the story above it, -1 the story below it.

referenceLevels.description: The Reference Levels page: two named levels that elevations can be measured from, besides Project Zero and the stories.

elevation.description: The elevation of the reference level from Project Zero in meters.

name.description: The name of the reference level, e.g. Sea Level.

elevation.description: The elevation of the reference level from Project Zero in meters.

name.description: The name of the reference level, e.g. Sea Level.

workingUnits.description: The Working Units page: the units and the number of decimals the model's lengths, areas, volumes and angles are shown with.

decimals.description: Number of decimals to display for angle values.
Number of decimals to display for area values.
Number of decimals to display for length values.

roundInch.description: Rounding of the fractional inch units, as the denominator of the smallest fraction shown: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

decimals.description: Number of decimals to display for volume values.

zones.description: The Zones page: the reduction of the calculated zone area under a low ceiling. The wall inset (niche) sizes of the page are not available through the API.

lowCeilingAreaReduction.description: Up to three ceiling height limits split a zone into height ranges; the area of each range is reduced by its own percent in the calculated area of the zone.

activeHeightLimits.description: How many of the three height limits are in use: 0 (no reduction) to 3.

heightLimits.description: The three height limits, each with the reduction of the area under it (and above the previous limit); the first activeHeightLimits of them are in use. In SetProjectPreferences the given items change the limits of the same index.

height.description: The ceiling height limit in meters.

reductionPercent.description: The reduction of the area under this limit, in percent.

reductionPercentAboveHeightLimits.description: The reduction of the area above the highest height limit, in percent.

returns.description: One execution result per page given in the input, by name.

SetPropertyValueOfAttributes.description: Sets one property value on several attributes (for example Building Materials) in one undo step. If the property is not available for any of the given attributes, no attribute is changed.
SetPropertyValueOfAttributes.name: SetPropertyValueOfAttributes

attributeIds.description: The attributes to set the value on. The property must be available for every one of them.

SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes.description: Sets the property values of attributes.
SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes.name: SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes

SetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults.description: Sets the property values of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of element types, so every element placed afterwards gets them, without saving and applying a favorite.
SetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults.name: SetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults

elementDefaultPropertyValues.description: The property values to set on the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of element types.

items.description: A property value with the identifier of the property and the element type whose defaults own it.

SetPropertyValuesOfElements.description: Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With valueStatus an element's value can also be reset to the default value of the property (Default) or made undefined (UserUndefined, from 1.8.1). With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value now (oldValue) and the value a real run would write (newValue), both as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives them.
SetPropertyValuesOfElements.name: SetPropertyValuesOfElements

elementPropertyValues.description: A single real value accepts '.' or ',' as the decimal separator, so the value strings GetPropertyValuesOfElements returns can be written back: when both appear the last one is the decimal separator, a separator that appears more than once groups thousands, and a single separator is the decimal one. Unitless real and integer lists accept semicolon-separated numbers; an empty string sets an empty list. Invalid items reject the entire property write.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementPropertyValues, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the property values of the element can be read, the value is editable for the element and converts to the property's type) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value now as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives it (left out when the property is not available or not evaluated for the element), newValue the value that would be written in the same format (left out for valueStatus Default). Archicad can still refuse a value that passes them.

SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails.description: Sets settings of the given Section and Elevation elements: pens, line types, horizontal and vertical range, model effects, story handles and markers. The name and the reference ID are changed with ModifySections.
SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails.name: SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails

SetStories.description: Sets the story sructure of the currently loaded project.
SetStories.name: SetStories

SetStructureDisplay.description: Sets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, e.g. the floor plan, a section or the 3D window. The change cannot be undone. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 27.
SetStructureDisplay.name: SetStructureDisplay

SetSuspendGroupsMode.description: Turns the Suspend Groups mode on or off. Suspend groups to perform operations on elements that are part of a group; remember to restore the previous state afterwards.
SetSuspendGroupsMode.name: SetSuspendGroupsMode

suspendGroups.description: Turn the Suspend Groups mode on or off.

SetURLReferencesOfElements.description: Sets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. Fails with APIERR_MOREUSER for an element that already holds a link.
SetURLReferencesOfElements.name: SetURLReferencesOfElements

elementsWithURLReferences.description: The elements and the web link to set on each.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page. At most 255 bytes in UTF-8. Empty when omitted.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com. At most 511 bytes in UTF-8.

SetUserDataOfAttributes.description: Stores string values under keys in the user data of attributes, for scripts to keep their own state on an attribute. The given pairs are merged into what each attribute already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it.
SetUserDataOfAttributes.name: SetUserDataOfAttributes

pairs.description: The key-value pairs to store on each attribute. A key the attribute already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order.

SetUserDataOfGroups.description: Stores string values under keys in the user data of groups, for scripts to keep their own state on a group. The given pairs are merged into what each group already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. One undo step per call.
SetUserDataOfGroups.name: SetUserDataOfGroups

groups.description: The groups to store the pairs on.

pairs.description: The key-value pairs to store on each group. A key the group already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

executionResults.description: One result per group, in the input order.

SetViewOptions.description: Switches the current plan window to a model view option combination by index, and/or changes the given model view options and on-screen view options. With an index, the model view options stored in the combination apply.
SetViewOptions.name: SetViewOptions

modelViewOptionIndex.description: Switches the window to the model view option combination with this index, as GetViewOptions, FindModelViewOption and GetModelViewOptionDetails return it. Archicad then applies the model view options stored in the combination: viewOptions.modelViewOptions are not applied together with an index, viewOptions.onScreenViewOptions are. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by name with FindModelViewOption right before switching.

SetViewRotation.description: Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database.
SetViewRotation.name: SetViewRotation

SetViewSettings.description: Sets the view settings of navigator items
SetViewSettings.name: SetViewSettings

SetZoneLabelingSettings.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off and selects the Label Favorite it places. Only the given settings are changed. Available from Archicad 28.
SetZoneLabelingSettings.name: SetZoneLabelingSettings

automaticLabeling.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) on or off.

favoriteName.description: The name of the Label Favorite that is placed on each new Zone by the automatic labeling.

SetZoom.description: Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates.
SetZoom.name: SetZoom

zoomBox.description: The area to zoom the current 2D window to, in model coordinates (meters). The window keeps its aspect ratio, so the shown area may be larger than the box. The rotation of the window is kept as it is.

ShowAlert.description: Display a dialog with up to three buttons.
ShowAlert.name: ShowAlert

alertType.description: The type of the alert dialog.

button2.description: Label for the second button (e.g. Cancel).

button3.description: Label for the optional third button.

subMessage.description: Optional smaller sub-message text below the main message.

title.description: The title of the alert dialog.

clickedButton.description: Index of the button the user clicked: 1 = button1, 2 = button2, 3 = button3.

ShowElementsIn3D.description: Opens the 3D window on the given elements, as Show Selection in 3D does: they become the selection and only they are shown. Without elements it shows every element, as Show All in 3D does.
ShowElementsIn3D.name: ShowElementsIn3D

elements.description: The elements to show in 3D. They become the selection, replacing the current one. Missing or empty: every element is shown, as Show All in 3D does.

ShowIFCExportSettings.description: Opens Archicad's IFC export settings dialog, where the user picks a view and an IFC export translator, waits for the user and returns the chosen view and translator, or cancelled. Available from Archicad 28.
ShowIFCExportSettings.name: ShowIFCExportSettings

navigatorItemId.description: Optional: the view (an item of the View Map) the dialog starts with.

translatorName.description: Optional: the name of the IFC export translator the dialog starts with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel; then no other field is given.

translatorName.description: The name of the IFC export translator the user chose, as IFCFileOperation's translatorName takes it.

viewName.description: The name of the chosen view, when Archicad finds it in the navigator.

ShowNotificationBubble.description: Shows a non-blocking notification bubble with a message in the current Archicad window, e.g. to report progress or a result without stopping the user as ShowAlert does. The bubble disappears by itself after the timeout. It is shown at a model coordinate or a pixel position of the current view, by default at the center of the current 2D view. Optionally it gets a large icon, is shown at most a given number of times, or is turned off, until the user runs 'Enable all informational messages'. Returns the bubble's settings read back from Archicad. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
ShowNotificationBubble.name: ShowNotificationBubble

coordinate.description: The model coordinate in the current database (meters) where the bubble is shown, converted like ModelToScreen does: in a 3D window it is projected with the current camera, in other windows z is disregarded. Do not give it together with screenPoint. When neither is given, the bubble is shown at the center of the current view in 2D windows and at the project's local origin otherwise.

disabled.description: True turns the bubble off instead of showing it: it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. False (the default) changes nothing.

icon.description: The icon shown in the bubble. Default: information.

largeIcon.description: The icon shown instead of icon when the "Use large alert cues" option is on in Work Environment. Not set by default.

message.description: The text of the notification bubble.

offset.description: Moves the bubble from its position by this many pixels.

h.description: Horizontal offset in pixels, positive to the right.

v.description: Vertical offset in pixels, positive downwards.

redrawCountLimit.description: Shows the bubble at most this many times. After that it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. Not set by default.

screenPoint.description: The pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates) where the bubble is shown, e.g. a point returned by ModelToScreen. Do not give it together with coordinate.

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds. Default: Archicad's default, 1000 (1 second).

returns.description: The settings of the bubble after the call, read back from Archicad.

largeIcon.description: The icon shown when the "Use large alert cues" option is on in Work Environment.

offset.description: The offset of the bubble from its position, in pixels.

redrawCountLimit.description: How many times the bubble is shown at most. Missing when it has no limit.

text.description: The text of the bubble. Missing when it has none.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds.

ShowScriptUI.description: Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts) and returns the uiId of its window. Each script can have its own window, picked by uiId or scriptId; without them the first window is used.
ShowScriptUI.name: ShowScriptUI

allowSelfSignedCertificates.description: Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.

autoHeight.description: Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.

clearCookies.description: Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.

contextMenuEnabled.description: Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.

height.description: Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

htmlContent.description: The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.

navigationDisabled.description: Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.

resizable.description: Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.

scriptId.description: Any text that identifies the calling script, so it uses its own window: ShowScriptUI gives a script without a window a free one, preferring the closed windows. The Tapir palette gives each script it starts its own id in the TAPIR_SCRIPT_ID environment variable, which aclib passes here automatically; that script's window is titled with its name and is freed when it ends. Without uiId and scriptId the first window is used.

scrollBarsVisible.description: Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.

title.description: Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

uiId.description: The window to use, as returned by ShowScriptUI (1 to 8). Takes precedence over scriptId.

width.description: Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

zoomEnabled.description: Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.

zoomLevel.description: Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.

uiId.description: The window the page is shown in (1 to 8). Pass it to GetScriptUIResult, or to a later ShowScriptUI to replace the page.

SolveStairBaseline.description: Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.
SolveStairBaseline.name: SolveStairBaseline

stairsData.description: Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

solutions.description: The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

SplitElements.description: Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step.
SplitElements.name: SplitElements

elements.description: The elements to split. Supported: straight walls (not polygonal, without doors, windows or openings), straight beams (not slanted or curved, one segment, without holes or openings), lines, slabs, meshes (without level lines or points), fills and polylines (one contour). Other types are reported with their type name.

line.description: The split line in project coordinates: the infinite line through begin and end, as the split line of Archicad's Split command.

results.description: One item per given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The parts, first the original element, then the new ones (copies of it). A wall, beam or line gives two parts: the original keeps the part from its begin point to the split line. A slab, mesh or fill gives one part per piece of its polygon on each side of the line (more than two when the line crosses a concave polygon more than twice); the original keeps the largest. A polyline is cut at every crossing; the original keeps the part with its begin point.

oneOf.description: The split line does not cross the element (or only touches one of its ends), so the element was left as it was.

StoreModulData.description: Creates or overwrites module data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name, with an optional data version. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data. Storing module data is not an undoable step.
StoreModulData.name: StoreModulData

modulData.description: The module data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

content.description: The content of the module data, for example a JSON string.

dataVersion.description: A version number stored with the data, returned by GetModulData, for example to tell the formats of your content apart. The default is 1.

name.description: The name of the module data; the empty name is the default section.

StoreViewSettings.description: Stores the current view settings (action Store) and puts them back later (action Restore), for example before and after a script that changes the view. The two must be called in pairs and cannot be stacked. Restoring may rebuild the view.
StoreViewSettings.name: StoreViewSettings

action.description: Store saves the current view settings, Restore puts the stored ones back. Call them in pairs: a second Store before a Restore is refused.

TeamworkReceive.description: Performs a receive operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
TeamworkReceive.name: TeamworkReceive

TeamworkSend.description: Performs a send operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
TeamworkSend.name: TeamworkSend

TransferMEPSettings.description: Picks up the settings of an MEP element and injects them into other MEP elements of the same type and domain, like Archicad's pick up and inject parameters. Works for routing elements, terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings, flexible segments, branches, take-offs and (from Archicad 30) electrical panels and devices. Each target is changed in its own undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.
TransferMEPSettings.name: TransferMEPSettings

sourceElementId.description: The MEP element to pick up the settings from: a routing element, terminal, accessory, equipment, fitting, flexible segment, branch, take-off, or (from Archicad 30) electrical panel or device.

targetElements.description: The MEP elements to inject the settings into. Each must be of the type and domain of the source element.

TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.description: Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.
TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.name: TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

convex.description: Optional. When true, the faces of the 3D model of each element (its own bodies, any element type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, as Archicad does it, and returned as convexPolygons. Default value is false.

triangulations.description: The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles (or with convex: true its convex polygons), or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

TrimElements.description: Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type. With several roofs or shells in the list Archicad decides which of them trims which element (they may also trim each other), so not every element is necessarily trimmed by each; to trim each element with each roof or shell, call it once per roof or shell with trimmingElement, and check the result with GetElementTrims.
TrimElements.name: TrimElements

elements.description: The construction elements to trim. Without trimmingElement the roofs and shells among them do the trimming: Archicad decides which roof or shell trims which element and with which trim type, and may trim the roofs and shells with each other, so not every element is necessarily trimmed by every roof or shell. The call reports no result per pair; read them back with GetElementTrims. For a known result, use trimmingElement and call the command once per roof or shell.

trimType.description: Used with trimmingElement; defaults to KeepInside.

trimmingElement.description: Optional. The roof or shell that trims every element in the list, with trimType.

UngroupElements.description: Ungroups the given groups one level, like Edit > Grouping > Ungroup: each group is dissolved, the elements and subgroups it directly contains stay. A group nested in another group is reported as failed; ungroup the containing group first. Returns an execution result per group.
UngroupElements.name: UngroupElements

groups.description: The groups to ungroup, as returned by CreateGroups or GetGroupsOfElements. A group nested in another group is reported as failed: ungroup the containing group first.

UnlinkElements.description: Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.
UnlinkElements.name: UnlinkElements

links.description: The links to remove, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

UnlockElements.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!
UnlockElements.name: UnlockElements

UnmergeElements.description: Removes the merge between the two elements of each given pair. Undoable; one execution result per pair.
UnmergeElements.name: UnmergeElements

elementPairs.description: The pairs of merged elements to separate. The order within a pair does not matter.

UpdateAnalyticalModel.description: Triggers an update of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given. Available from Archicad 27.
UpdateAnalyticalModel.name: UpdateAnalyticalModel

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model to update. The model of the current view is updated when it is omitted.

UpdateClassificationItems.description: Updates the id (code), name and/or description of existing Classification Items, keeping their guid and so the elements classified with them. Items cannot be moved to another parent.
UpdateClassificationItems.name: UpdateClassificationItems

classificationItems.description: The classification items to update. Only the fields given change; items keep their guid and their parent.

UpdateClassificationSystems.description: Updates the name, description, source, version and/or date of existing Classification Systems, keeping their guid.
UpdateClassificationSystems.name: UpdateClassificationSystems

classificationSystems.description: The classification systems to update. Only the fields given change.

UpdateDrawings.description: Performs a drawing update on the given elements.
UpdateDrawings.name: UpdateDrawings

UpdateFavoritesFromElements.description: Update existing favorites from the given elements.
UpdateFavoritesFromElements.name: UpdateFavoritesFromElements

UpdateHotlinks.description: Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.
UpdateHotlinks.name: UpdateHotlinks

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to update, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. Each node's cached content is re-read from its source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

UpdateLibraryPartSections.description: Replaces the text of existing sections (scripts, comment, keywords, copyright) of a loaded library part, found by its name. Each section is read back after the update, and the output has one execution result per section.
UpdateLibraryPartSections.name: UpdateLibraryPartSections

name.description: The name of the loaded library part, without the file extension (a trailing '.gsm' is accepted too).

sections.description: The sections to replace. Each section must already exist in the library part; this command does not add new sections.

subIdent.description: The secondary identifier of the section, for a library part with more sections of the same type. Default value is 0.

text.description: The new content of the section.

type.description: The type of the text section.

UpdatePropertyDefinitions.description: Updates existing Custom Property Definitions in place, keeping their guid: name, description, group, default value or expressions, availability, and enum options (add, rename, remove, reorder).
UpdatePropertyDefinitions.name: UpdatePropertyDefinitions

propertyDefinitions.description: The property definitions to update. Only the fields given change; the definition keeps its guid, so element values survive.

UpdatePropertyGroups.description: Updates the name and/or description of existing Custom Property Groups, keeping their guid.
UpdatePropertyGroups.name: UpdatePropertyGroups

propertyGroups.description: The custom property groups to update. Only the fields given change.

UpdateZones.description: Updates Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements): the selected Zones, every Zone when nothing is selected, or the Zones given in zones. Archicad runs the update right after the command has returned, on the Zones selected at that moment, so the new geometry can only be read with a later command.
UpdateZones.name: UpdateZones

keepStampPosition.description: Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.

undoBottomTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.

undoTopTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.

zones.description: Optional list of the Zones to update, on any story. They are selected instead of the current selection and stay selected: Archicad updates the selected Zones right after the command has returned, not during it, and clears the selection when it is done. So do not change the selection until then, and read the new geometry with a later command. Every Zone is checked first; if one cannot be updated (not a Zone, listed twice, hidden or locked layer, not editable), nothing is selected or updated. An empty list updates nothing. Without the list the current selection is updated, or every Zone when nothing is selected.

UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud.description: Uploads local library folders or container files (.lcf) to a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server, as BIMcloud libraries. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29.
UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud.name: UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud

libraryPaths.description: The paths of the local library folders or container files (.lcf) to upload.

parentPath.description: The path of the folder on the server that holds the libraries, as shown in BIMcloud Manager.

serverUrl.description: The URL of the BIMcloud or Teamwork server, e.g. 'https://bimcloud.example.com:22000'.

executionResults.description: One result per library, in the order of the input.

ZoomToElements.description: Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer.
ZoomToElements.name: ZoomToElements

keepSelection.description: Restore the selection the window had before the command (default). With false the given elements stay selected.

data.description: The data the add-on attached to the item, base64 encoded. Empty when there is none.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

itemType.description: Whether the item is a root, a group or a leaf node.

parentViewpointId.description: The identifier of the root or group the item is in. Missing when Archicad reports no parent, as for a root.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item.

AxonometryProjectionType.description: The projection type of an axonometric 3D projection, the projMod of the Archicad API. Archicad works out the transformation matrix of every type but Custom from the type and the azimuth. XY is the top view and Bottom the view from below. YZ and XZ are both the side view (an elevation), looking from the azimuth. Frontal, Monometric, Isometric and Dimetric are the predefined axonometries, and FrontalBottom, MonometricBottom, IsometricBottom and DimetricBottom the same seen from below; an Isometric at azimuth 270 is the isometric from the south-east (X axis at -30 degrees, Y at 30, Z at 90).
